core/autothrow:
-- The computer thrower (DESIGN.md section 4: "the computer throws the same
-- way: it plans a target and an arc and makes a swing with mistakes in it").
-- For a match setup (core/match) it does what a player does: picks a target,
-- stands behind it (tw.plan.stance), takes the default arc (tw.plan.arcFor),
-- solves the plan at a throw level (tw.plan.solve), then makes a synthetic
-- swing (the fields core/swing measures at a release) with seeded mistakes
-- in it, and tw.plan.launch turns that swing into the launch. Self-tests,
-- headless physics matches (tools/physmatch.lua) and the Playdate opponent
-- use it. Pure Lua: no playdate.*.
--
--   local r = autothrow.rng(seed)
--   local a = autothrow.choose(setup, r [, scale [, level]])
--   -- a = { x, y, swivel, loftDeg, speed, tumbleRate, tilt, legal,
--   --       plan  = the solve (tx, ty, back, release, powerLo/Hi, releaseLo/Hi, ...),
--   --       swing = the synthetic swing (back, releaseAngle, flickDps, flickFrac,
--   --               smoothness, shake, pull, how),
--   --       launch = tw.plan.launch's table (verdicts powerV, releaseV, steady),
--   --       drill = for a kubb: { markerX, markerY (from lineY), noseDown, rollLand,
--   --               spin, wobble } (world.launchDrill's arguments) }
--   autothrow.launch(w, s, a)  -- puts the throw into world w (core/world)
import "core/tw"
import "core/flight"
import "core/swing"
import "core/throwplan"
import "core/world"

local flight, swing, plan, world = tw.flight, tw.swing, tw.plan, tw.world
local cos = math.cos

local autothrow = {}

autothrow.tune = {
	level = "club",          -- the throw level it solves at (tw.plan.levels) when none is given
	-- the swing's mistakes times this at each level (autothrow.cpuLevel); pro is
	-- the recorded tournament games (Jamie, 2026-11-17), club and beginner below it
	drillSpin = { beginner = 0, club = 1, pro = 2 }, -- taps of axial spin to steady the flight
	swingScale = { beginner = 1.6, club = 1.3, pro = 1 },
	batonShort = 0,          -- m the baton's target is short of the kubb's center: none, the
	                         -- center, where a player's target snaps (measured 2026-11-15 with
	                         -- the plan's arcs: a clean baton landing up to 0.2 m past the
	                         -- center hits most often at 2 to 8 m; aimed 0.15 short, a 2 m
	                         -- baton at a field kubb hit a quarter of the time)
	minRange = 2.0,          -- m: never stands nearer its target than this, even with the
	                         -- advantage line further up (a slow lofted baton under 2 m
	                         -- hit 2 to 7 in 40; at 2 to 3 m about half)
	halfWidth = 2.4,         -- m: the stance stays inside the throwing line's ends (the stakes)
	-- The basket (Jamie, 2026-11-14; "basket" is the right term): real
	-- throwers put their kubbs in one of the two corners of the far half
	-- nearest the centre line, by a sideline,
	-- so a kubb that runs goes out (a rethrow) rather than somewhere bad. A
	-- turn's kubbs go to the corner that already has more field kubbs in it
	-- (either when it is a tie), so they group. The kubb is drilled to rest there.
	basketX = 1.9,           -- m from the middle: just inside the sideline's middle stake
	basketY = 4.75,          -- m from the baseline (view y): just past the centre line
	basketNear = 1.5,        -- m: field kubbs within this of a basket count for it
	-- The spot (2026-11-16): a kubb drilled onto one already lying in the
	-- basket lands on it and skips a metre away, so each kubb goes beside
	-- the group instead: the clear spot nearest the basket on a small grid.
	spotStepX = 0.12,        -- m between spots across (a kubb's width and a gap)
	spotStepY = 0.16,        -- m between spots along the throw (a kubb's length and a finger)
	spotCols = 3,            -- spots tried this many steps either side of the basket ...
	spotRows = 4,            -- ... and this many short of it and past it
	spotClearX = 0.11,       -- m: a spot is taken when a kubb's centre is within this across ...
	spotClearY = 0.15,       -- ... and this along (an ellipse: kubbs lie along the throw)
	spotLane = 0.10,         -- m: half the width of the lane the kubb comes down in
	spotShortLying = 0.12,   -- m: a lying kubb this far short of the spot in its lane is in the way
	                         -- (at least: a drill lands short of its spot by its run on,
	                         -- drill.slideFor, and a lying kubb that far short is in the way too) ...
	spotShortStanding = 0.6, -- ... a standing one this far
	spotCostY = 0.1,         -- how much a step along counts against a step across: low, so the
	                         -- kubbs go in one line along the throw, where a baton takes two ...
	-- Jamie, 2026-11-16: "trying to build lines is exactly what drillers do. You
	-- either, if you have 2 or 3, you would build a line. If you have more than that,
	-- you build a big cluster."
	clusterFrom = 4,         -- ... with this many kubbs or more to throw in the turn ...
	spotCostYCluster = 1,    -- ... a step along counts as much as one across: the spots pack round
	                         -- the first kubbs in a cluster
	spotMinY = 4.05,         -- m from the baseline: no spot nearer the centre line than this
	spotMaxX = 2.2,          -- m from the middle: no spot nearer the sideline than this
	into = 1,                -- 1: aim a later kubb into the group (intoSpot) before the clear spots; 0: the clear spots only
	intoShort = 0.03,        -- m from a lying kubb's near face to where the drill is aimed to rest
	-- How far off a throw goes, and how much more off a long one goes, is
	-- the shared nerves model (tw.plan.tune "Nerves"), the same for the
	-- player; this file only adds the computer's swing below. The computer
	-- drills its kubbs closer than it throws batons (drillScale).
	-- The lane (2026-11-16): a baton takes two kubbs when one stands behind
	-- the other along its flight, so it aims down the lane with the most
	-- field kubbs in it, at the front one.
	laneHalf = 0.07,         -- m: kubbs within this across of the front one are in its lane ...
	laneDeep = 0.6,          -- ... and within this behind it
	drillScale = 0.2,        -- a drilled kubb's swing mistakes are this much of a baton's
	-- The synthetic swing: the mistakes, each multiplied by choose's scale.
	-- Halved 2026-11-16 when the nerves took over most of the miss (they
	-- were 5, 9 and 0.44 when the swing was the only error).
	backSd = 2.5,            -- degrees sd of the backswing about the power target's center
	releaseSd = 4.5,         -- degrees sd of where the crank stops about the release target's center
	flickDps = { 1050, 1400 }, -- deg/s: a strong flick (swing.tune.fullFlickDps and over: all the power)
	softChance = 0.05,       -- chance the flick is not quite full ...
	softDps = { 850, 1000 }, -- ... and then this fast (flickFrac 0.85 to 1: short)
	shakeMax = 0.22,         -- a steady swing's shake is even between 0 and this (tw.plan.launch
	                         -- pulls the swivel and tilts the baton by it, and it widens the nerves)
	shakyChance = 0.015,     -- chance of a shaky swing ...
	shaky = { 0.25, 0.6 },   -- ... with this much shake (over about 0.44 a baton is a helicopter at club)
}

-- Park-Miller with a scrambled seed (as tools/thrower.lua): tw.plan.rng.
autothrow.rng = plan.rng

-- The launch speed that lands a baton's center at distance d (along the
-- throw) at this loft, through still air with its drag (flight.predict's
-- arc), up to the fastest throw the plan makes (the backswing's cap). Tools,
-- tests and core/bench aim with it.
function autothrow.speedFor(d, loftDeg)
	local hi = plan.speedFor(swing.tune.backswingMaxDeg)
	if d <= 0 then return 0.5 end
	local ft = flight.tune
	local v = flight.speedForCarry(d, math.rad(loftDeg), ft.handHeight, ft.dragK.baton)
	if v > hi then return hi end
	if v < 0.5 then return 0.5 end
	return v
end

-- Which basket a toss goes to: -1 (left, view frame) or 1 (right), the one
-- with more field kubbs of the far half within basketNear of it.
function autothrow.basket(s, r)
	local t = autothrow.tune
	local left, right = 0, 0
	local ky = s.lineY + t.basketY
	local near2 = t.basketNear * t.basketNear
	for _, p in ipairs(s.pieces) do
		if p.role == "field" and p.half ~= s.side then
			local dy = p.y - ky
			local dl, dr = p.x + t.basketX, p.x - t.basketX
			if dl * dl + dy * dy < near2 then left = left + 1 end
			if dr * dr + dy * dy < near2 then right = right + 1 end
		end
	end
	if left > right then return -1 elseif right > left then return 1 end
	return (r.next() < 0.5) and -1 or 1
end

-- Where a toss to basket `side` should rest (view frame): the basket when
-- nothing is near it, else the clear spot nearest it (tune.spot*): not on a
-- kubb and with none in the lane it comes down and runs on in (a drill lands
-- short of its spot by its run on, so a kubb already down just past the spot
-- is its backstop). Nearest counts a step along the throw as little against
-- one across (a line along the throw) when the turn has fewer than
-- clusterFrom kubbs to throw, else the same (a cluster). The basket itself
-- when every spot is taken. Since 2026-11-16 a later kubb is first aimed
-- into the group (intoSpot below).

-- Is (x, y) a spot a drill can be aimed at: on the allowed part of the
-- half, not on a field kubb and with none in the lane it comes down and runs
-- on in (a lying one within shortLying short of it, a standing one within
-- spotShortStanding)? Piece `except` (or nil) is left out.
local function spotClear(s, t, x, y, shortLying, except)
	local ax = x < 0 and -x or x
	if ax > t.spotMaxX or y < s.lineY + t.spotMinY then return false end
	for _, p in ipairs(s.pieces) do
		if p ~= except and p.role == "field" and p.half ~= s.side then
			local dx, dy = (p.x - x) / t.spotClearX, (p.y - y) / t.spotClearY
			if dx * dx + dy * dy < 1 then return false end
			local lx, short = p.x - x, y - p.y
			if lx < 0 then lx = -lx end
			if lx < t.spotLane and short > 0
				and short < (p.toppled and shortLying or t.spotShortStanding) then
				return false
			end
		end
	end
	return true
end

-- Into the group (2026-11-16, Jamie: "good drillers roll into other kubbs
-- because it is impossible to stop that much energy with just the ground and
-- grass"). Once a kubb of the far half lies near the basket, a drill is aimed
-- so that it would rest intoShort in front of a lying kubb's near face, in
-- that kubb's lane: the half of the run-ons that would carry it on are
-- stopped by the kubb, so the two end together. A line (fewer than
-- clusterFrom kubbs this turn): the front kubb of the group nearest the
-- basket, so the line grows toward the thrower. A cluster: in front of
-- whichever lying kubb leaves the aim nearest the group's middle, so the
-- kubbs pile round it. nil when no lying kubb is near the basket, or no aim
-- in front of one is clear.
local function intoSpot(s, t, bx, by, shortLying)
	local near2 = t.basketNear * t.basketNear
	local cluster = (s.of or 0) >= t.clusterFrom
	local n, cx, cy = 0, 0, 0
	for _, p in ipairs(s.pieces) do
		if p.role == "field" and p.half ~= s.side and p.toppled then
			local dx, dy = p.x - bx, p.y - by
			if dx * dx + dy * dy < near2 then n, cx, cy = n + 1, cx + p.x, cy + p.y end
		end
	end
	if n == 0 then return nil end
	cx, cy = cx / n, cy / n
	local best, bestX, bestY
	for _, p in ipairs(s.pieces) do
		if p.role == "field" and p.half ~= s.side and p.toppled then
			local dx, dy = p.x - bx, p.y - by
			if dx * dx + dy * dy < near2 then
				-- the kubb's half extent along the throw (it lies along its angle)
				local a = p.pose and p.pose.angle or 0
				local ca, sa = cos(a), math.sin(a)
				if ca < 0 then ca = -ca end
				if sa < 0 then sa = -sa end
				local ext = 0.075 * sa + 0.035 * ca
				local x, y = p.x, p.y - ext - t.intoShort
				-- clear of every other kubb (this one is the backstop: the aim
				-- sits in its own clear ellipse on purpose)
				local ok = spotClear(s, t, x, y, shortLying, p)
				if ok then
					local cost
					if cluster then
						local ex, ey = x - cx, y - cy
						cost = ex * ex + ey * ey
					else
						-- the front of the group: least y, then nearest the basket across
						local ex = x - bx
						cost = y * 100 + ex * ex
					end
					if not best or cost < best - 1e-9 then best, bestX, bestY = cost, x, y end
				end
			end
		end
	end
	if not best then return nil end
	return bestX, bestY
end

function autothrow.spot(s, side)
	local t = autothrow.tune
	local bx, by = side * t.basketX, s.lineY + t.basketY
	local best, bestX, bestY
	local costY = ((s.of or 0) >= t.clusterFrom) and t.spotCostYCluster or t.spotCostY
	local shortLying = tw.drill.slideFor(plan.loftFor(plan.arcFor("drill")), s.surface)
	if shortLying < t.spotShortLying then shortLying = t.spotShortLying end
	if t.into ~= 0 then
		local ix, iy = intoSpot(s, t, bx, by, shortLying)
		if ix then return ix, iy end
	end
	for i = -t.spotCols, t.spotCols do
		for j = -t.spotRows, t.spotRows do
			local x, y = bx + i * t.spotStepX, by + j * t.spotStepY
			if spotClear(s, t, x, y, shortLying) then
				local cx, cy = i, j * costY
				local cost = cx * cx + cy * cy
				if not best or cost < best - 1e-9 then best, bestX, bestY = cost, x, y end
			end
		end
	end
	if not best then return bx, by end
	return bestX, bestY
end

-- The swing a thrower makes at solution sol, with seeded mistakes scaled by
-- scale (0: the clean swing, every field on its target). Always draws the
-- same number of values from r. Fills and returns out: core/swing's result
-- fields (back, releaseAngle, flickDps, flickFrac, smoothness, shake, pull,
-- how = "stopped").
function autothrow.swing(sol, r, scale, out)
	local t, st = autothrow.tune, swing.tune
	out = out or {}
	local back = sol.back + r.normal(t.backSd) * scale
	if back > st.backswingMaxDeg then back = st.backswingMaxDeg end
	out.back = back
	local rel = sol.release + r.normal(t.releaseSd) * scale
	if rel < 1 then rel = 1 elseif rel > st.skyDeg - 1 then rel = st.skyDeg - 1 end
	out.releaseAngle = rel
	-- the flick: strong, now and then not quite
	local soft = r.next() < t.softChance * scale
	local u = r.next()
	local dps
	if soft then dps = t.softDps[1] + (t.softDps[2] - t.softDps[1]) * u
	else dps = t.flickDps[1] + (t.flickDps[2] - t.flickDps[1]) * u end
	if scale <= 0 then dps = st.fullFlickDps end
	local f = (dps - st.swingStartDps) / (st.fullFlickDps - st.swingStartDps)
	if f < 0 then f = 0 elseif f > 1 then f = 1 end
	out.flickDps = dps
	out.flickFrac = st.minFlickFrac + (1 - st.minFlickFrac) * f
	-- the steadiness: mostly steady, now and then shaky
	local shaky = r.next() < t.shakyChance * scale
	local u2 = r.next()
	local shake = t.shakeMax * r.next() * scale
	if shaky then shake = t.shaky[1] + (t.shaky[2] - t.shaky[1]) * u2 end
	if shake > 1 then shake = 1 end
	out.shake, out.smoothness = shake, 1 - shake
	out.pull = (r.next() < 0.5) and -1 or 1
	out.how = "stopped"
	return out
end

-- The computer's level tables (2026-11-17). A level's gauge forgiveness
-- (powerHalf, releaseHalf, inGain, shakeGain, overGain) is there to help a
-- player's crank; the computer's swing has the same mistakes at every
-- level, so forgiving it more made club throw better than pro. So the
-- computer always throws on pro's gauge, with the named level's nerves and
-- tumble, and its swing's mistakes times tune.swingScale for the level.
-- Pro is the recorded tournament games (Jamie, 2026-11-17). Made once.
local cpuLevels = {}
for name, lv in pairs(plan.levels) do
	local pro = plan.levels.pro
	cpuLevels[name] = { powerHalf = pro.powerHalf, releaseHalf = pro.releaseHalf, inGain = pro.inGain,
		shakeGain = pro.shakeGain, overGain = pro.overGain, nervesDeg = lv.nervesDeg,
		nervesLen = lv.nervesLen, tumbleTurns = lv.tumbleTurns, tumbleSd = lv.tumbleSd }
end
-- The computer's level table for a level name (tune.level when unknown).
function autothrow.cpuLevel(name)
	return cpuLevels[name] or cpuLevels[autothrow.tune.level] or cpuLevels.club
end

-- A throw for match setup `s` (view frame). Batons: target the nearest
-- live target and stand behind it as far forward as allowed (never nearer
-- than minRange), its centre aimed through the target at plan.aimZFor's
-- height; the king from the baseline. Kubbs: drilled to the basket
-- (autothrow.basket) from the baseline. scale (default 1) multiplies every
-- mistake: below 1 a steadier thrower. level: a tw.plan level (default
-- tune.level).
function autothrow.choose(s, r, scale, level)
	scale = scale or 1
	local t = autothrow.tune
	local lname = level or (s.thrower and s.thrower.level) or t.level
	if type(lname) ~= "string" then lname = t.level end
	scale = scale * (t.swingScale[lname] or 1)
	local q = { level = autothrow.cpuLevel(lname), surface = s.surface }
	local tx, ty, py, arc
	if s.kind == "toss" then
		local side = autothrow.basket(s, r)
		tx, ty = autothrow.spot(s, side)
		q.spin = t.drillSpin[lname] or t.drillSpin[t.level]
		q.projectile, arc = "kubb", plan.arcFor("drill")
		py = s.lineY
	else
		local pos = {}
		for _, p in ipairs(s.pieces) do pos[p.id] = p end
		local target = pos[s.targets[1]]
		-- the nearest target to the line
		for _, id in ipairs(s.targets) do
			local p = pos[id]
			if p and p.y < target.y then target = p end
		end
		tx = target.x
		if target.role == "field" then
			-- the lane with the most standing field kubbs; the nearest front on a tie
			local bestN = 0
			for _, id in ipairs(s.targets) do
				local f = pos[id]
				if f and f.role == "field" then
					local n, lo, hi = 0, f.x, f.x
					for _, id2 in ipairs(s.targets) do
						local p = pos[id2]
						if p and p.role == "field" then
							local dx, dy = p.x - f.x, p.y - f.y
							if dx < t.laneHalf and dx > -t.laneHalf and dy >= 0 and dy <= t.laneDeep then
								n = n + 1
								if p.x < lo then lo = p.x elseif p.x > hi then hi = p.x end
							end
						end
					end
					if n > bestN or (n == bestN and f.y < target.y) then
						bestN, target, tx = n, f, (lo + hi) / 2
					end
				end
			end
		end
		ty = target.y - t.batonShort
		q.projectile = "baton"
		-- through the piece at its aim height (plan.tune.aimHeightShare), as a
		-- player's circle on a piece is
		q.aimZ = plan.aimZFor((s.kingShot or target.role == "king") and "king" or "kubb")
		if s.kingShot or target.role == "king" then arc = plan.arcFor("king")
		elseif target.role == "field" then arc = plan.arcFor("field")
		else arc = plan.arcFor("base") end
		py = s.kingShot and s.lineY or (s.forwardY or s.lineY)
		if py > target.y - t.minRange then py = target.y - t.minRange end
		if py < s.lineY then py = s.lineY end
	end
	local st = plan.stance(tx, ty, s.lineY, py, t.halfWidth, {})
	q.px, q.py, q.tx, q.ty, q.release = st.x, st.y, tx, ty, arc
	local sol = plan.solve(q, {})
	if q.projectile == "kubb" then scale = scale * t.drillScale end
	local sw = autothrow.swing(sol, r, scale, {})
	-- the nerves are the player's (tw.plan.launch), drawn from this stream;
	-- scale 0 is the clean throw, no nerves either
	local L = plan.launch(sol, sw, { projectile = q.projectile, tilt = 0, spin = q.spin,
		nerves = scale > 0 and r or nil }, {})
	local a = { x = st.x, y = st.y, swivel = L.swivel, loftDeg = L.loft, speed = L.speed,
		tumbleRate = L.tumble, tilt = L.tilt, legal = L.legal, plan = sol, swing = sw, launch = L }
	if q.projectile == "kubb" then
		a.drill = { markerX = tx, markerY = ty - s.lineY, noseDown = L.noseDown, rollLand = L.rollLand,
			spin = L.spin, wobble = L.wobble }
	end
	return a
end

-- Put throw a (autothrow.choose) for setup s into world w: a drilled kubb
-- (world.launchDrill, kubb s.kubb) or a baton (world.launchBaton, the turn's
-- baton id s.batonId). Returns the body.
function autothrow.launch(w, s, a)
	local d = a.drill
	if d then
		return world.launchDrill(w, s.kubb, a.x, a.y, a.swivel, a.loftDeg, a.speed, d.noseDown, d.rollLand,
			d.spin, d.wobble)
	end
	return world.launchBaton(w, a.x, a.y, a.swivel, a.loftDeg, a.speed, a.tumbleRate, a.tilt, s.batonId)
end

tw.autothrow = autothrow
core/bench:
-- The physics benchmark (DESIGN 5): one fixed scenario, a baton thrown into a
-- tight group of five kubbs, stepped for 3 simulated seconds whether or not
-- everything has come to rest. `make bench` runs it on the desktop
-- (tools/bench.lua) and the System Menu "Bench" item runs the very same
-- function on the device; only the clock differs.
import "core/tw"
import "core/world"
import "core/quat"
import "core/autothrow"
import "core/drill"
import "core/match"

local world, quat = tw.world, tw.quat

local bench = {}

bench.seconds = 3
-- five field kubbs standing close together around (0, 4.3), turned a little
bench.pieces = {
	{ id = "b1", kind = "kubb", x = 0.00, y = 4.20, yaw = 0.0 },
	{ id = "b2", kind = "kubb", x = 0.10, y = 4.30, yaw = 0.3 },
	{ id = "b3", kind = "kubb", x = -0.10, y = 4.32, yaw = -0.2 },
	{ id = "b4", kind = "kubb", x = 0.03, y = 4.42, yaw = 0.6 },
	{ id = "b5", kind = "kubb", x = -0.06, y = 4.52, yaw = 0.1 },
}
-- from the baseline center, straight up the pitch, 35 degrees of loft,
-- end over end at 7 rad/s; 6.11 m/s carries it through the air's drag as
-- far as 6.0 did with none (before 2026-11-16), into the same group
bench.throw = { x = 0, lineY = 0, swivel = 0, loft = 35, speed = 6.11, tumble = 7, tilt = 0 }

-- A match's worst case for the bodies a throw starts with (docs/notes/match.md
-- "Match"): six batons and ten kubbs lying on the pitch from earlier throws
-- of the turn, already down and asleep, away from the scenario's throw
-- except two batons and a kubb just behind the group (the throw may reach
-- them). bench.run(..., true) adds them.
local function lying(id, kind, x, y, yaw)
	local tw_, tx, ty, tz = quat.fromAxisAngle(1, 0, 0, -math.pi / 2)   -- long axis along +y, a face down
	local zw, zx, zy, zz = quat.fromAxisAngle(0, 0, 1, yaw - math.pi / 2)
	local qw, qx, qy, qz = quat.mul(zw, zx, zy, zz, tw_, tx, ty, tz)
	return { id = id, kind = kind, x = x, y = y, qw = qw, qx = qx, qy = qy, qz = qz, toppled = true }
end
bench.debris = {
	lying("baton1", "baton", -0.15, 4.75, 0.4),
	lying("baton2", "baton", 0.20, 4.85, 1.9),
	lying("baton3", "baton", 1.40, 5.60, 0.2),
	lying("baton4", "baton", -1.30, 6.10, 2.8),
	lying("baton5", "baton", 0.80, 7.30, 1.2),
	lying("baton6", "baton", -0.60, 7.70, 0.7),
	lying("d1", "kubb", 0.05, 4.95, 0.1),
	lying("d2", "kubb", -1.80, 5.20, 1.5),
	lying("d3", "kubb", 1.90, 5.40, 0.3),
	lying("d4", "kubb", -1.00, 6.60, 2.2),
	lying("d5", "kubb", 1.10, 6.80, 0.9),
	lying("d6", "kubb", -2.00, 7.95, 0.0),
	lying("d7", "kubb", -1.00, 8.10, 1.6),
	lying("d8", "kubb", 0.00, 7.85, 0.2),
	lying("d9", "kubb", 1.00, 8.05, 1.4),
	lying("d10", "kubb", 2.00, 7.90, 3.0),
}

-- The match case (the device autobench's "match" lines): a turn in progress
-- as the owner plays it, in the view frame. Base kubbs and the king, two
-- standing field kubbs, and the turn's debris (three lying batons, three
-- downed kubbs). bench.matchSetup(projectile) gives a core/match-style setup
-- for scenes/throw (throw.prepare); bench.matchThrows are the throws played
-- in it, each from that same setup: a baton that hits a field kubb, a baton
-- that misses and rolls on through the debris, and a drilled kubb. They are
-- fixed launches (no scatter): the same throws on every run.
local function standing(id, kind, x, y, yaw)
	local qw, qx, qy, qz = quat.fromAxisAngle(0, 0, 1, yaw or 0)
	return { id = id, kind = kind, x = x, y = y, qw = qw, qx = qx, qy = qy, qz = qz, toppled = false }
end
function bench.matchSetup(projectile)
	local pieces = {}
	for i, x in ipairs { -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 } do pieces[i] = standing("b" .. i, "kubb", x, 8, 0) end
	pieces[#pieces + 1] = standing("f1", "kubb", 0.8, 5.0, 0.2)
	pieces[#pieces + 1] = standing("f2", "kubb", -0.9, 5.6, -0.3)
	pieces[#pieces + 1] = standing("king", "king", 0, 4, 0)
	local debris = {
		lying("baton1", "baton", 0.35, 5.95, 0.4),
		lying("baton2", "baton", -1.6, 6.9, 1.9),
		lying("baton3", "baton", 1.5, 7.0, 0.2),
		lying("d1", "kubb", 1.1, 5.35, 0.3),
		lying("d2", "kubb", -0.2, 7.3, 1.2),
		lying("d3", "kubb", 1.8, 6.2, 2.2),
	}
	for _, p in ipairs(debris) do
		-- resting on the ground: the half side of the lying box or the baton's radius
		p.z = (p.kind == "baton") and 0.022 or 0.035
	end
	local kubb = projectile == "kubb"
	return {
		kind = kubb and "toss" or "baton", side = "A", projectile = projectile or "baton",
		kubb = kubb and "f3" or nil, batonId = (not kubb) and "baton4" or nil,
		pieces = pieces, debris = debris, lineY = 0, forwardY = 0,
		targets = { "f1", "f2" }, label = "bench",
	}
end
-- core/autothrow-style throws ({x, y, swivel, loftDeg, speed, tumbleRate,
-- tilt, legal}; a drill has drill = {markerX, markerY}: thrown at the band's
-- center, clean). `aim` = {tx, ty}: where the launch is aimed (the speed that
-- lands the center there at this loft); filled in by bench.matchThrow.
bench.matchThrows = {
	{ name = "hit", projectile = "baton", x = 0.8, aim = { 0.8, 4.85 }, loftDeg = 30, tumbleRate = 5.5 },
	{ name = "miss", projectile = "baton", x = -1.0, aim = { -1.25, 6.2 }, loftDeg = 30, tumbleRate = 5.5 },
	-- (the marker moved from (0.3, 6.4) on 2026-11-16: a drill aimed short of it for its
	-- run on lands on baton1 there)
	{ name = "drill", projectile = "kubb", drill = { markerX = -0.5, markerY = 6.4 } },
}
function bench.matchThrow(t)
	local a = { x = t.x or 0, y = 0, swivel = 0, loftDeg = t.loftDeg or 30, speed = 0,
		tumbleRate = t.tumbleRate or 0, tilt = 0, legal = true, drill = t.drill }
	if t.aim then
		local dx, dy = t.aim[1] - a.x, t.aim[2] - a.y
		a.swivel = math.atan(dx, dy)
		a.speed = tw.autothrow.speedFor(math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy), a.loftDeg)
	end
	return a
end

function bench.world(withDebris)
	local pieces = bench.pieces
	if withDebris then
		pieces = {}
		for i, p in ipairs(bench.pieces) do pieces[i] = p end
		for _, p in ipairs(bench.debris) do pieces[#pieces + 1] = p end
	end
	local w = world.new{ surface = "grass", pieces = pieces }
	local t = bench.throw
	world.launchBaton(w, t.x, t.lineY, t.swivel, t.loft, t.speed, t.tumble, t.tilt)
	return w
end

-- Bodies that were ever awake (the projectile included).
local function woke(w)
	local n = 0
	for i = 1, w.n do if w.bodies[i].everAwake then n = n + 1 end end
	return n
end

-- Run the scenario. clock() returns seconds. If `chunk` is given, `yield`
-- is called every `chunk` steps (the device redraws a progress line there;
-- the time spent in yield is not counted). withDebris adds bench.debris.
-- Returns a result table.
function bench.run(clock, chunk, yield, withDebris)
	local w = bench.world(withDebris)
	local steps = math.floor(bench.seconds / world.tune.dt + 0.5)
	local busy, maxAwake, maxContacts = 0, 0, 0
	-- the collision phase: steps with two or more bodies awake (timed one by one)
	local hotSteps, hotTime = 0, 0
	local done = 0
	while done < steps do
		local n = chunk and math.min(chunk, steps - done) or (steps - done)
		local t0 = clock()
		local ts = t0
		for _ = 1, n do
			world.step(w)
			local te = clock()
			if w.awakeCount >= 2 then hotSteps, hotTime = hotSteps + 1, hotTime + (te - ts) end
			ts = te
			if w.awakeCount > maxAwake then maxAwake = w.awakeCount end
			if w.contacts > maxContacts then maxContacts = w.contacts end
		end
		busy = busy + (ts - t0)
		done = done + n
		if yield then yield(done, steps) end
	end
	local r = world.result(w)
	return {
		steps = steps,
		simSeconds = steps * world.tune.dt,
		seconds = busy,
		msPerStep = busy * 1000 / steps,
		stepsPerSecond = steps / busy,
		msPerSimSecond = busy * 1000 / (steps * world.tune.dt),
		hotSteps = hotSteps,
		hotMsPerStep = hotSteps > 0 and hotTime * 1000 / hotSteps or 0,
		maxAwake = maxAwake,
		maxContacts = maxContacts,
		toppled = #r.toppled,
		touched = #r.touched,
		bodies = w.n,
		woke = woke(w),
	}
end

-- The scenario again with world.prof on: ms per step of each phase of
-- world.step, separately for the collision phase (2+ bodies awake) and the
-- rest. Returns lines of text. yield(done, steps) as in bench.run.
function bench.profile(clock, chunk, yield)
	local w = bench.world()
	local steps = math.floor(bench.seconds / world.tune.dt + 0.5)
	local P = world.newProf(clock)
	local hot, cold = world.newProf(clock), world.newProf(clock)
	local nh, nc = 0, 0
	local phases = world.PHASES
	world.prof = P
	for s = 1, steps do
		for _, k in ipairs(phases) do P[k] = 0 end
		P.narrow = 0
		world.step(w)
		local acc = (w.awakeCount >= 2) and hot or cold
		if acc == hot then nh = nh + 1 else nc = nc + 1 end
		for _, k in ipairs(phases) do acc[k] = acc[k] + P[k] end
		acc.narrow = acc.narrow + P.narrow
		acc.contacts = (acc.contacts or 0) + w.contacts
		if yield and s % (chunk or 24) == 0 then
			world.prof = nil
			yield(s, steps)
			world.prof = P
		end
	end
	world.prof = nil
	local lines = {}
	for _, row in ipairs { { "collision", hot, nh }, { "other", cold, nc } } do
		local acc, n = row[2], row[3]
		if n > 0 then
			local sum = 0
			local parts = {}
			for _, k in ipairs(phases) do
				sum = sum + acc[k]
				parts[#parts + 1] = string.format("%s %.3f", k, acc[k] * 1000 / n)
			end
			lines[#lines + 1] = string.format("  %s steps %d: %.3f ms/step (narrowphase pairs %.1f, contacts %.1f per step)",
				row[1], n, sum * 1000 / n, acc.narrow / n, (acc.contacts or 0) / n)
			lines[#lines + 1] = "    " .. table.concat(parts, ", ")
		end
	end
	return lines
end

-- The match case's throws (bench.matchThrows) stepped to rest with nothing
-- drawn: ms per step for each kind of step (lone: taken by world.loneFlight;
-- air: one body awake and no contact; ground: one body awake touching
-- something; multi: two or more awake). Returns one line of text. The device
-- runs it with world.loneFlight off and on.
function bench.matchPhysics(clock, yield)
	local acc = { lone = { 0, 0 }, air = { 0, 0 }, ground = { 0, 0 }, multi = { 0, 0 } }
	local steps, busy = 0, 0
	for _, t in ipairs(bench.matchThrows) do
		local s = bench.matchSetup(t.projectile)
		local w = world.new { surface = "grass", pieces = tw.match.worldPieces(s) }
		local a = bench.matchThrow(t)
		if a.drill then
			local drill = tw.drill
			local sol = drill.solve(a.drill.markerX, a.drill.markerY, 0, {})
			local L = drill.launch(sol, { power = sol.band, smoothness = 1, tilt = 0 }, 0, {})
			world.launchDrill(w, s.kubb, sol.x, 0, L.swivel, L.loft, L.speed, L.noseDown, L.rollLand, L.spin,
				L.wobble)
		else
			world.launchBaton(w, a.x, a.y, a.swivel, a.loftDeg, a.speed, a.tumbleRate, a.tilt, s.batonId)
		end
		while not world.isAtRest(w) do
			local t0 = clock()
			world.step(w)
			local dt = clock() - t0
			local c
			if w.loneStep == w.steps then c = "lone"
			elseif w.awakeCount >= 2 then c = "multi"
			elseif w.contacts > 0 then c = "ground"
			else c = "air" end
			local A = acc[c]
			A[1], A[2] = A[1] + 1, A[2] + dt
			steps, busy = steps + 1, busy + dt
			if yield and steps % 24 == 0 then yield() end
		end
	end
	local parts = {}
	for _, c in ipairs { "lone", "air", "ground", "multi" } do
		local A = acc[c]
		parts[#parts + 1] = string.format("%s %d at %.3f", c, A[1], A[1] > 0 and A[2] * 1000 / A[1] or 0)
	end
	return string.format("match physics (lone flight %s): %d steps, %.3f ms/step; %s",
		world.loneFlight and "on" or "off", steps, busy * 1000 / steps, table.concat(parts, ", "))
end

-- One line of text for the result (the device appends it to bench.txt).
function bench.line(r, where)
	return string.format("%s: %d steps (%.1f s simulated) in %.3f s; %.3f ms/step; %.0f steps/s; %.1f ms per simulated s; %.1f steps per 20 ms frame; collision phase %d steps at %.3f ms/step (%.1f per 20 ms frame); awake max %d, contacts max %d; toppled %d",
		where or "bench", r.steps, r.simSeconds, r.seconds, r.msPerStep, r.stepsPerSecond, r.msPerSimSecond,
		20 / r.msPerStep, r.hotSteps, r.hotMsPerStep, r.hotMsPerStep > 0 and 20 / r.hotMsPerStep or 0,
		r.maxAwake, r.maxContacts, r.toppled) .. string.format("; bodies %d, woke %d", r.bodies, r.woke)
end

tw.bench = bench
core/body:
-- Rigid bodies: the baton (a capsule) and kubbs and the king (boxes).
-- Pure Lua: no playdate.*.
--
-- A body is one flat table of numbers so the physics step makes no garbage:
--   x, y, z          center of mass (world meters)
--   vx, vy, vz       linear velocity
--   qw, qx, qy, qz   orientation (body local -> world)
--   wx, wy, wz       angular velocity, world frame (rad/s)
--   r11 .. r33       rotation matrix of q, row-major; column 3 is the local z
--                    axis, which is the long axis of every piece
--   i11 .. i33       inverse inertia tensor in the world frame (symmetric)
-- Local frame: z is the long axis (a standing kubb has local z up; the
-- baton's segment runs along local z).
import "core/tw"
import "core/quat"

local quat = tw.quat
local sqrt = math.sqrt

local body = {}

body.BOX, body.CAPSULE = 1, 2

-- Piece sizes and masses (DESIGN 2). Not tunables: the rules fix them.
body.kinds = {
	kubb = { shape = 1, hx = 0.035, hy = 0.035, hz = 0.075, mass = 0.40 },
	king = { shape = 1, hx = 0.045, hy = 0.045, hz = 0.15, mass = 1.2 },
	-- 30 cm long overall, 4.4 cm diameter: a segment of half length
	-- 0.15 - 0.022 plus a 0.022 m radius
	baton = { shape = 2, hl = 0.128, r = 0.022, length = 0.30, mass = 0.25 },
	-- a pitch stake: a fixed vertical post (static: it never moves). Radius
	-- from core/pitch; world.addStakes sets its height from world.tune.
	stake = { shape = 2, hl = 0.135, r = 0.015, length = 0.30, mass = 1, static = true },
}

-- Principal moments of inertia (kg m^2) about the local axes.
-- Box (full sides a, b, c): Ix = m (b^2 + c^2) / 12, and so on.
-- Baton: a real baton is a solid wooden cylinder (the capsule is only its
-- collision shape), so it gets the solid cylinder's inertia:
-- axial m r^2 / 2, transverse m (3 r^2 + L^2) / 12.
function body.inertia(k)
	local m = k.mass
	if k.shape == 1 then
		local a, b, c = 2 * k.hx, 2 * k.hy, 2 * k.hz
		return m * (b * b + c * c) / 12, m * (a * a + c * c) / 12, m * (a * a + b * b) / 12
	end
	local r, L = k.r, k.length
	local t = m * (3 * r * r + L * L) / 12
	return t, t, 0.5 * m * r * r
end

function body.new(kind, id)
	local k = body.kinds[kind]
	assert(k, "unknown body kind " .. tostring(kind))
	local Ix, Iy, Iz = body.inertia(k)
	local b = {
		kind = kind, id = id or kind, shape = k.shape,
		hx = k.hx or 0, hy = k.hy or 0, hz = k.hz or 0,
		hl = k.hl or 0, r = k.r or 0,
		m = k.mass, im = 1 / k.mass,
		Ix = Ix, Iy = Iy, Iz = Iz, iIx = 1 / Ix, iIy = 1 / Iy, iIz = 1 / Iz,
		x = 0, y = 0, z = 0, vx = 0, vy = 0, vz = 0,
		qw = 1, qx = 0, qy = 0, qz = 0, wx = 0, wy = 0, wz = 0,
		r11 = 1, r12 = 0, r13 = 0, r21 = 0, r22 = 1, r23 = 0, r31 = 0, r32 = 0, r33 = 1,
		i11 = 0, i12 = 0, i13 = 0, i22 = 0, i23 = 0, i33 = 0,
		awake = false, sleepTime = 0, everAwake = false,
		wokeStep = -1,       -- the step a touch woke it in (world.step wakes the group it rests against)
		bounceStep = -1,     -- the last step it bounced off another piece (world.step's restitution)
		rowStep = -1,        -- the last step it was in a bounce group that spread past the pieces that bounce
		cStep = -1,          -- the last step it had a contact (world.step: a body with none moves by
		                     -- the trapezoid)
		-- what holds it up and what it waits for before it sleeps (world.step, phase 8):
		restStep = -1,       -- the last step it pressed on a sleeping or static piece
		propStep = -1,       -- the last step it pressed on an awake piece, propBy
		propBy = false,
		mateStep = -1,       -- the last step it pressed on an awake piece, and mateMin the
		mateMin = 0,         -- least sleep timer among those pieces (the step before)
		-- bounding sphere radius about the center
		radius = (k.shape == 1) and sqrt(k.hx ^ 2 + k.hy ^ 2 + k.hz ^ 2) or (k.hl + k.r),
		-- the outcome of the throw
		toppled = false, touched = false, leftPitch = false,
		-- ground contact slots (one per box corner or capsule end) for warm
		-- starting: accumulated impulses from the last step that had them
		gStamp = {}, gN = {}, gT1 = {}, gT2 = {}, gDig = {}, gBite = {}, gMf = {}, gEf = {},
		groundImpulse = 0,   -- sum of ground normal impulses in this step
		dig = 0,             -- extra rolling-resistance lever from digging in (m), decays
		plough = 0,          -- m slid on the ground since it last left it (snow piles up)
		impact = -1,         -- the last step a ground contact arrived faster than restitutionSpeed
		index = 0,
	}
	if k.static then
		-- infinite mass: no impulse moves it
		b.static = true
		b.im, b.iIx, b.iIy, b.iIz = 0, 0, 0, 0
	end
	for i = 1, 8 do
		b.gStamp[i], b.gN[i], b.gT1[i], b.gT2[i], b.gDig[i], b.gBite[i] = -1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
		b.gMf[i], b.gEf[i] = 1, 1   -- the ground texture's friction and bounce factors
	end
	body.updateDerived(b)
	return b
end

-- Rotation matrix and world inverse inertia from the quaternion.
function body.updateDerived(b)
	local r11, r12, r13, r21, r22, r23, r31, r32, r33 = quat.toMatrix(b.qw, b.qx, b.qy, b.qz)
	b.r11, b.r12, b.r13, b.r21, b.r22, b.r23, b.r31, b.r32, b.r33 = r11, r12, r13, r21, r22, r23, r31, r32, r33
	-- I^-1 world = R diag(iI) R^T
	local a, c, e = b.iIx, b.iIy, b.iIz
	b.i11 = r11 * r11 * a + r12 * r12 * c + r13 * r13 * e
	b.i12 = r11 * r21 * a + r12 * r22 * c + r13 * r23 * e
	b.i13 = r11 * r31 * a + r12 * r32 * c + r13 * r33 * e
	b.i22 = r21 * r21 * a + r22 * r22 * c + r23 * r23 * e
	b.i23 = r21 * r31 * a + r22 * r32 * c + r23 * r33 * e
	b.i33 = r31 * r31 * a + r32 * r32 * c + r33 * r33 * e
end

function body.setPose(b, x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz)
	b.x, b.y, b.z = x, y, z
	b.qw, b.qx, b.qy, b.qz = quat.normalize(qw or 1, qx or 0, qy or 0, qz or 0)
	body.updateDerived(b)
end

function body.setVelocity(b, vx, vy, vz, wx, wy, wz)
	b.vx, b.vy, b.vz = vx or 0, vy or 0, vz or 0
	b.wx, b.wy, b.wz = wx or 0, wy or 0, wz or 0
end

-- World inverse inertia times a vector.
function body.invInertiaMul(b, x, y, z)
	return b.i11 * x + b.i12 * y + b.i13 * z,
		b.i12 * x + b.i22 * y + b.i23 * z,
		b.i13 * x + b.i23 * y + b.i33 * z
end

-- Angular momentum about the center, world frame: I_world w = R I R^T w.
function body.angularMomentum(b)
	local wx, wy, wz = b.wx, b.wy, b.wz
	-- to body frame
	local lx = b.r11 * wx + b.r21 * wy + b.r31 * wz
	local ly = b.r12 * wx + b.r22 * wy + b.r32 * wz
	local lz = b.r13 * wx + b.r23 * wy + b.r33 * wz
	lx, ly, lz = lx * b.Ix, ly * b.Iy, lz * b.Iz
	return b.r11 * lx + b.r12 * ly + b.r13 * lz,
		b.r21 * lx + b.r22 * ly + b.r23 * lz,
		b.r31 * lx + b.r32 * ly + b.r33 * lz
end

-- Kinetic energy (J), and kinetic plus potential with gravity g above z = 0.
function body.kinetic(b)
	local Lx, Ly, Lz = body.angularMomentum(b)
	return 0.5 * b.m * (b.vx * b.vx + b.vy * b.vy + b.vz * b.vz)
		+ 0.5 * (Lx * b.wx + Ly * b.wy + Lz * b.wz)
end

function body.energy(b, g)
	return body.kinetic(b) + b.m * g * b.z
end

-- The world z of the body's lowest point.
function body.lowestZ(b)
	if b.shape == 1 then
		return b.z - (b.hx * math.abs(b.r31) + b.hy * math.abs(b.r32) + b.hz * math.abs(b.r33))
	end
	return b.z - b.hl * math.abs(b.r33) - b.r
end

-- Is the long axis within `sinTol` (sine of the angle) of parallel to the ground?
function body.lying(b, sinTol)
	return math.abs(b.r33) <= sinTol
end

-- Would a box fall if whatever it leans on were taken away? True when the
-- plumb line through its centre lands outside the end face it stands on.
-- (A kubb goes at about 25 degrees from upright, the king at about 17.)
function body.wouldFall(b)
	local up = math.abs(b.r33)
	return b.hz * math.abs(b.r31) > b.hx * up or b.hz * math.abs(b.r32) > b.hy * up
end

tw.body = body
core/burstpick:
-- Which hit burst a baton throw shows, and when (docs/design/README.md "Hit
-- effects"). Pure: reads a core/world (its bodies' kind, toppleT and index)
-- and the time on screen.
--
-- A burst starts when the picture reaches the moment the first kubb or king
-- the throw knocks over was struck (Jamie: the burst and its knock at the
-- impact, not once the piece is down). World bodies carry touchT, the first
-- time something struck them, and toppleT, the time they went down; a piece
-- struck hard enough (falling, below) is taken as going down at its impact,
-- before the physics has run as far as its topple.
-- What kind: the king toppled within `window` s of the first topple, or by
-- now (whenever it fell), is "king" (the winning hit or the losing one); two
-- or more kubbs down within `window` s of the first is "double"; one is
-- "clean". So a king that falls well after a kubb turns the burst into the
-- king's when the picture reaches it (render/burst restarts it). A baton that touches a kubb and leaves it
-- standing, or a miss, gets nothing. Pieces already down when the throw
-- started have no toppleT and never count.
import "core/tw"

local burstpick = {}

burstpick.tune = {
	window = 0.4,     -- s after the first impact that a second one makes it a double
	-- A struck kubb is taken as falling at its impact when, just after the
	-- strike, it moves faster than this or turns faster than this: a 7 x 7 x 15
	-- cm kubb tips over with about 0.39 m/s or 4.1 rad/s about its edge, and a
	-- baton strike gives far more. On the device the physics cannot reach the
	-- topple before the picture reaches the impact (it was 260 ms of shown
	-- time late), so the burst cannot wait for it.
	fallV = 0.5,      -- m/s
	fallW = 5,        -- rad/s
	judgeFor = 0.5,   -- s after the strike the speeds are read (later, the topple or the rest decides)
	grazeFor = 1.0,   -- s: a topple this long after the first touch was a later blow (a slow tip
	                  -- from a hit takes well under a second), so the topple is the moment
}

-- The moment a body was struck: its first touch, unless it toppled more
-- than grazeFor after that (a graze, then a later blow that felled it: the
-- topple is the moment), or nothing recorded a touch.
local function hitTime(b)
	local t, tt = b.touchT, b.toppleT
	if not t or (tt and tt - t > burstpick.tune.grazeFor) then return tt end
	return t
end
burstpick.hitTime = hitTime

-- Is body b falling, as far as the physics knows at world time w.time?
-- Returns falling, sure: sure when it has toppled; a fast-moving struck
-- piece is falling but not sure (its burst may be taken back).
local function falling(b, w)
	if b.kind ~= "kubb" and b.kind ~= "king" then return false end
	if b.toppleT then return true, true end
	if b.toppled then return false end          -- down before this throw
	-- the king only once it has toppled: its burst inverts the screen and
	-- plays the game's end, so a king merely pushed must never get it (its
	-- burst may come up to the physics' lead late; Jamie can weigh that)
	if b.kind == "king" then return false end
	local ht = b.touchT
	if not ht or w.time - ht > burstpick.tune.judgeFor or not b.awake then return false end
	local t = burstpick.tune
	local v2 = b.vx * b.vx + b.vy * b.vy + b.vz * b.vz
	local w2 = b.wx * b.wx + b.wy * b.wy + b.wz * b.wz
	return (v2 >= t.fallV * t.fallV or w2 >= t.fallW * t.fallW), false
end
burstpick.falling = falling

-- The pieces first struck in world time (t0, t1]: kubbs, the king, batons
-- lying on the pitch and the stakes (Jamie, 2026-11-14: "if wood hits wood
-- play a sound"; the ground is not a body, so it never counts), not the
-- thrown piece itself (its own touch is the same blow): a knock each
-- (sound.lua). Fills out[1..count] and returns the count. A plain scan, no
-- tables.
function burstpick.touches(w, t0, t1, out)
	local n, bodies, proj = 0, w.bodies, w.projectile
	for i = 1, w.n do
		local b = bodies[i]
		local t = b.touchT
		if t and t > t0 and t <= t1 and b ~= proj then
			n = n + 1
			out[n] = b
		end
	end
	return n
end

-- Returns nil before the first falling piece's impact is on screen (or when
-- nothing is falling), else kind, first body, second body (the double's
-- second kubb) or nil, and whether the first is sure (toppled). No tables
-- are made.
function burstpick.pick(w, showTime)
	local bodies, n = w.bodies, w.n
	local first, ft, sure = nil, nil, false
	for i = 1, n do
		local b = bodies[i]
		local f, s = falling(b, w)
		if f then
			local ht = hitTime(b)
			if not ft or ht < ft then first, ft, sure = b, ht, s end
		end
	end
	if not first or ft > showTime then return nil end
	local limit = ft + burstpick.tune.window
	local second, king = nil, first.kind == "king" and first or nil
	for i = 1, n do
		local b = bodies[i]
		if b ~= first and falling(b, w) then
			local ht = hitTime(b)
			if b.kind == "king" then
				if ht <= limit or ht <= showTime then king = b end
			elseif ht <= limit and (not second or ht < hitTime(second)) then
				second = b
			end
		end
	end
	if king then
		-- the king's burst is anchored on the king: its own certainty, so a
		-- king struck hard that stays standing is taken back even after a
		-- kubb that surely fell
		if king ~= first then local _, ks = falling(king, w); sure = ks end
		return "king", king, nil, sure
	end
	if second then
		local _, s2 = falling(second, w)
		return "double", first, second, sure, s2
	end
	return "clean", first, nil, sure
end

-- Was a body taken as falling at its impact in the end left standing? (Its
-- burst is taken back.) True once it has gone to sleep, or the throw is
-- over, without toppling.
function burstpick.stoodUp(b, done)
	return not b.toppleT and (done or not b.awake)
end

tw.burstpick = burstpick
core/camera:
-- Pinhole cameras in the world frame of DESIGN.md section 2 (meters; x across,
-- y downfield, z up) projecting onto the 400x240 screen.
-- Pure Lua: no playdate.*.
--
-- A camera is a plain table (see camera.new). It is filled in place by
-- camera.lookAt / camera.aim / camera.impact / camera.follow so the game can
-- keep one table per camera and make no garbage per frame. camera.project
-- returns plain numbers (sx, sy, depth), never a table.
--
-- Every number that sets the framing is in camera.tune.
import "core/tw"

local sqrt, sin, cos, max, min, abs = math.sqrt, math.sin, math.cos, math.max, math.min, math.abs

local camera = {}

camera.SCREEN_W = 400
camera.SCREEN_H = 240

camera.tune = {
	near = 0.05,           -- m; points closer than this along the view axis are not projected
	aim = {
		back = 3.0,          -- m behind the throwing line (DESIGN 3), measured along the aim
		height = 3.4,        -- m above the ground (DESIGN 3)
		lookDist = 7.5,      -- m from the thrower, along the aim, to the ground point at screen center x
		cy = 110,            -- screen row of that ground point (the principal point)
		minTargetPx = 12.5,  -- farthest live target (a standing 0.15 m kubb) at least this tall
		fMin = 880,          -- px; the long lens of DESIGN 3 (about 26 degrees wide) ...
		fMax = 1000,         -- ... to about 23 degrees wide
		stepBackRef = 11,    -- m from the camera to the far baseline with the player on the line;
		                     -- the lens limit grows by stepBack / this when the player steps back
		lookBeyond = 1.5,    -- m past the nearest live target the match camera looks (lookDistFor)
		lookMin = 3.0,       -- m; lookDistFor never looks nearer than this
		side = 0,            -- m the crane stands to the thrower's right, still looking at the
		                     -- same ground point. 0: first person, straight behind (Jamie,
		                     -- 2026-11-15: "return to the first person view"); the over-the-
		                     -- shoulder view is camera.shoulder, while B is held
		circleBeyond = 1.5,  -- m past the target circle the first-person camera looks
		                     -- (camera.lookDistAt), between lookMin and lookDist: the circle
		                     -- stays on screen wherever the d-pad puts it
		-- A target close in front of the thrower (an advantage line near the
		-- middle: Codex on #96) projects under the screen at the long lens:
		-- camera.fitNear lifts it above fitBottom, first by raising the
		-- principal row (as far as fitCyMin), then by widening the lens (never
		-- wider than fitFMin).
		fitBottom = 200,     -- px: the near edge of the circle stays above this row
		fitCyMin = 40,       -- px: the principal row may rise this far
		fitFMin = 360,       -- px: the widest lens the fit may use
	},
	-- The plan view (Jamie, 2026-11-15: "when we hold down B to adjust loft we
	-- should move the camera to that over the shoulder view to see the loft
	-- ... it moves position and zooms out"): while B is held the aim camera
	-- swings from first person to a crane over the thrower's right shoulder,
	-- standing back and up, turned to the middle of the target half, its
	-- lens as long as keeps the whole target half, the planned arc and the
	-- circle in the box below (camera.shoulder). Guesses, tuned by eye on the
	-- Simulator's frames.
	shoulder = {
		side = 2.6,          -- m to the thrower's right
		back = 3.6,          -- m behind the thrower, along the aim
		height = 3.4,        -- m above the ground (first person: 3.4)
		lookY = 6.0,         -- m out from the line to the ground point it turns to (x = 0): the
		                     -- target half's middle
		farX = 2.7,          -- m either side of the middle kept in view on the far baseline (the
		                     -- pitch is 2.5: its corners and the base kubbs)
		nearX = 1.0,         -- m either side kept on the centerline (the king and the middle;
		                     -- the whole width there would need a much wider lens)
		pad = 0.3,           -- m kept beyond the far baseline and short of the centerline
		cornerZ = 0.3,       -- m: the far corners are kept at this height too (a kubb's top)
		left = 12,           -- px: the box everything is fitted into (lens shift: the principal
		right = 388,         -- point moves so the box is filled evenly)
		top = 24,            -- under the rail
		bottom = 200,        -- the arc and the half's near corners may come this low (the minimap
		                     -- and the clock sit below the clear band's 156)
		fMin = 300,          -- px: never wider (a far base kubb about 4 px tall)
		fMax = 880,          -- px: never longer than the first-person lens
		time = 0.4,          -- s for the swing out or back (eased: camera.smooth)
		refit = 0.15,        -- s: the time constant a new fit (a tap of the arc) is eased in with
	},
	impact = {
		dist = 2.75,         -- m, horizontal, from the predicted landing point (DESIGN 3: 2.5 to 3)
		height = 0.9,        -- m (DESIGN 3: low, about 0.9)
		yaw = 0.42,          -- rad the camera sits off the line of flight, toward the pitch center
		lookUp = 0.08,       -- m above the landing point it looks at
		f = 700,             -- px; a standing kubb at the landing point is about 35 px tall
		cy = 104,            -- px row of the look point: high enough that a kubb there stands clear
		                     -- of the throw gauge and its label (stage 2: the hit happens there)
		-- the half circle round a hit (throw.tune.swingDeg) also opens the view
		-- by its end, so the pitch round the piece shows: guesses
		openHeight = 1.6,    -- m
		openDist = 3.4,      -- m
		openF = 420,         -- px
	},
	follow = {
		marginX = 30,        -- px kept between the baton's center and the screen edge while following
		marginTop = 60,
		marginBottom = 40,
		catchBy = 0.25,      -- fraction of the flight by which the baton must be in frame; before
		                     -- that it may still be below the frame (it rises into the aim view
		                     -- from the thrower's hand) and the camera does not chase it
		slack = 600,         -- px it may be below the frame at release, shrinking to 0 by catchBy
		midZoomOut = 0.45,   -- the lens widens by up to this fraction mid-flight, so the high
		                     -- baton and the pitch below it fit in one frame
	},
}

local KUBB_H <const> = 0.15

function camera.new()
	return {
		px = 0, py = 0, pz = 0,      -- position
		fx = 0, fy = 1, fz = 0,      -- forward (unit)
		rx = 1, ry = 0, rz = 0,      -- right (unit, horizontal)
		ux = 0, uy = 0, uz = 1,      -- up (unit)
		f = 900, cx = 200, cy = 120, -- focal length in px and principal point
		lx = 0, ly = 1, lz = 0,      -- the point looked at
	}
end

-- Point the camera at (tx, ty, tz) from (px, py, pz). The right vector stays
-- horizontal, so the horizon is level. Not for looking straight down.
function camera.lookAt(c, px, py, pz, tx, ty, tz)
	c.px, c.py, c.pz = px, py, pz
	c.lx, c.ly, c.lz = tx, ty, tz
	local fx, fy, fz = tx - px, ty - py, tz - pz
	local n = sqrt(fx * fx + fy * fy + fz * fz)
	fx, fy, fz = fx / n, fy / n, fz / n
	local rx, ry = fy, -fx
	local rn = sqrt(rx * rx + ry * ry)
	rx, ry = rx / rn, ry / rn
	c.fx, c.fy, c.fz = fx, fy, fz
	c.rx, c.ry, c.rz = rx, ry, 0
	-- up = right x forward
	c.ux = ry * fz
	c.uy = -rx * fz
	c.uz = rx * fy - ry * fx
	return c
end

-- Camera-space coordinates: right, up, depth (along the view axis).
function camera.toView(c, x, y, z)
	local dx, dy, dz = x - c.px, y - c.py, z - c.pz
	return dx * c.rx + dy * c.ry + dz * c.rz,
		dx * c.ux + dy * c.uy + dz * c.uz,
		dx * c.fx + dy * c.fy + dz * c.fz
end

-- Screen position of a world point: sx, sy, depth. Returns nil when the
-- point is behind the near plane.
function camera.project(c, x, y, z)
	local dx, dy, dz = x - c.px, y - c.py, z - c.pz
	local d = dx * c.fx + dy * c.fy + dz * c.fz
	if d < camera.tune.near then return nil end
	local s = c.f / d
	return c.cx + s * (dx * c.rx + dy * c.ry + dz * c.rz),
		c.cy - s * (dx * c.ux + dy * c.uy + dz * c.uz),
		d
end

-- Screen size in px of a standing upright segment of height h at (x, y):
-- the distance between its projected base and top.
function camera.uprightPx(c, x, y, h)
	local ax, ay = camera.project(c, x, y, 0)
	local bx, by = camera.project(c, x, y, h)
	if not ax or not bx then return 0 end
	return sqrt((ax - bx) ^ 2 + (ay - by) ^ 2)
end

-- Unit aim direction for a swivel angle in radians (0 = straight downfield,
-- positive = to the right, toward +x).
function camera.aimDir(swivel)
	return sin(swivel), cos(swivel)
end

-- The aim camera (DESIGN 3): a crane behind the thrower standing at
-- (playerX, lineY), looking along the swivel. `targets` is an array of
-- {x=, y=} live targets (standing kubbs): the focal length is the smallest in
-- [fMin, fMax] that shows the farthest of them at least minTargetPx tall.
-- `stepBack` (m, optional) is how far behind the throwing line the player
-- stands: the lens limit grows in proportion, so stepping back does not
-- shrink the targets below minTargetPx.
-- `lookDist` (m, optional, default tune.aim.lookDist) moves the ground point
-- at screen center nearer the thrower (the match: field kubbs close by).
function camera.aim(c, playerX, lineY, swivel, targets, stepBack, lookDist)
	local t = camera.tune.aim
	local dx, dy = camera.aimDir(swivel)
	local ld = lookDist or t.lookDist
	local sd = t.side
	camera.lookAt(c,
		playerX - dx * t.back + dy * sd, lineY - dy * t.back - dx * sd, t.height,
		playerX + dx * ld, lineY + dy * ld, 0)
	c.cx, c.cy = camera.SCREEN_W / 2, t.cy
	c.f = 1
	local need = t.fMin
	if targets then
		for i = 1, #targets do
			local k = targets[i]
			local px = camera.uprightPx(c, k.x, k.y, KUBB_H)
			if px > 0 then need = max(need, t.minTargetPx / px) end
		end
	end
	local fMax = t.fMax * (1 + (stepBack or 0) / t.stepBackRef)
	c.f = min(fMax, max(t.fMin, need))
	return c
end

-- Keep the ground point (x, y) (the near edge of the target circle) above
-- tune.aim.fitBottom on camera c: raise the principal row, then widen the
-- lens, within fitCyMin and fitFMin. Nothing changes when it is already
-- above. Returns c.
function camera.fitNear(c, x, y)
	local t = camera.tune.aim
	local _, sy = camera.project(c, x, y, 0)
	if not sy or sy <= t.fitBottom then return c end
	local lift = sy - t.fitBottom
	local cy = c.cy - lift
	if cy < t.fitCyMin then cy = t.fitCyMin end
	sy = sy - (c.cy - cy)
	c.cy = cy
	if sy > t.fitBottom then
		-- the point sits (sy - cy) under the principal row; scale the lens so
		-- it sits (fitBottom - cy) under it
		local f = c.f * (t.fitBottom - cy) / (sy - cy)
		if f < t.fitFMin then f = t.fitFMin end
		c.f = f
	end
	return c
end

-- The look distance that frames the live targets (n of them, {x=, y=}) for a
-- thrower at (playerX, playerY): lookBeyond past the nearest, between lookMin
-- and the default lookDist. Base kubbs on the far baseline give the default.
function camera.lookDistFor(playerX, playerY, targets, n)
	local t = camera.tune.aim
	local best = nil
	for i = 1, n or #targets do
		local k = targets[i]
		local dx, dy = k.x - playerX, k.y - playerY
		local d = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
		if not best or d < best then best = d end
	end
	if not best then return t.lookDist end
	return max(t.lookMin, min(t.lookDist, best + t.lookBeyond))
end

-- The first-person look distance for a target circle at (x, y) and a thrower
-- at (playerX, playerY): circleBeyond past the circle, between lookMin and
-- lookDist (the far baseline gives the default framing).
function camera.lookDistAt(playerX, playerY, x, y)
	local t = camera.tune.aim
	local dx, dy = x - playerX, y - playerY
	return max(t.lookMin, min(t.lookDist, sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) + t.circleBeyond))
end

-- The plan view (tune.shoulder): a crane over the right shoulder of the
-- thrower at (playerX, playerY) facing `swivel`, turned to (0, lineY +
-- lookY), with the lens and principal point that fit the target half
-- (lineY + 4 to lineY + 8 padded, farX either side on the far baseline and
-- nearX on the centerline; the far corners also at cornerZ) and the n extra points xs, ys, zs (the planned arc, the circle)
-- into the box left..right, top..bottom: the longest lens that does, between
-- fMin and fMax, and the principal point that centres them in the box (a lens
-- shift: verticals stay vertical). The first `across` of the extra points
-- (default 0) are kept inside the sides only (the arc's first rise, near the
-- hand: it may come in from the lower edge). Points behind the camera are
-- left out. No tables.
function camera.shoulder(c, playerX, playerY, swivel, lineY, n, xs, ys, zs, across)
	local t = camera.tune.shoulder
	local dx, dy = camera.aimDir(swivel)
	camera.lookAt(c,
		playerX - dx * t.back + dy * t.side, playerY - dy * t.back - dx * t.side, t.height,
		0, lineY + t.lookY, 0)
	local near = camera.tune.near
	local umin, umax, vmin, vmax = math.huge, -math.huge, math.huge, -math.huge
	local px, py, pz = c.px, c.py, c.pz
	local rx, ry = c.rx, c.ry
	local ux, uy, uz = c.ux, c.uy, c.uz
	local fx, fy, fz = c.fx, c.fy, c.fz
	local y0, y1 = lineY + 4 - t.pad, lineY + 8 + t.pad
	local onlyTo = 6 + (across or 0)
	for i = 1, 6 + (n or 0) do
		local x, y, z
		if i <= 6 then
			-- the half: near left, near right (nearX), far left, far right
			-- (farX), then the far ones again at cornerZ
			local hx = (i <= 2) and t.nearX or t.farX
			x = (i % 2 == 1) and -hx or hx
			y = (i <= 2) and y0 or y1
			z = (i >= 5) and t.cornerZ or 0
		else
			x, y, z = xs[i - 6], ys[i - 6], zs and zs[i - 6] or 0
		end
		local ax, ay, az = x - px, y - py, z - pz
		local d = ax * fx + ay * fy + az * fz
		if d >= near then
			local u = (ax * rx + ay * ry) / d
			local v = (ax * ux + ay * uy + az * uz) / d
			if u < umin then umin = u end
			if u > umax then umax = u end
			if i <= 6 or i > onlyTo then
				if v < vmin then vmin = v end
				if v > vmax then vmax = v end
			end
		end
	end
	local f = t.fMax
	if umax > umin then
		local fw = (t.right - t.left) / (umax - umin)
		if fw < f then f = fw end
	end
	if vmax > vmin then
		local fh = (t.bottom - t.top) / (vmax - vmin)
		if fh < f then f = fh end
	end
	if f < t.fMin then f = t.fMin end
	c.f = f
	if umax >= umin then
		c.cx = (t.left + t.right) / 2 - f * (umin + umax) / 2
		c.cy = (t.top + t.bottom) / 2 + f * (vmin + vmax) / 2
	else
		c.cx, c.cy = camera.SCREEN_W / 2, camera.SCREEN_H / 2
	end
	return c
end

-- Camera c between cameras a (e = 0) and b (e = 1): position, the point
-- looked at and the principal point straight, the lens in log space (the
-- zoom feels even). e is already eased. c may not be a or b.
function camera.blend(c, a, b, e)
	if e <= 0 then e = 0 elseif e >= 1 then e = 1 end
	c.f = a.f * (b.f / a.f) ^ e
	c.cx = a.cx + (b.cx - a.cx) * e
	c.cy = a.cy + (b.cy - a.cy) * e
	return camera.lookAt(c,
		a.px + (b.px - a.px) * e, a.py + (b.py - a.py) * e, a.pz + (b.pz - a.pz) * e,
		a.lx + (b.lx - a.lx) * e, a.ly + (b.ly - a.ly) * e, a.lz + (b.lz - a.lz) * e)
end

-- The impact camera (DESIGN 3): low and close to the predicted landing point
-- (lx, ly), set back along the line of flight (dirX, dirY, unit horizontal)
-- and turned off it by tune.impact.yaw toward the pitch center. `side`
-- (1 or -1) fixes which way it turns; by default it is chosen from lx, so a
-- caller that moves the point during a throw passes the side it started with
-- (otherwise the camera jumps across when the point crosses x = 0).
-- `orbit` (radians, default 0) carries the camera further round the point
-- the same way: the half circle of the slow motion after a hit.
-- `open` (0 to 1, default 0) blends height, distance and lens toward the
-- tune's open view as the half circle goes round.
function camera.impact(c, lx, ly, dirX, dirY, side, orbit, open)
	local t = camera.tune.impact
	side = side or ((lx > 0) and 1 or -1)       -- swing the camera toward x = 0
	local a = (t.yaw + (orbit or 0)) * side
	local ca, sa = cos(a), sin(a)
	-- rotate the backwards direction (-dir) by a about z
	local bx, by = -dirX, -dirY
	bx, by = bx * ca - by * sa, bx * sa + by * ca
	local dist, height, f = t.dist, t.height, t.f
	if open and open > 0 then
		dist = dist + (t.openDist - dist) * open
		height = height + (t.openHeight - height) * open
		f = f * (t.openF / f) ^ open        -- in log space, like the follow's zoom
	end
	camera.lookAt(c, lx + bx * dist, ly + by * dist, height, lx, ly, t.lookUp)
	c.f, c.cx, c.cy = f, camera.SCREEN_W / 2, t.cy
	return c
end

local function smooth(s)
	if s <= 0 then return 0 elseif s >= 1 then return 1 end
	return s * s * (3 - 2 * s)
end
camera.smooth = smooth

-- Is the screen point inside the frame less the follow margins? `slack`
-- extends the bottom edge downward.
local function inFrame(sx, sy, slack)
	local m = camera.tune.follow
	return sx and sx >= m.marginX and sx <= camera.SCREEN_W - m.marginX
		and sy >= m.marginTop and sy <= camera.SCREEN_H - m.marginBottom + slack
end

-- The follow camera: blends from camera a (aim) to camera b (impact) as s
-- goes 0 -> 1 over the flight, eased. The baton at (bx, by, bz) is kept in
-- frame: if it would fall outside, the look point is pulled toward it just
-- far enough (found by bisection). Right after release the baton is still
-- below the aim view; it is allowed to rise into frame on its own until
-- tune.follow.catchBy of the flight, so the shot starts as the aim view.
function camera.follow(c, a, b, s, bx, by, bz)
	local e = smooth(s)
	local px = a.px + (b.px - a.px) * e
	local py = a.py + (b.py - a.py) * e
	local pz = a.pz + (b.pz - a.pz) * e
	local lx = a.lx + (b.lx - a.lx) * e
	local ly = a.ly + (b.ly - a.ly) * e
	local lz = a.lz + (b.lz - a.lz) * e
	-- focal length blends in log space so the zoom feels even
	local f = a.f * (b.f / a.f) ^ e
	f = f * (1 - camera.tune.follow.midZoomOut * math.sin(math.pi * e))
	c.f = f
	c.cx = a.cx + (b.cx - a.cx) * e   -- (the aim camera's is off centre while the plan view shows)
	c.cy = a.cy + (b.cy - a.cy) * e
	camera.lookAt(c, px, py, pz, lx, ly, lz)
	if not bx then return c end
	local m = camera.tune.follow
	local slack = m.slack * (1 - min(1, s / m.catchBy))
	local sx, sy = camera.project(c, bx, by, bz)
	if not inFrame(sx, sy, slack) then
		local lo, hi = 0, 1
		for _ = 1, 12 do
			local w = (lo + hi) / 2
			camera.lookAt(c, px, py, pz, lx + (bx - lx) * w, ly + (by - ly) * w, lz + (bz - lz) * w)
			sx, sy = camera.project(c, bx, by, bz)
			if inFrame(sx, sy, slack) then hi = w else lo = w end
		end
		camera.lookAt(c, px, py, pz, lx + (bx - lx) * hi, ly + (by - ly) * hi, lz + (bz - lz) * hi)
	end
	return c
end

-- Clip a ground-plane (z = 0) or general polygon against the near plane and
-- project it. `xs, ys, zs` hold n world points; the screen polygon is written
-- as x1, y1, x2, y2, ... into `out` (reused). Returns the number of screen
-- points (0 when it is all behind the camera).
local vx, vy, vd = {}, {}, {}
function camera.projectPoly(c, n, xs, ys, zs, out)
	local near = camera.tune.near
	for i = 1, n do
		vx[i], vy[i], vd[i] = camera.toView(c, xs[i], ys[i], zs and zs[i] or 0)
	end
	local m = 0
	local f, cx, cy = c.f, c.cx, c.cy
	for i = 1, n do
		local j = (i % n) + 1
		local ai, aj = vd[i] >= near, vd[j] >= near
		if ai then
			m = m + 1
			out[2 * m - 1] = cx + f * vx[i] / vd[i]
			out[2 * m] = cy - f * vy[i] / vd[i]
		end
		if ai ~= aj then
			local t = (near - vd[i]) / (vd[j] - vd[i])
			m = m + 1
			out[2 * m - 1] = cx + f * (vx[i] + (vx[j] - vx[i]) * t) / near
			out[2 * m] = cy - f * (vy[i] + (vy[j] - vy[i]) * t) / near
		end
	end
	return m
end

-- Clip a segment against the near plane and project it. Returns
-- x1, y1, x2, y2 on screen, or nil when it is all behind the camera.
function camera.projectSegment(c, x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2)
	local near = camera.tune.near
	local ax, ay, ad = camera.toView(c, x1, y1, z1)
	local bx, by, bd = camera.toView(c, x2, y2, z2)
	if ad < near and bd < near then return nil end
	if ad < near then
		local t = (near - ad) / (bd - ad)
		ax, ay, ad = ax + (bx - ax) * t, ay + (by - ay) * t, near
	elseif bd < near then
		local t = (near - bd) / (ad - bd)
		bx, by, bd = bx + (ax - bx) * t, by + (ay - by) * t, near
	end
	local f = c.f
	return c.cx + f * ax / ad, c.cy - f * ay / ad, c.cx + f * bx / bd, c.cy - f * by / bd
end

-- The minimap (DESIGN 3): a 45 x 72 px top-down pitch at 9 px per meter with
-- the far baseline (y = 8) at the top. ox, oy is its top-left pixel: the
-- bottom left of the screen, inside a 2 px frame at 4 162 49 76 (docs/design).
camera.minimap = { scale = 9, w = 45, h = 72, ox = 6, oy = 164 }

-- The HUD's clear area (docs/design "HUD" 7): under the rail (y rail) the
-- full width down to y top, then x x0 to x1 down to y bottom (the box
-- 58 16 188 222). What the camera has to keep in view belongs in it.
camera.clear = { rail = 14, top = 156, x0 = 58, x1 = 246, bottom = 238 }

function camera.toMinimap(x, y)
	local m = camera.minimap
	return m.ox + (x + 2.5) * m.scale, m.oy + (8 - y) * m.scale
end

tw.camera = camera
core/cards:
-- What the match's cards say (docs/design/boards/HandOff.png, Winner.png),
-- from the engine's state and its score sheet. Pure Lua: no playdate.*. Once
-- per card, not a per-frame path.
--
--   cards.batonCounts(token)   field, base kubbs a baton token toppled,
--                              whether it is a hit (toppled a kubb, or the
--                              king on a king shot) and whether it is a throw
--   cards.took(g, turn)        { field, base } toppled by batons in that turn
--   cards.handoff(m, setup)    the hand-off card's facts (below)
--   cards.hitRate(g, side)     hits, batons thrown by that side (whole game)
--   cards.winner(m, finish)    the winner card's facts (below)
import "core/tw"
import "core/notation"
import "core/frame"
import "core/pitch"
import "core/match"
import "core/history"

local notation, frame, pitch, cmatch, history = tw.notation, tw.frame, tw.pitch, tw.match, tw.history

local cards = {}

local function team(side, g)
	local t = g and g.teams and g.teams[side]
	return t and t.name or ("Team " .. side)
end
cards.teamName = team

-- "2FB" -> 2, 1, hit; "F" -> 1, 0, hit; "K" -> 0, 0, hit; "2FE" -> 2, 0,
-- hit; "E", "-", "=", "Z" -> 0, 0, no hit. The fourth value is false for
-- "X" (a baton left when the game ended) and "G" (a resign): not throws.
function cards.batonCounts(token)
	if token == "K" then return 0, 0, true, true end
	if token == "X" or token == "G" then return 0, 0, false, false end
	local f, b = 0, 0
	local fs = token:match("^(%d*)F")
	if fs then f = fs == "" and 1 or tonumber(fs) end
	local bs = token:match("(%d*)BE?$")
	if bs then b = bs == "" and 1 or tonumber(bs) end
	return f, b, f + b > 0, true
end

-- Kubbs the batons of sheet turn `turn` toppled (nil when there is no such
-- turn).
function cards.took(g, turn)
	local t = g.sheet.turns[turn]
	if not t then return nil end
	local field, base = 0, 0
	for _, bt in ipairs(t.batons) do
		local f, b = cards.batonCounts(bt.token)
		field, base = field + f, base + b
	end
	return { field = field, base = base }
end

-- Batons a side threw in the whole game and how many were hits.
function cards.hitRate(g, side)
	local hits, thrown = 0, 0
	for _, t in pairs(g.sheet.turns) do
		if t.side == side then
			for _, bt in ipairs(t.batons) do
				local _, _, hit, isThrow = cards.batonCounts(bt.token)
				if isThrow then thrown = thrown + 1 end
				if hit then hits = hits + 1 end
			end
		end
	end
	return hits, thrown
end

-- The hand-off card, before team `setup.side` takes the Playdate (call it
-- after match.setup, so raising and punishment are done):
--   to, toName        the team on turn
--   from, fromName    the team that threw last turn (nil on turn 1)
--   took              { field, base } its batons toppled last turn (nil on turn 1)
--   kubbs             kubbs to throw in first (0 when it starts with batons)
--   batons            batons this turn
--   turn              the turn number
--   base              { top, bottom } standing base kubbs: `from`'s half
--                     (the far end), then `to`'s
--   baseText          the card's line for them, the receiving team's own
--                     first: "YOUR BASE 4 · THEIRS 5" ("BASE 5 V 4" read the
--                     wrong way round: the RC review of 2026-11-15)
--   pieces            the pitch in `to`'s view frame (it throws from y = 0,
--                     the bottom): { x, y, kind = "base"|"field"|"king",
--                     down }: the ten base slots (down = that base kubb is
--                     no longer standing there), every field kubb on the
--                     pitch, then the king
-- and for a team of several players (core/order, docs/PLAYERS.md 5):
--   thrower           the name of the player who throws first (the card is
--                     passed to them)
--   order             this turn's batons by player: { { name, n }, ... }
--   inkaster          the name of the player who throws the kubbs in
function cards.handoff(m, setup)
	local g = m.game
	local to = setup.side
	local from = to == "A" and "B" or "A"
	local c = {
		to = to, toName = team(to, g), turn = g.turn,
		kubbs = setup.kind == "toss" and setup.of or 0,
		batons = g.batonsTotal or 6,
	}
	if g.turn > 1 then
		c.from, c.fromName = from, team(from, g)
		c.took = cards.took(g, g.turn - 1)
	end
	c.base = { #g:baseKubbs(from), #g:baseKubbs(to) }
	c.baseText = { "YOUR BASE " .. c.base[2], "THEIRS " .. c.base[1] }
	local pieces = {}
	-- the ten base slots: standing, or empty (down) once that base kubb is
	-- knocked; then every field kubb on the pitch
	for _, side in ipairs { "A", "B" } do
		for i, bx in ipairs(pitch.baseX) do
			local k = g.kubbs[side:lower() .. i]
			local x, y = frame.point(to, bx, pitch.baseline[side])
			pieces[#pieces + 1] = { id = k.id, x = x, y = y, kind = "base",
				down = not (k.kind == "base" and k.where == "pitch") }
		end
	end
	for _, id in ipairs(g.ids) do
		local k = g.kubbs[id]
		if k.kind == "field" and k.where == "pitch" then
			local x, y = frame.point(to, k.pose.x, k.pose.y)
			pieces[#pieces + 1] = { id = id, x = x, y = y, kind = "field", down = not k.pose.standing }
		end
	end
	local kp = g.king.pose
	local kx, ky = frame.point(to, kp.x, kp.y)
	pieces[#pieces + 1] = { id = "king", x = kx, y = ky, kind = "king", down = false }
	c.pieces = pieces
	if #g.teams[to].players > 1 and setup.thrower then
		c.thrower = setup.thrower.name
		local list, ink = cmatch.turnOrder(m)
		c.order = {}
		for i, e in ipairs(list) do c.order[i] = { name = e.name, n = e.n } end
		c.inkaster = ink and ink.name
	end
	return c
end

-- The pass card inside a team (docs/PLAYERS.md 5), before a throw by a
-- player other than the last one:
--   name       who takes the Playdate
--   team       the team's name
--   level      their throw level (nil when not known)
--   kind       "kubbs" (the kubbs in, and any rethrows) or "batons"
--   from, to   the batons they throw in a row from this one (baton numbers)
function cards.pass(m, setup)
	local g = m.game
	local th = setup.thrower or {}
	local c = { name = th.name or "", team = team(setup.side, g), level = th.level }
	if setup.kind == "toss" then
		c.kind = "kubbs"
	else
		c.kind = "batons"
		c.from, c.to = setup.n, setup.n
		local deal = m.order and m.order.deal or {}
		while deal[c.to + 1] == th.id do c.to = c.to + 1 end
	end
	return c
end

-- The winner card. finish = {year, month, day, hour, min} (the start is
-- m.start; minutes is nil without both):
--   winner, winnerName, how (core/match howText is the sentence), turns,
--   minutes, hits, thrown (the winner's batons)
function cards.winner(m, finish)
	local g = m.game
	local c = { winner = g.winner, winnerName = team(g.winner, g), turns = g.turn }
	if m.start and finish then c.minutes = notation.minutesBetween(m.start, finish) end
	c.hits, c.thrown = cards.hitRate(g, g.winner)
	-- a team of several: each player's hits and batons
	local ps = g.teams[g.winner].players
	if #ps > 1 then
		local stats = history.gameStats(g)
		c.players = {}
		for i, p in ipairs(ps) do
			local st = stats[p.id]
			c.players[i] = { name = p.name, hits = st.hits, thrown = st.batons }
		end
	end
	return c
end

-- The pass card before the defender raises and places punishment kubbs by
-- hand (PASS + PLAY): who takes the Playdate (the defender), how many kubbs
-- it raises (its field kubbs lying), how many punishment kubbs it places,
-- and who it hands the Playdate back to (the attacker, for its batons):
--   side, toName, raise, punish, backName
function cards.settle(g)
	local raise = 0
	for _, k in ipairs(g:fieldKubbs(g.defender)) do
		if not k.pose.standing then raise = raise + 1 end
	end
	return { side = g.defender, toName = team(g.defender, g), raise = raise,
		punish = #g.punishQueue, backName = team(g.attacker, g) }
end

tw.cards = cards
core/collide:
-- Contact generation (narrow phase). Pure Lua: no playdate.*.
--
-- Contacts go into one reused buffer of parallel arrays (no tables per
-- contact). A contact is between body A and body B (B = false for the
-- ground), at world point P on A, with unit normal N pointing from B toward
-- A, and separation `sep` (negative = overlapping). Contacts are made a little
-- before touching (speculative, within `margin`), so fast pieces do not pass
-- through each other between steps.
--
-- Shapes (DESIGN 5):
--   box vs ground       the eight corners
--   capsule vs ground   the two end spheres (on a plane the lowest points of
--                       a capsule are always at its end spheres, so a baton
--                       lying flat rests on both and rolls about its axis)
--   capsule vs box      the closest points of the segment and the box, plus
--                       each end sphere, so a baton lying across a kubb rests
--   box vs box          corners of each box inside (or near) the other, plus
--                       edge on edge: the closest points of two crossing
--                       edges, and the points where crossed faces' edges
--                       cross (collide.boxBox)
--   capsule vs capsule  closest points of the two segments
import "core/tw"

local sqrt, abs = math.sqrt, math.abs

local collide = {}

-- The contact buffer.
local C = {
	n = 0,
	A = {}, B = {}, slot = {},
	px = {}, py = {}, pz = {},
	nx = {}, ny = {}, nz = {},
	sep = {},
}
collide.C = C

function collide.reset()
	C.n = 0
end

local cA, cB, cSlot = C.A, C.B, C.slot
local cPx, cPy, cPz, cNx, cNy, cNz, cSep = C.px, C.py, C.pz, C.nx, C.ny, C.nz, C.sep

local function add(a, b, px, py, pz, nx, ny, nz, sep, slot)
	local i = C.n + 1
	C.n = i
	cA[i], cB[i], cSlot[i] = a, b, slot
	cPx[i], cPy[i], cPz[i] = px, py, pz
	cNx[i], cNy[i], cNz[i] = nx, ny, nz
	cSep[i] = sep
end
collide.add = add

local SX = { -1, 1, 1, -1, -1, 1, 1, -1 }
local SY = { -1, -1, 1, 1, -1, -1, 1, 1 }
local SZ = { -1, -1, -1, -1, 1, 1, 1, 1 }
collide.SX, collide.SY, collide.SZ = SX, SY, SZ

-- The functions below run for every pair and corner of every step, so they
-- write out add, pointBox, the extents and math.abs instead of calling them
-- (on the device a Lua call costs about 9 us, a C call about 4 us; see
-- docs/notes/physics.md, "Physics"). The arithmetic is the same, term for term.

-- Box b against the ground plane z = 0: each corner below `margin`.
function collide.groundBox(b, margin)
	local hx, hy, hz = b.hx, b.hy, b.hz
	local r31, r32, r33 = b.r31, b.r32, b.r33
	local z0 = b.z
	local x0, y0 = b.x, b.y
	local az, bz, cz = r31 * hx, r32 * hy, r33 * hz
	-- quick reject: the lowest corner is above the margin
	local aaz, abz, acz = az, bz, cz
	if aaz < 0 then aaz = -aaz end
	if abz < 0 then abz = -abz end
	if acz < 0 then acz = -acz end
	if z0 - (aaz + abz + acz) >= margin then return end
	local ax, ay = b.r11 * hx, b.r21 * hx
	local bx, by = b.r12 * hy, b.r22 * hy
	local cx, cy = b.r13 * hz, b.r23 * hz
	local i = C.n
	for k = 1, 8 do
		local sx, sy, sz = SX[k], SY[k], SZ[k]
		local pz = z0 + sx * az + sy * bz + sz * cz
		if pz < margin then
			i = i + 1
			cA[i], cB[i], cSlot[i] = b, false, k
			cPx[i], cPy[i], cPz[i] = x0 + sx * ax + sy * bx + sz * cx, y0 + sx * ay + sy * by + sz * cy, pz
			cNx[i], cNy[i], cNz[i] = 0, 0, 1
			cSep[i] = pz
		end
	end
	C.n = i
end

-- Capsule b against the ground: its two end spheres.
function collide.groundCapsule(b, margin)
	local hl, r = b.hl, b.r
	local ax, ay, az = b.r13 * hl, b.r23 * hl, b.r33 * hl
	local z1, z2 = b.z - az - r, b.z + az - r
	if z1 < margin then add(b, false, b.x - ax, b.y - ay, z1, 0, 0, 1, z1, 1) end
	if z2 < margin then add(b, false, b.x + ax, b.y + ay, z2, 0, 0, 1, z2, 2) end
end

-- Closest point of box B to the world point p. Returns the distance from
-- the box surface (negative inside: minus the depth to the nearest face),
-- the world unit normal pointing out of the box toward p, and the box point.
-- (Written out again in cornersInto and sphereBox.)
local function pointBox(B, px, py, pz)
	local dx, dy, dz = px - B.x, py - B.y, pz - B.z
	local r11, r12, r13, r21, r22, r23, r31, r32, r33 =
		B.r11, B.r12, B.r13, B.r21, B.r22, B.r23, B.r31, B.r32, B.r33
	local lx = r11 * dx + r21 * dy + r31 * dz
	local ly = r12 * dx + r22 * dy + r32 * dz
	local lz = r13 * dx + r23 * dy + r33 * dz
	local hx, hy, hz = B.hx, B.hy, B.hz
	local qx = lx > hx and hx or (lx < -hx and -hx or lx)
	local qy = ly > hy and hy or (ly < -hy and -hy or ly)
	local qz = lz > hz and hz or (lz < -hz and -hz or lz)
	local ex, ey, ez = lx - qx, ly - qy, lz - qz
	local d2 = ex * ex + ey * ey + ez * ez
	local nx, ny, nz, dist
	if d2 > 1e-14 then
		dist = sqrt(d2)
		nx, ny, nz = ex / dist, ey / dist, ez / dist
	else
		-- inside: the face of least penetration
		local px_, py_, pz_ = hx - abs(lx), hy - abs(ly), hz - abs(lz)
		if px_ <= py_ and px_ <= pz_ then
			nx, ny, nz, dist = (lx >= 0) and 1 or -1, 0, 0, -px_
			qx = nx * hx
		elseif py_ <= pz_ then
			nx, ny, nz, dist = 0, (ly >= 0) and 1 or -1, 0, -py_
			qy = ny * hy
		else
			nx, ny, nz, dist = 0, 0, (lz >= 0) and 1 or -1, -pz_
			qz = nz * hz
		end
	end
	return dist,
		r11 * nx + r12 * ny + r13 * nz, r21 * nx + r22 * ny + r23 * nz, r31 * nx + r32 * ny + r33 * nz,
		B.x + r11 * qx + r12 * qy + r13 * qz, B.y + r21 * qx + r22 * qy + r23 * qz, B.z + r31 * qx + r32 * qy + r33 * qz
end
collide.pointBox = pointBox
