		frameDt = frameDt,
		frames = 0,       -- last recorded frame (frame 0 is the start)
		frame = 0,        -- the frame on screen; the scene advances it
		done = false,     -- the world came to rest (or ran out of time)
		rec = {},
		steps = 0,        -- physics steps taken
		busy = 0,         -- seconds spent in advance()
		awakeMax = 0,     -- the most bodies awake in any step
		contactsMax = 0,  -- the most contacts in any step
		calmFrom = nil,   -- see playback.calm
		calmLin2 = playback.calm.lin * playback.calm.lin,
		calmAng2 = playback.calm.ang * playback.calm.ang,
		v = 0,            -- the pace (playback.pace)
	}
	record(pb)
	return pb
end

-- Step the world until `ahead` frames past the one on screen are recorded,
-- the world is at rest, or `budget` seconds of clock() have gone by.
-- Returns the number of steps taken.
function playback.advance(pb, budget, clock, ahead)
	if pb.done then return 0 end
	local w = pb.w
	local t0 = clock()
	local stop = t0 + budget
	local want = pb.frame + (ahead or 1000000)
	local n = 0
	local dt = world.tune.dt
	local last = t0
	while pb.frames < want do
		world.step(w)
		n = n + 1
		if w.awakeCount > pb.awakeMax then pb.awakeMax = w.awakeCount end
		if w.contacts > pb.contactsMax then pb.contactsMax = w.contacts end
		local rest = world.isAtRest(w)
		-- record each display frame this step reached (within half a step)
		while w.time + dt * 0.5 >= (pb.frames + 1) * pb.frameDt do
			pb.frames = pb.frames + 1
			record(pb)
		end
		if rest then
			pb.frames = pb.frames + 1
			record(pb)
			pb.done = true
			break
		end
		-- stop when the next step, as long as this one, would end more than
		-- half of it past the budget (a contact step costs several times a
		-- free flight's: stopping only once the budget was spent overran it by
		-- up to a whole step, stopping before any overrun wastes up to one)
		local now = clock()
		if now + (now - last) * 0.5 >= stop then break end
		last = now
	end
	pb.steps = pb.steps + n
	pb.busy = pb.busy + (clock() - t0)
	return n
end

-- Pose of body index i at frame f (clamped to what is recorded).
function playback.pose(pb, i, f)
	local r = pb.rec[i]
	if f > pb.frames then f = pb.frames end
	if r.start < 0 or f < r.start then
		return r.x, r.y, r.z, r.qw, r.qx, r.qy, r.qz
	end
	local d, k = r.data, (f - r.start) * 7
	return d[k + 1], d[k + 2], d[k + 3], d[k + 4], d[k + 5], d[k + 6], d[k + 7]
end

-- Pose of body index i at time t (s from the release; clamped to what is
-- recorded), between the two recorded frames around it: position linear,
-- rotation the normalized linear blend of the two quaternions (the frames
-- are 20 ms apart, so the difference from a true slerp is far below a pixel).
function playback.poseAt(pb, i, t)
	local u = t / pb.frameDt
	local f = floor(u)
	if f < 0 then f, u = 0, 0 end
	local r = pb.rec[i]
	local start = r.start
	if f >= pb.frames or start < 0 or f + 1 < start then return playback.pose(pb, i, f) end
	local a = u - f
	local d = r.data
	local x0, y0, z0, w0, i0, j0, k0
	if f < start then
		x0, y0, z0, w0, i0, j0, k0 = r.x, r.y, r.z, r.qw, r.qx, r.qy, r.qz
	else
		local k = (f - start) * 7
		x0, y0, z0, w0, i0, j0, k0 = d[k + 1], d[k + 2], d[k + 3], d[k + 4], d[k + 5], d[k + 6], d[k + 7]
	end
	if a <= 0 then return x0, y0, z0, w0, i0, j0, k0 end
	local k = (f + 1 - start) * 7
	local x1, y1, z1, w1, i1, j1, k1 = d[k + 1], d[k + 2], d[k + 3], d[k + 4], d[k + 5], d[k + 6], d[k + 7]
	if w0 * w1 + i0 * i1 + j0 * j1 + k0 * k1 < 0 then w1, i1, j1, k1 = -w1, -i1, -j1, -k1 end
	local qw, qx, qy, qz = w0 + (w1 - w0) * a, i0 + (i1 - i0) * a, j0 + (j1 - j0) * a, k0 + (k1 - k0) * a
	local n = sqrt(qw * qw + qx * qx + qy * qy + qz * qz)
	if n > 0 then n = 1 / n; qw, qx, qy, qz = qw * n, qx * n, qy * n, qz * n end
	return x0 + (x1 - x0) * a, y0 + (y1 - y0) * a, z0 + (z1 - z0) * a, qw, qx, qy, qz
end

-- The pace: how fast the picture plays (1 = real time) so that it never
-- catches up with the physics. It follows the simulated time computed ahead
-- of the screen: horizon seconds of it or more play in real time, less plays
-- slower in proportion (so the picture runs at the rate the physics makes
-- frames, and a frame budget that buys more steps fills the store up again).
-- The pace rises by at most rise per second and falls by at most fall per
-- second, so a change of speed is a smooth ease, never a jump; never below
-- floor. Once the throw is computed to rest it eases back to real time.
playback.paceTune = { horizon = 0.4, floor = 0.1, rise = 1.5, fall = 3.0 }

-- Advance the pace by dt seconds of real time with the picture at showTime;
-- returns the new pace (also kept in pb.v).
function playback.pace(pb, showTime, dt)
	local k = playback.paceTune
	local target = 1
	if not pb.done then
		target = (pb.frames * pb.frameDt - showTime) / k.horizon
		if target > 1 then target = 1 elseif target < k.floor then target = k.floor end
	end
	local v = pb.v
	if target > v then
		v = v + k.rise * dt
		if v > target then v = target end
	else
		v = v - k.fall * dt
		if v < target then v = target end
	end
	pb.v = v
	return v
end

-- Slow motion around a hit. Because the physics runs ahead of the screen,
-- the time of the first hit is known before it is shown. Returns the speed
-- of the picture (1 = real time) at screen time `t` for a hit at `hitTime`
-- (nil = no hit known): slowRate from `lead` seconds before the hit until
-- `hold` seconds after it, then easing back to 1 over `ease` seconds.
-- Jamie (2026-11-14): the slow motion is there for the impact, so it ends
-- right after it (it was hold 0.45, ease 0.35: it went on while the baton
-- slid to a stop and held the play up).
playback.slow = { rate = 0.3, lead = 0.10, hold = 0.12, ease = 0.15 }

function playback.speed(t, hitTime)
	if not hitTime then return 1 end
	local k = playback.slow
	local d = t - hitTime
	if d < -k.lead then return 1 end
	if d <= k.hold then return k.rate end
	local e = (d - k.hold) / k.ease
	if e >= 1 then return 1 end
	return k.rate + (1 - k.rate) * e
end

-- Run to the end without a clock (tests, the desktop).
function playback.finish(pb)
	while not pb.done do playback.advance(pb, math.huge, function() return 0 end) end
	return pb
end

-- Bytes of pose data held (8 per number; a rough figure for the readout).
function playback.size(pb)
	local n = 0
	for i = 1, #pb.rec do n = n + #pb.rec[i].data end
	return n * 8
end

tw.playback = playback
core/quat:
-- Unit quaternions for body orientation. Pure Lua: no playdate.*.
--
-- To make no garbage in the physics step, every function takes and returns
-- plain numbers (w, x, y, z), never tables. A quaternion q turns body-local
-- vectors into world vectors: v_world = q v_local q*.
--
-- Rotation matrices are returned as nine numbers, row-major:
-- r11, r12, r13, r21, r22, r23, r31, r32, r33. Column k is the body's local
-- axis k in world coordinates (column 3 = the local z axis).
import "core/tw"

local sqrt, sin, cos = math.sqrt, math.sin, math.cos

local quat = {}

function quat.identity()
	return 1, 0, 0, 0
end

function quat.normalize(w, x, y, z)
	local n = sqrt(w * w + x * x + y * y + z * z)
	if n < 1e-12 then return 1, 0, 0, 0 end
	n = 1 / n
	return w * n, x * n, y * n, z * n
end

-- Hamilton product a * b (apply b first, then a).
function quat.mul(aw, ax, ay, az, bw, bx, by, bz)
	return aw * bw - ax * bx - ay * by - az * bz,
		aw * bx + ax * bw + ay * bz - az * by,
		aw * by - ax * bz + ay * bw + az * bx,
		aw * bz + ax * by - ay * bx + az * bw
end

function quat.conj(w, x, y, z)
	return w, -x, -y, -z
end

-- Rotation by `angle` radians about the unit axis (ax, ay, az).
function quat.fromAxisAngle(ax, ay, az, angle)
	local h = angle * 0.5
	local s = sin(h)
	return cos(h), ax * s, ay * s, az * s
end

-- Rotate the vector (vx, vy, vz) by q.
function quat.rotate(w, x, y, z, vx, vy, vz)
	-- t = 2 (q.xyz x v); v' = v + w t + q.xyz x t
	local tx = 2 * (y * vz - z * vy)
	local ty = 2 * (z * vx - x * vz)
	local tz = 2 * (x * vy - y * vx)
	return vx + w * tx + (y * tz - z * ty),
		vy + w * ty + (z * tx - x * tz),
		vz + w * tz + (x * ty - y * tx)
end

-- The rotation matrix of q (nine numbers, row-major).
function quat.toMatrix(w, x, y, z)
	local xx, yy, zz = x * x, y * y, z * z
	local xy, xz, yz = x * y, x * z, y * z
	local wx, wy, wz = w * x, w * y, w * z
	return 1 - 2 * (yy + zz), 2 * (xy - wz), 2 * (xz + wy),
		2 * (xy + wz), 1 - 2 * (xx + zz), 2 * (yz - wx),
		2 * (xz - wy), 2 * (yz + wx), 1 - 2 * (xx + yy)
end

-- The quaternion of a rotation matrix (row-major). Shepperd's method.
function quat.fromMatrix(r11, r12, r13, r21, r22, r23, r31, r32, r33)
	local tr = r11 + r22 + r33
	local w, x, y, z
	if tr > 0 then
		local s = sqrt(tr + 1) * 2
		w, x, y, z = 0.25 * s, (r32 - r23) / s, (r13 - r31) / s, (r21 - r12) / s
	elseif r11 > r22 and r11 > r33 then
		local s = sqrt(1 + r11 - r22 - r33) * 2
		w, x, y, z = (r32 - r23) / s, 0.25 * s, (r12 + r21) / s, (r13 + r31) / s
	elseif r22 > r33 then
		local s = sqrt(1 + r22 - r11 - r33) * 2
		w, x, y, z = (r13 - r31) / s, (r12 + r21) / s, 0.25 * s, (r23 + r32) / s
	else
		local s = sqrt(1 + r33 - r11 - r22) * 2
		w, x, y, z = (r21 - r12) / s, (r13 + r31) / s, (r23 + r32) / s, 0.25 * s
	end
	return quat.normalize(w, x, y, z)
end

-- The quaternion whose local x, y, z axes are the given world vectors
-- (orthonormal, right-handed: x cross y = z).
function quat.fromAxes(xx, xy, xz, yx, yy, yz, zx, zy, zz)
	return quat.fromMatrix(xx, yx, zx, xy, yy, zy, xz, yz, zz)
end

-- Advance q by the world angular velocity (wx, wy, wz) over dt:
-- q' = q + dt/2 (0, w) q, renormalized.
function quat.integrate(w, x, y, z, wx, wy, wz, dt)
	local h = 0.5 * dt
	local dw = -(wx * x + wy * y + wz * z)
	local dx = wx * w + wy * z - wz * y
	local dy = wy * w + wz * x - wx * z
	local dz = wz * w + wx * y - wy * x
	return quat.normalize(w + h * dw, x + h * dx, y + h * dy, z + h * dz)
end

-- Angle in radians between two orientations.
function quat.angleBetween(aw, ax, ay, az, bw, bx, by, bz)
	local d = math.abs(aw * bw + ax * bx + ay * by + az * bz)
	if d > 1 then d = 1 end
	return 2 * math.acos(d)
end

tw.quat = quat
core/raising:
-- Raising geometry (Rules V4.0 II.D) and punishment placement (II.D.11).
-- Pure Lua: no playdate.*. Not a per-frame path.
--
-- A pose is { x, y, standing, angle, onTop }:
--   x, y      center of the kubb on the ground, meters
--   standing  true when it stands on an end (upright), false when lying
--   angle     lying: direction of the long axis (radians from +x);
--             standing: yaw of the 7 x 7 square
--   onTop     id of a kubb it rests on (II.D.6), else nil
--
-- Raising a lying kubb tips it onto one end, keeping that end's two bottom
-- corners on the ground (II.D.1). Pivoting about that bottom edge leaves the
-- end face flat on the ground just beyond the old end, so the two footprints
-- are 7 x 7 squares centered 7.5 + 3.5 = 11 cm out along the axis each way.
-- End 1 is the +axis end, end 2 the -axis end.
--
-- A context says what is around the kubb being raised:
--   ctx.half    the defender's half ("A" or "B"): where it must be raised
--   ctx.king    the king's pose (standing)
--   ctx.others  array of { id, pose } for every other kubb on the pitch
import "core/tw"
import "core/pitch"
import "core/rect"
import "core/quat"

local pitch, rect = tw.pitch, tw.rect
local cos, sin, pi, sqrt, huge, floor = math.cos, math.sin, math.pi, math.sqrt, math.huge, math.floor

local raising = {}

raising.tune = {
	searchDirections = 32,   -- directions tried when a footprint must slide clear of an obstruction
	searchStep = 0.004,      -- m, coarse step of that search before bisection
	searchMax = 0.6,         -- m, give up beyond this
	punishGrid = 0.1,        -- m, spacing of candidate punishment spots
}

local HALF_LONG, HALF_SIDE = pitch.kubbLong / 2, pitch.kubbSide / 2
local FOOT_OFFSET = HALF_LONG + HALF_SIDE

function raising.pose(x, y, standing, angle, onTop)
	return { x = x, y = y, standing = standing and true or false, angle = angle or 0, onTop = onTop }
end

local function copyPose(p)
	return { x = p.x, y = p.y, standing = p.standing, angle = p.angle or 0, onTop = p.onTop }
end
raising.copyPose = copyPose

-- The ground rectangle a kubb occupies in this pose.
function raising.kubbRect(p)
	if p.standing then return rect.new(p.x, p.y, p.angle or 0, HALF_SIDE, HALF_SIDE) end
	return rect.new(p.x, p.y, p.angle or 0, HALF_LONG, HALF_SIDE)
end

function raising.kingRect(p)
	local h = pitch.kingSide / 2
	return rect.new(p.x, p.y, p.angle or 0, h, h)
end

-- Both standing poses of a lying kubb: { [1] = +axis end, [2] = -axis end }.
function raising.footprints(p)
	local a = p.angle or 0
	local c, s = cos(a), sin(a)
	return {
		{ x = p.x + c * FOOT_OFFSET, y = p.y + s * FOOT_OFFSET, standing = true, angle = a },
		{ x = p.x - c * FOOT_OFFSET, y = p.y - s * FOOT_OFFSET, standing = true, angle = a },
	}
end

-- A lying kubb part way up onto end `which` (1 = +axis, 2 = -axis): it
-- pivots on that end's bottom edge (II.D.1), t = 0 lying, t = 1 standing on
-- that end's footprint. Returns its centre and orientation, x, y, z, qw, qx,
-- qy, qz (the long axis is the body's local z, as core/body has it), for
-- drawing the crank raise. Pure numbers, no tables.
function raising.tipPose(p, which, t)
	local a = p.angle or 0
	local ux, uy = cos(a), sin(a)
	if which == 2 then ux, uy = -ux, -uy end
	local L, S = pitch.kubbLong, pitch.kubbSide
	local th = t * pi / 2
	local c, sn = cos(th), sin(th)
	-- the pivot (the end's bottom edge) and the centre around it, in the plane
	-- of the axis and up
	local px, py = p.x + ux * L / 2, p.y + uy * L / 2
	local along, up = -L / 2 * c + S / 2 * sn, L / 2 * sn + S / 2 * c
	-- the orientation: first turned about the vertical to the kubb's angle (so
	-- the square cross-section is square to its axis and a face lies flat),
	-- then the long axis turned from up to along the ground (a quarter turn
	-- about the horizontal normal) and on by th toward down
	local quat = tw.quat
	local zw, zx, zy, zz = quat.fromAxisAngle(0, 0, 1, a)
	local tw_, tx, ty, tz = quat.fromAxisAngle(-uy, ux, 0, pi / 2 + th)
	local qw, qx, qy, qz = quat.mul(tw_, tx, ty, tz, zw, zx, zy, zz)
	return px + ux * along, py + uy * along, up, qw, qx, qy, qz
end

-- A standing pose is in bounds when its center is in the half (50% in is in).
function raising.inBounds(p, half)
	return pitch.inHalf(half, p.x, p.y)
end

-- Can this kubb end up standing in bounds? Standing on an end: already raised
-- if 50% in (II.D.2). Lying: if either footprint is in bounds (II.D.3).
function raising.canRaise(p, half)
	if p.standing then return raising.inBounds(p, half) end
	local f = raising.footprints(p)
	return raising.inBounds(f[1], half) or raising.inBounds(f[2], half)
end

-- What obstructs a standing footprint: "king", "stake" or a kubb id; nil if clear.
function raising.obstruction(fp, ctx)
	local r = raising.kubbRect(fp)
	if ctx.king and rect.overlap(r, raising.kingRect(ctx.king)) then return "king" end
	for _, s in ipairs(pitch.stakes) do
		if rect.pointDistance(r, s.x, s.y) < pitch.stakeRadius - rect.eps then return "stake" end
	end
	for _, o in ipairs(ctx.others or {}) do
		if rect.overlap(r, raising.kubbRect(o.pose)) then return o.id end
	end
	return nil
end

-- Slide `p` the shortest distance that makes ok(pose) true, trying evenly
-- spread directions. Returns the moved pose and the distance, or nil.
function raising.nearestClear(p, ok, dirs)
	local t = raising.tune
	local best, bestD = nil, huge
	local n = t.searchDirections
	local list = dirs
	if not list then
		list = {}
		for k = 0, n - 1 do
			local a = 2 * pi * k / n
			list[#list + 1] = { cos(a), sin(a) }
		end
	end
	for _, d in ipairs(list) do
		local prev = 0
		local step = t.searchStep
		local dist = step
		while dist <= t.searchMax and dist < bestD do
			local q = copyPose(p)
			q.x, q.y = p.x + d[1] * dist, p.y + d[2] * dist
			if ok(q) then
				local lo, hi = prev, dist
				for _ = 1, 20 do
					local mid = (lo + hi) / 2
					local m = copyPose(p)
					m.x, m.y = p.x + d[1] * mid, p.y + d[2] * mid
					if ok(m) then hi = mid else lo = mid end
				end
				local r = copyPose(p)
				r.x, r.y = p.x + d[1] * hi, p.y + d[2] * hi
				if hi < bestD then best, bestD = r, hi end
				break
			end
			prev = dist
			dist = dist + step
		end
	end
	return best, best and bestD or nil
end

-- The raising decision for one kubb (II.D.1 to II.D.5). Returns
--   { mode, choices, ends }
-- where ends[i] = { pose, inBounds, obstructedBy } for both footprints and
-- choices is the list the defender may pick from, each { which = 1|2, pose,
-- displaced }. Modes:
--   "standing"  it already stands on an end in bounds: not moved (II.D.2)
--   "choice"    both footprints clear and in bounds: the defender chooses
--   "forced"    exactly one footprint clear and in bounds: raised there
--   "displaced" no clear footprint: raised on an in-bounds end touching the
--               obstruction as close as possible to its footprint (II.D.5);
--               when both ends qualify the defender chooses
--   "out"       it cannot be raised in bounds (the engine never asks then)
function raising.options(p, ctx)
	if p.standing then
		local mode = raising.inBounds(p, ctx.half) and "standing" or "out"
		return { mode = mode, choices = mode == "standing" and { { which = 0, pose = copyPose(p) } } or {}, ends = {} }
	end
	local fps = raising.footprints(p)
	local ends = {}
	for i = 1, 2 do
		ends[i] = { pose = fps[i], inBounds = raising.inBounds(fps[i], ctx.half), obstructedBy = raising.obstruction(fps[i], ctx) }
	end
	local clear = {}
	for i = 1, 2 do
		if ends[i].inBounds and not ends[i].obstructedBy then clear[#clear + 1] = i end
	end
	if #clear == 2 then
		return { mode = "choice", ends = ends, choices = {
			{ which = 1, pose = fps[1] }, { which = 2, pose = fps[2] } } }
	elseif #clear == 1 then
		return { mode = "forced", ends = ends, choices = { { which = clear[1], pose = fps[clear[1]] } } }
	end
	local choices = {}
	local ok = function(q)
		return raising.inBounds(q, ctx.half) and not raising.obstruction(q, ctx)
	end
	for i = 1, 2 do
		if ends[i].inBounds then
			local q = raising.nearestClear(fps[i], ok)
			if q then choices[#choices + 1] = { which = i, pose = q, displaced = true } end
		end
	end
	if #choices == 0 then
		-- Nowhere clear within reach (a crowded corner): an in-bounds
		-- footprint is used as it is rather than leaving the kubb down.
		for i = 1, 2 do
			if ends[i].inBounds then choices[#choices + 1] = { which = i, pose = fps[i], displaced = false, crowded = true } end
		end
		if #choices == 0 then return { mode = "out", ends = ends, choices = {} } end
	end
	return { mode = "displaced", ends = ends, choices = choices }
end

-- II.D.6: a kubb resting on another is lowered straight down to the pitch,
-- touching the lower kubb. It keeps its axis, lies flat, and slides out
-- along the line from the lower kubb's center to its own (or across the
-- lower kubb's axis when the centers coincide) until it just touches.
function raising.lower(upper, lowerPose)
	local p = copyPose(upper)
	p.standing, p.onTop = false, nil
	local lr = raising.kubbRect(lowerPose)
	local dx, dy = p.x - lowerPose.x, p.y - lowerPose.y
	local len = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
	if len < 1e-6 then
		local a = (lowerPose.angle or 0) + pi / 2
		dx, dy, len = cos(a), sin(a), 1
	end
	local dir = { { dx / len, dy / len } }
	local ok = function(q) return not rect.overlap(raising.kubbRect(q), lr) end
	if ok(p) then return p end
	local q = raising.nearestClear(p, ok, dir)
	return q or p
end

-- Automatic choosers for the "auto raise" setting and the computer. Each takes
-- (decision, ctx) and returns an index into decision.choices.
local function spread(pose, ctx)
	local m = huge
	for _, o in ipairs(ctx.others or {}) do
		local dx, dy = o.pose.x - pose.x, o.pose.y - pose.y
		local d = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
		if d < m then m = d end
	end
	return m
end

raising.policies = {
	-- Keep kubbs apart: the end farthest from the nearest other kubb (the
	-- defender's usual aim: no doubles). Ties go to the deeper end.
	apart = function(dec, ctx)
		local best, bestScore = 1, -huge
		for i, c in ipairs(dec.choices) do
			local s = spread(c.pose, ctx) + 1e-3 * pitch.fromBaseline(pitch.other(ctx.half), c.pose.y)
			if s > bestScore + 1e-12 then best, bestScore = i, s end
		end
		return best
	end,
	-- Group them (for drills and tests).
	together = function(dec, ctx)
		local best, bestScore = 1, huge
		for i, c in ipairs(dec.choices) do
			local s = spread(c.pose, ctx)
			if s < bestScore - 1e-12 then best, bestScore = i, s end
		end
		return best
	end,
	first = function() return 1 end,
}

function raising.choose(dec, ctx, policy)
	if #dec.choices <= 1 then return 1 end
	local fn = type(policy) == "function" and policy or raising.policies[policy or "apart"]
	return fn(dec, ctx)
end

-- II.D.11: a punishment kubb stands anywhere in the defender's half, at
-- least one baton length (30 cm, edge to edge) from the king and from every
-- stake, not overlapping another kubb. Returns true, or false and a reason.
function raising.punishmentCheck(p, ctx)
	if not raising.inBounds(p, ctx.half) then return false, "not in the half" end
	local r = raising.kubbRect(p)
	if ctx.king and rect.distance(r, raising.kingRect(ctx.king)) < pitch.batonLength - 1e-9 then
		return false, "closer than a baton length to the king"
	end
	for _, s in ipairs(pitch.stakes) do
		if rect.pointDistance(r, s.x, s.y) < pitch.batonLength - 1e-9 then
			return false, "closer than a baton length to a stake"
		end
	end
	for _, o in ipairs(ctx.others or {}) do
		if rect.overlap(r, raising.kubbRect(o.pose)) then return false, "overlaps kubb " .. o.id end
	end
	return true
end

-- Every valid punishment spot on a grid (standing, yaw 0).
function raising.punishmentCandidates(ctx)
	local g = raising.tune.punishGrid
	local out = {}
	local y0 = pitch.baseline[ctx.half]
	local dirY = ctx.half == "A" and 1 or -1
	local nx = floor(2 * pitch.halfWidth / g + 0.5)
	local ny = floor(pitch.center / g + 0.5)
	for j = 0, ny do
		for i = 0, nx do
			local p = { x = -pitch.halfWidth + i * g, y = y0 + dirY * j * g, standing = true, angle = 0 }
			if raising.punishmentCheck(p, ctx) then out[#out + 1] = p end
		end
	end
	return out
end

-- A spot this far (center to center) from everything is valid without the
-- rectangle tests: farther than a baton length plus both half-diagonals from
-- the king and the stakes, and than both half-diagonals from every kubb.
local KUBB_DIAG = HALF_SIDE * sqrt(2)
local LYING_DIAG = sqrt(HALF_LONG * HALF_LONG + HALF_SIDE * HALF_SIDE)
local scratch = { x = 0, y = 0, standing = true, angle = 0 }

-- The spot (x, y) with nothing near it: true, or nil when something is close
-- enough that raising.punishmentCheck has to decide. Makes no tables.
local function clearSpot(x, y, ctx)
	local king = ctx.king
	if king then
		local dx, dy = king.x - x, king.y - y
		local r = pitch.batonLength + KUBB_DIAG + pitch.kingSide / 2 * sqrt(2) + 1e-6
		if dx * dx + dy * dy < r * r then return nil end
	end
	local r = pitch.batonLength + KUBB_DIAG + 1e-6
	local r2 = r * r
	local stakes = pitch.stakes
	for i = 1, #stakes do
		local dx, dy = stakes[i].x - x, stakes[i].y - y
		if dx * dx + dy * dy < r2 then return nil end
	end
	r = KUBB_DIAG + LYING_DIAG + 1e-6
	r2 = r * r
	local others = ctx.others
	if others then
		for i = 1, #others do
			local o = others[i].pose
			local dx, dy = o.x - x, o.y - y
			if dx * dx + dy * dy < r2 then return nil end
		end
	end
	return true
end

-- The automatic placement: deep in the half (far from the attacker) and away
-- from other kubbs. `policy` may be a function(candidates, ctx) -> pose.
-- The default search makes no table per spot: on the device the plain
-- candidate list (2091 spots, a dozen rectangles each) ran past the 10 s
-- watchdog. It picks the same spot as scoring raising.punishmentCandidates.
function raising.autoPunishment(ctx, policy)
	if type(policy) == "function" then
		local cands = raising.punishmentCandidates(ctx)
		if #cands == 0 then return nil end
		return policy(cands, ctx)
	end
	local g = raising.tune.punishGrid
	local y0 = pitch.baseline[ctx.half]
	local dirY = ctx.half == "A" and 1 or -1
	local nx = floor(2 * pitch.halfWidth / g + 0.5)
	local ny = floor(pitch.center / g + 0.5)
	local far = pitch.other(ctx.half)
	local p = scratch
	local bx, by, bestScore = nil, nil, -huge
	for j = 0, ny do
		-- rows run from the deepest; a row whose best possible score cannot
		-- beat the spot in hand ends the search (the usual case: row one)
		local rowBest = pitch.fromBaseline(far, y0 + dirY * j * g) + 0.5
		if rowBest <= bestScore + 1e-12 then break end
		for i = 0, nx do
			p.x, p.y = -pitch.halfWidth + i * g, y0 + dirY * j * g
			if rowBest - 0.01 * math.abs(p.x) > bestScore + 1e-12 and raising.inBounds(p, ctx.half)
				and (clearSpot(p.x, p.y, ctx) or raising.punishmentCheck(p, ctx)) then
				local sp = spread(p, ctx)
				if sp > 1 then sp = 1 end
				local s = pitch.fromBaseline(far, p.y) + 0.5 * sp - 0.01 * math.abs(p.x)
				if s > bestScore + 1e-12 then bx, by, bestScore = p.x, p.y, s end
			end
		end
	end
	if not bx then return nil end
	return { x = bx, y = by, standing = true, angle = 0 }
end

tw.raising = raising
core/rect:
-- Oriented rectangles on the ground plane, for footprints and obstruction.
-- Pure Lua: no playdate.*. A rect is { x, y, a, hl, hw }: center, angle of the
-- long axis (radians from +x), half-length along that axis, half-width across.
-- Not for per-frame paths: functions return new tables.
import "core/tw"

local cos, sin, sqrt, abs, huge = math.cos, math.sin, math.sqrt, math.abs, math.huge

local rect = {}

-- Overlap closer than this counts as touching, not overlapping.
rect.eps = 1e-6

function rect.new(x, y, a, hl, hw)
	return { x = x, y = y, a = a or 0, hl = hl, hw = hw }
end

function rect.corners(r)
	local c, s = cos(r.a), sin(r.a)
	local ux, uy = c * r.hl, s * r.hl
	local vx, vy = -s * r.hw, c * r.hw
	return {
		{ r.x + ux + vx, r.y + uy + vy },
		{ r.x - ux + vx, r.y - uy + vy },
		{ r.x - ux - vx, r.y - uy - vy },
		{ r.x + ux - vx, r.y + uy - vy },
	}
end

-- Projection half-extent of rect r on unit axis (ax, ay).
local function extent(r, ax, ay)
	local c, s = cos(r.a), sin(r.a)
	return r.hl * abs(c * ax + s * ay) + r.hw * abs(-s * ax + c * ay)
end

-- Separating-axis test. True when the rects overlap by more than eps.
function rect.overlap(p, q)
	local dx, dy = q.x - p.x, q.y - p.y
	for _, r in ipairs { p, q } do
		local c, s = cos(r.a), sin(r.a)
		for _, ax in ipairs { { c, s }, { -s, c } } do
			local d = abs(dx * ax[1] + dy * ax[2])
			if d >= extent(p, ax[1], ax[2]) + extent(q, ax[1], ax[2]) - rect.eps then
				return false
			end
		end
	end
	return true
end

-- Distance from a point to a rect (0 inside).
function rect.pointDistance(r, px, py)
	local c, s = cos(r.a), sin(r.a)
	local dx, dy = px - r.x, py - r.y
	local u = dx * c + dy * s
	local v = -dx * s + dy * c
	local eu = abs(u) - r.hl
	local ev = abs(v) - r.hw
	if eu < 0 then eu = 0 end
	if ev < 0 then ev = 0 end
	return sqrt(eu * eu + ev * ev)
end

-- Smallest distance between two rects (0 when they overlap or touch). For
-- two disjoint convex polygons a closest pair always includes a vertex.
function rect.distance(p, q)
	if rect.overlap(p, q) then return 0 end
	local best = huge
	for _, pair in ipairs { { p, q }, { q, p } } do
		for _, v in ipairs(rect.corners(pair[1])) do
			local d = rect.pointDistance(pair[2], v[1], v[2])
			if d < best then best = d end
		end
	end
	return best
end

tw.rect = rect
core/roster:
-- Saved players (docs/PLAYERS.md section 2): who plays on this Playdate,
-- each with a name, a throw level and all-time totals. Pure Lua: no
-- playdate.*; source/players.lua reads and writes it (datastore "players").
-- Each player's recent games, drill records and level changes are their own
-- file (core/history).
--
-- A roster is plain data (playdate.datastore writes JSON):
--   { v = 1, nextKey = n, players = { record, ... } }
-- and a record:
--   { key = "p7"      permanent, never reused (history and saves point at it)
--     name = "Kim"    as typed (core/names rules: letters, spaces, - and ')
--     id = "kim"      notation.baseId(name): the game file id, unique here
--     level = "club"  the throw level (tw.plan.LEVELS)
--     made, last      "YYYY-MM-DD": added, last played (match or drill)
--     totals = { games, wins, resigned, batons, hits, field, base, kings,
--                kingMisses, illegal, I, R, P, Q } }
--
-- Names are unique by id, not only by spelling ("Jo" and "jo-" are both
-- jo), so a player's id is the same in every game file and two saved
-- players never share one in a game.
import "core/tw"
import "core/names"
import "core/notation"
import "core/throwplan"

local cnames, notation, plan = tw.names, tw.notation, tw.plan

local roster = {}

roster.version = 1

roster.tune = {
	max = 40,          -- saved players at most (Jamie, 2026-11-15)
}

roster.TOTALS = { "games", "wins", "resigned", "batons", "hits", "field", "base", "kings", "kingMisses",
	"illegal", "I", "R", "P", "Q" }

local function blankTotals()
	local t = {}
	for _, k in ipairs(roster.TOTALS) do t[k] = 0 end
	return t
end
roster.blankTotals = blankTotals

function roster.new()
	return { v = roster.version, nextKey = 1, players = {} }
end

-- The default throw level, and whether `l` is one.
function roster.defaultLevel() return plan.tune.defaultLevel end
function roster.isLevel(l)
	for _, x in ipairs(plan.LEVELS) do
		if x == l then return true end
	end
	return false
end

local function isDate(s) return type(s) == "string" and s:match("^%d%d%d%d%-%d%d%-%d%d$") ~= nil end

-- A roster read back from the datastore, cleaned: a record without a name
-- that keeps a letter, a second record with a taken id or key, or records
-- past the cap are dropped; a bad level is the default, missing totals are
-- zero. Anything that is not a roster gives an empty one (never an error:
-- this runs at launch).
function roster.valid(d)
	local r = roster.new()
	if type(d) ~= "table" or type(d.players) ~= "table" then return r end
	local ids, keys, top = {}, {}, 0
	for _, p in ipairs(d.players) do
		if #r.players >= roster.tune.max then break end
		local name = type(p) == "table" and type(p.name) == "string" and cnames.finish(p.name) or nil
		local key = type(p) == "table" and p.key
		local n = type(key) == "string" and tonumber(key:match("^p(%d+)$")) or nil
		if name and n then
			local id = notation.baseId(name)
			if not ids[id] and not keys[key] then
				ids[id], keys[key] = true, true
				if n > top then top = n end
				local totals = blankTotals()
				if type(p.totals) == "table" then
					for _, k in ipairs(roster.TOTALS) do
						local v = p.totals[k]
						if type(v) == "number" and v >= 0 then totals[k] = math.floor(v) end
					end
				end
				r.players[#r.players + 1] = {
					key = key, name = name, id = id,
					level = roster.isLevel(p.level) and p.level or roster.defaultLevel(),
					made = isDate(p.made) and p.made or nil, last = isDate(p.last) and p.last or nil,
					totals = totals,
				}
			end
		end
	end
	local nk = type(d.nextKey) == "number" and math.floor(d.nextKey) or 1
	r.nextKey = nk > top and nk or top + 1
	return r
end

function roster.find(r, key)
	for i, p in ipairs(r.players) do
		if p.key == key then return p, i end
	end
	return nil
end

function roster.byId(r, id)
	for _, p in ipairs(r.players) do
		if p.id == id then return p end
	end
	return nil
end

-- Whether `name` (as typed) can be a player's name, the player with key
-- `except` aside (a rename). Returns the finished name, or nil and why:
-- "empty" (no letter), "taken" (another player has its id), "full".
function roster.canName(r, name, except)
	local n = cnames.finish(name or "")
	if not n then return nil, "empty" end
	local other = roster.byId(r, notation.baseId(n))
	if other and other.key ~= except then return nil, "taken" end
	if not except and #r.players >= roster.tune.max then return nil, "full" end
	return n
end

-- Add a player; returns the record, or nil and why (roster.canName).
function roster.add(r, name, level, today)
	local n, why = roster.canName(r, name)
	if not n then return nil, why end
	local p = { key = "p" .. r.nextKey, name = n, id = notation.baseId(n),
		level = roster.isLevel(level) and level or roster.defaultLevel(),
		made = today, last = nil, totals = blankTotals() }
	r.nextKey = r.nextKey + 1
	r.players[#r.players + 1] = p
	return p
end

-- Rename; returns ok, why.
function roster.rename(r, key, name)
	local p = roster.find(r, key)
	if not p then return false, "gone" end
	local n, why = roster.canName(r, name, key)
	if not n then return false, why end
	p.name, p.id = n, notation.baseId(n)
	return true
end

-- Set the level; returns the level it had (nil when nothing changed).
function roster.setLevel(r, key, level)
	local p = roster.find(r, key)
	if not p or not roster.isLevel(level) or p.level == level then return nil end
	local was = p.level
	p.level = level
	return was
end

function roster.remove(r, key)
	local _, i = roster.find(r, key)
	if not i then return false end
	table.remove(r.players, i)
	return true
end

-- The players most recently played first (never played last, newest made
-- first among them), then by name. A new list.
function roster.sorted(r)
	local out = {}
	for i, p in ipairs(r.players) do out[i] = p end
	table.sort(out, function(a, b)
		local la, lb = a.last or "", b.last or ""
		if la ~= lb then return la > lb end
		local ma, mb = a.made or "", b.made or ""
		if ma ~= mb then return ma > mb end
		return a.name < b.name
	end)
	return out
end

-- Hit rate in whole percent, or nil before any baton.
function roster.hitRate(p)
	local t = p.totals
	if not t or t.batons == 0 then return nil end
	return math.floor(100 * t.hits / t.batons + 0.5)
end

-- The first launch with saved players: the names typed for matches before
-- (datastore "names": { match = { A, B }, vs = { A } }) become players at
-- the default level, the defaults ("Team A", "Team B", "You") aside, unless
-- one with that id exists. Returns the players added, in order.
function roster.migrateNames(r, names, today)
	local added = {}
	if type(names) ~= "table" then return added end
	local skip = { [cnames.defaults.A] = true, [cnames.defaults.B] = true, [cnames.defaults.you] = true }
	for _, mode in ipairs { "match", "vs" } do
		local m = names[mode]
		if type(m) == "table" then
			for _, side in ipairs { "A", "B" } do
				local n = m[side]
				if type(n) == "string" and not skip[n] then
					local p = roster.add(r, n, nil, today)
					if p then added[#added + 1] = p end
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return added
end

tw.roster = roster
core/rules:
-- The turn engine: U.S. National Kubb Championship Rules V4.0 as a pure state
-- machine (DESIGN.md section 6). Pure Lua: no playdate.*.
--
-- The engine knows nothing about physics. It says what is needed next
-- (game:need()) and consumes resolved throws (THROW OUTCOMES, documented in
-- docs/notes/rules-engine.md "Rules engine") and the defender's choices. Everything it does
-- is written to game.sheet (tw.notation) as it happens.
--
--   local g = tw.rules.new{ teams = { A = { name = "Jamie", players = { { name = "Jamie" } } },
--                                     B = { name = "Playdate", players = { { name = "Club" } } } },
--                           surface = "Grass", opening = "2-4-6", first = "A" }
--   local n = g:need()   -- { kind = "toss" | "raise" | "punish" | "baton" | "over", ... }
--   g:toss(outcome) / g:raise(choice) / g:placePunishment(pose) / g:throwBaton(outcome)
--   g:resign(side)
--
-- Kubbs have permanent ids "a1".."a5" (Team A's base kubbs, x = -2..2 on
-- y = 0) and "b1".."b5" (y = 8). The king is "king".
import "core/tw"
import "core/pitch"
import "core/raising"
import "core/notation"

local pitch, raising, notation = tw.pitch, tw.raising, tw.notation
local other = pitch.other
local sort = table.sort

local rules = {}

local Game = {}
Game.__index = Game
rules.Game = Game        -- (core/save restores a saved game with it)
rules.Game = Game

local function fail(msg) error("rules: " .. msg, 3) end

local function copyPose(p) return raising.copyPose(p) end

-- Batons for a turn: 2-4-6 opening (II.A) or six from the start.
function rules.batonsFor(opening, turn)
	if opening ~= "six" then
		if turn == 1 then return 2 end
		if turn == 2 then return 4 end
	end
	return 6
end

function rules.new(opts)
	opts = opts or {}
	local g = setmetatable({}, Game)
	g.teams = {}
	for _, side in ipairs { "A", "B" } do
		local t = (opts.teams or {})[side] or {}
		local players = {}
		for i, p in ipairs(t.players or { { name = t.name or ("Team " .. side) } }) do
			if type(p) == "string" then p = { name = p } end
			players[i] = { name = p.name, id = p.id }
		end
		g.teams[side] = { name = t.name or ("Team " .. side), players = players }
	end
	notation.assignIds(g.teams)
	g.surface = opts.surface or "Grass"
	g.opening = opts.opening == "six" and "six" or "2-4-6"
	g.first = opts.first == "B" and "B" or "A"
	g.raisePolicy = opts.raisePolicy or "apart"
	g.kubbs, g.ids = {}, {}
	for _, side in ipairs { "A", "B" } do
		for i, x in ipairs(pitch.baseX) do
			local id = side:lower() .. i
			g.kubbs[id] = {
				id = id, kind = "base", half = side, where = "pitch",
				pose = { x = x, y = pitch.baseline[side], standing = true, angle = 0 },
				thrown = 0, established = false,
			}
			g.ids[#g.ids + 1] = id
		end
	end
	g.king = { id = "king", pose = { x = pitch.king.x, y = pitch.king.y, standing = true, angle = 0 } }
	g.hand = { A = {}, B = {} }
	g.sheet = notation.sheet()
	g.turn = 0
	g.winner, g.how = nil, nil
	g:_startTurn()
	return g
end

-- ---------- queries ----------

function Game:player(side, p)
	local ps = self.teams[side].players
	if p == nil then return ps[1].id end
	for _, q in ipairs(ps) do
		if q.id == p or q.name == p then return q.id end
	end
	fail("no player " .. tostring(p) .. " on Team " .. side)
end

-- Kubbs on the pitch, in id order, optionally filtered.
function Game:onPitch(filter)
	local out = {}
	for _, id in ipairs(self.ids) do
		local k = self.kubbs[id]
		if k.where == "pitch" and (not filter or filter(k)) then out[#out + 1] = k end
	end
	return out
end

-- Standing field kubbs in `side`'s half.
function Game:fieldKubbs(side)
	return self:onPitch(function(k) return k.kind == "field" and k.half == side end)
end

function Game:baseKubbs(side)
	return self:onPitch(function(k) return k.kind == "base" and k.half == side end)
end

-- Every kubb of `side`'s half is down: what a king shot needs.
function Game:allDown(side)
	return #self:fieldKubbs(side) == 0 and #self:baseKubbs(side) == 0
end

-- Context for raising/punishment geometry in `half`, without kubb `except`.
function Game:context(half, except)
	local others = {}
	for _, k in ipairs(self:onPitch()) do
		if k.id ~= except then others[#others + 1] = { id = k.id, pose = k.pose } end
	end
	return { half = half, king = self.king.pose, others = others }
end

-- Where kubbs are: counts by `where` (pitch, hand, out, punish). Ten always.
function Game:census()
	local c = { pitch = 0, hand = 0, out = 0, punish = 0, total = 0 }
	for _, id in ipairs(self.ids) do
		local w = self.kubbs[id].where
		c[w] = (c[w] or 0) + 1
		c.total = c.total + 1
	end
	return c
end

-- What the engine needs next.
function Game:need()
	local ph = self.phase
	if ph == "over" then
		return { kind = "over", winner = self.winner, how = self.how }
	elseif ph == "toss" or ph == "rethrow" then
		return { kind = "toss", side = self.attacker, kubb = self.current, rethrow = ph == "rethrow",
			throwY = pitch.baseline[self.attacker], half = self.defender,
			left = #self.firstQueue + #self.rethrowQueue }
	elseif ph == "raise" then
		local k = self.kubbs[self.current]
		local ctx = self:context(self.defender, k.id)
		return { kind = "raise", side = self.defender, kubb = k.id, pose = copyPose(k.pose),
			decision = raising.options(k.pose, ctx) }
	elseif ph == "punish" then
		return { kind = "punish", side = self.defender, kubb = self.current, half = self.defender }
	elseif ph == "batons" then
		local def = self.defender
		local kingShot = self:allDown(def)
		local targets = {}
		if kingShot then
			targets = { "king" }
		else
			local f = self:fieldKubbs(def)
			if #f == 0 then f = self:baseKubbs(def) end
			for _, k in ipairs(f) do targets[#targets + 1] = k.id end
		end
		local throwY = pitch.baseline[self.attacker]
		if self.advantageY and not kingShot then throwY = self.advantageY end
		return { kind = "baton", side = self.attacker, n = self.batonIndex + 1, of = self.batonsTotal,
			left = self.batonsLeft, kingShot = kingShot, throwY = throwY,
			advantageY = self.advantageY, targets = targets }
	end
end

-- ---------- turn flow ----------

function Game:_startTurn()
	self.turn = self.turn + 1
	local att = (self.turn % 2 == 1) and self.first or other(self.first)
	local def = other(att)
	self.attacker, self.defender = att, def
	self.batonsTotal = rules.batonsFor(self.opening, self.turn)
	self.batonsLeft, self.batonIndex = self.batonsTotal, 0
	-- Every field kubb standing now is established (left from an earlier turn).
	for _, k in ipairs(self:onPitch()) do
		k.thrown = 0
		if k.kind == "field" then k.established = true end
	end
	local q = self.hand[att]
	sort(q)
	for _, id in ipairs(q) do
		local k = self.kubbs[id]
		k.thrown, k.established, k.kind = 0, false, "field"
	end
	self.firstQueue, self.rethrowQueue, self.punishQueue = q, {}, {}
	self.hand[att] = {}
	self.firstThrows = 0
	self.roundThrows = 0          -- kubbs thrown in the round not yet judged
	self.judgment = nil           -- what the last judgment did (set by _judge)
	self.lastTosser = nil
	self.tossSeq = 0
	self.sheet:beginTurn(self.turn, att)
	-- II.B.2: the opponent left field kubbs standing in the attacker's own
	-- half; the line runs through the center of the one closest to the
	-- centerline. The inkast cannot legally move them (II.C.4b puts them
	-- back), so it is fixed for the turn.
	self:_advantage()
	self.phase = "toss"
	self:_next()
end

-- The advantage line from the attacker's own field kubbs as they stand now,
-- written to the sheet. _startTurn sets it; core/match calls it again when it
-- settles a carried standing kubb before the turn's first throw.
function Game:_advantage()
	local att = self.attacker
	self.advantageY = nil
	self.sheet:advantage(nil)
	local own = self:fieldKubbs(att)
	if #own > 0 then
		local best
		for _, k in ipairs(own) do
			if not best or pitch.fromBaseline(att, k.pose.y) > pitch.fromBaseline(att, best.pose.y) then best = k end
		end
		self.advantageY = best.pose.y
		self.sheet:advantage(pitch.advantageMeters(att, best.pose.y))
	end
end

-- Pick the phase and current piece from the queues.
function Game:_next()
	if self.phase == "over" then return end
	if self.phase == "toss" or self.phase == "rethrow" then
		if #self.firstQueue > 0 then
			self.phase, self.current = "toss", self.firstQueue[1]
			return
		elseif #self.rethrowQueue > 0 then
			self.phase, self.current = "rethrow", self.rethrowQueue[1]
			return
		end
		self.phase = "raise"
	end
	if self.phase == "raise" then
		for _, k in ipairs(self:fieldKubbs(self.defender)) do
			if not k.pose.standing then
				self.current = k.id
				return
			end
		end
		self.phase = "punish"
	end
	if self.phase == "punish" then
		if #self.punishQueue > 0 then
			self.current = self.punishQueue[1]
			return
		end
		self.phase, self.current = "batons", nil
		self:_inkastPositions()
	end
end

-- Positions for the inkast tokens (written once, as the batons begin: every
-- kubb thrown this turn is raised or placed by then). Each kubb a player
-- threw this turn that is on the pitch now, where it stands, in the order
-- of its last throw, on the token of the player who made that throw; a
-- punishment kubb on the token that counts its P (core/notation caps them
-- at the token's count). Kubbs out of play have none. A turn saved before
-- positions has no inkBy on its kubbs: they go to its one inkaster, or
-- nowhere when it had several.
-- Written as the batons begin; core/match calls it again (it starts the list
-- afresh) when it settles the turn's kubbs before the first baton.
function Game:_inkastPositions()
	local t = self.sheet.current
	if not t then return end
	t.inkastAt = nil
	if #t.inkastOrder == 0 then return end
	local def = self.defender
	local list = {}
	for _, id in ipairs(self.ids) do
		local k = self.kubbs[id]
		if k.where == "pitch" and k.kind == "field" and k.half == def and (k.thrown or 0) > 0 then
			list[#list + 1] = k
		end
	end
	sort(list, function(a, b)
		local sa, sb = a.tossSeq or 0, b.tossSeq or 0
		if sa ~= sb then return sa < sb end
		return a.id < b.id
	end)
	local only = #t.inkastOrder == 1 and t.inkastOrder[1] or nil
	for _, k in ipairs(list) do
		local pid = k.inkBy or only
		if pid and t.inkast[pid] then self.sheet:inkAt(pid, k.pose.x, k.pose.y) end
	end
end

local function removeFrom(list, id)
	for i, v in ipairs(list) do
		if v == id then table.remove(list, i) return true end
	end
	return false
end

-- Game over: the rest of this turn's batons are X.
function Game:_finish(winner, how)
	if self.winner then fail("winner already set") end
	self.winner, self.how = winner, how
	self.phase, self.current = "over", nil
	for _ = 1, self.batonsLeft do self.sheet:baton(nil, "X") end
	self.batonsLeft = 0
end

-- When a game ends before the inkast is done (king toppled by a kubb, or a
-- resign), the inkast token still counts every kubb that was to be thrown,
-- so it says how many kubbs the turn had (kubb.js checks I against the
-- kubbs knocked down last turn). Returns how many were added.
function Game:_completeInkast(pid)
	local pending = #self.firstQueue
	if pending > 0 then self.sheet:ink(pid, "I", pending) end
	return pending
end

-- ---------- kubb tossing (II.C) ----------

local function poseFrom(o, fallback)
	if not o then return copyPose(fallback) end
	return { x = o.x, y = o.y, standing = o.standing and true or false, angle = o.angle or 0, onTop = o.onTop }
end

-- The kubb throwing is judged at the final position (Jamie, 2026-11-13):
-- whether a thrown kubb is in or out is not decided when it stops. Every
-- thrown kubb stays a piece on the pitch at its rest pose (in, out of
-- bounds, short of the middle line, in the thrower's own half) and later
-- kubbs may move it. A round is every kubb queued when it starts (first
-- throws before rethrows, II.C.6); when its last throw has come to rest,
-- _judge rules on every field kubb of the target half by where it lies
-- then.

-- Out for now: a fouled kubb (II.C.4b), or one that cannot be raised in
-- bounds where it lies.
function Game:_outNow(k)
	return k.fouled and true or not raising.canRaise(k.pose, self.defender)
end

-- Where a kubb thrown this turn lies before the round is judged: "in" or
-- "out" (what the judgment would say if the round ended now, before any
-- lowering), or nil when it is not on the pitch.
function Game:liesNow(id)
	local k = self.kubbs[id]
	if not k or k.where ~= "pitch" then return nil end
	return self:_outNow(k) and "out" or "in"
end

-- Lower a kubb resting on another (II.D.6) and count N.
function Game:_settle(k, pid)
	if k.pose.onTop then
		local lower = self.kubbs[k.pose.onTop]
		local lp = lower and lower.pose or self.king.pose
		k.pose = raising.lower(k.pose, lp)
		self.sheet:ink(pid, "N")
		return true
	end
	return false
end

-- The judgment at the end of a round, on every field kubb of the target
-- half as it lies now (II.C.4, II.C.5a/b/c, II.C.6, II.D.6, II.D.11):
--   * a kubb resting on another is lowered beside it (N), unless the kubb
--     under it is itself out (it is lifted away: the upper one lies where
--     it is, no N);
--   * an established field kubb that cannot be raised in bounds is rescued
--     (Q): back to the attacker as a kubb not yet thrown this turn;
--   * a kubb thrown once that cannot be raised in bounds (or that fouled,
--     II.C.4b) is picked up and rethrown in the next round;
--   * a kubb thrown twice that is still out is a punishment kubb (P).
-- Sets self.judgment = { thrown, rethrow, punish, rescue, lowered, lifted }
-- (lifted: ids of kubbs whose support was picked up).
function Game:_judge(pid)
	local def = self.defender
	local cands = self:onPitch(function(k) return k.kind == "field" and k.half == def end)
	local isCand = {}
	for _, k in ipairs(cands) do isCand[k.id] = true end
	local status, pending = {}, {}
	for _, k in ipairs(cands) do
		if k.pose.onTop then pending[#pending + 1] = k
		else status[k.id] = self:_outNow(k) and "out" or "in" end
	end
	local j = { thrown = self.roundThrows, rethrow = 0, punish = 0, rescue = 0, lowered = 0, lifted = {} }
	-- kubbs resting on another, each once the kubb under it is judged (a
	-- support whose own support is never judged counts as in)
	while #pending > 0 do
		local rest, progress = {}, false
		for _, k in ipairs(pending) do
			local sid = k.pose.onTop
			local sup = "in"
			if isCand[sid] then sup = status[sid] end
			if sup == nil then
				rest[#rest + 1] = k
			else
				progress = true
				if sup == "out" then
					k.pose.onTop, k.pose.standing = nil, false
					j.lifted[#j.lifted + 1] = k.id
				elseif self:_settle(k, pid) then
					j.lowered = j.lowered + 1
				end
				status[k.id] = self:_outNow(k) and "out" or "in"
			end
		end
		if not progress then
			-- a ring of kubbs on each other (cannot happen in practice)
			for _, k in ipairs(rest) do
				if self:_settle(k, pid) then j.lowered = j.lowered + 1 end
				status[k.id] = self:_outNow(k) and "out" or "in"
			end
			rest = {}
		end
		pending = rest
	end
	for _, k in ipairs(cands) do
		if status[k.id] == "out" then
			if k.established then
				-- II.C.5a, the rescue
				k.established, k.thrown, k.where = false, 0, "hand"
				self.firstQueue[#self.firstQueue + 1] = k.id
				self.sheet:ink(pid, "Q")
				j.rescue = j.rescue + 1
			elseif k.thrown <= 1 then
				k.where = "out"
				self.rethrowQueue[#self.rethrowQueue + 1] = k.id
				j.rethrow = j.rethrow + 1
			else
				k.where = "punish"
				k.inkBy = pid          -- its position goes on the token that counts its P
				self.punishQueue[#self.punishQueue + 1] = k.id
				self.sheet:ink(pid, "P")
				j.punish = j.punish + 1
			end
		end
		k.fouled = nil
	end
	self.roundThrows = 0
	self.judgment = j
end

-- outcome: see docs/notes/rules-engine.md "Kubb-toss outcome".
function Game:toss(o, player)
	if self.phase ~= "toss" and self.phase ~= "rethrow" then fail("not tossing now (" .. self.phase .. ")") end
	o = o or {}
	local att, def = self.attacker, self.defender
	local pid = self:player(att, player)
	local k = self.kubbs[self.current]
	removeFrom(self.firstQueue, k.id)
	removeFrom(self.rethrowQueue, k.id)
	self.judgment = nil
	k.thrown = k.thrown + 1
	if k.thrown == 1 then
		self.sheet:ink(pid, "I")
		self.firstThrows = self.firstThrows + 1
	else
		self.sheet:ink(pid, "R")
	end
	self.lastTosser = pid
	self.roundThrows = self.roundThrows + 1
	-- who threw it last, and when (for the inkast positions)
	self.tossSeq = (self.tossSeq or 0) + 1
	k.inkBy, k.tossSeq = pid, self.tossSeq

	if o.kingToppled then
		k.where, k.kind, k.half = "pitch", "field", def
		k.pose = poseFrom(o.rest, k.pose)
		self:_completeInkast(pid)
		self.sheet:ink(pid, "E")
		self.sheet:note("king toppled by a thrown kubb")
		self:_finish(def, "king toppled by a thrown kubb")
		return
	end

	-- Other pieces it moved. Base kubbs are stood back where they were; a
	-- piece in the thrower's own half makes it II.C.4b. Kubbs thrown this
	-- turn are field kubbs of the target half wherever they lie, so moving
	-- one is never II.C.4b.
	local ownHit = false
	for _, id in ipairs(o.ownHalfHit or {}) do
		local p = self.kubbs[id]
		if p and p.where == "pitch" and p.half == att then ownHit = true end
	end
	local struck = {}
	for id, pose in pairs(o.moved or {}) do
		if id == "king" then
			self.king.pose = poseFrom(pose, self.king.pose)
			self.king.pose.standing = true
		else
			local p = self.kubbs[id]
			if not p then fail("unknown piece " .. tostring(id)) end
			if p.where == "pitch" and p.id ~= k.id then
				if p.half == att then
					ownHit = true
				elseif p.kind == "field" then
					struck[#struck + 1] = { p = p, pose = poseFrom(pose, p.pose) }
				end
			end
		end
	end

	-- Kubbs it struck lie where the throw left them (II.C.4); nothing is
	-- judged until the round is over. When the toss is II.C.4b nothing in
	-- the own half was applied (put back); kubbs it moved in the target half
	-- still stay where they came to rest.
	sort(struck, function(a, b) return a.p.id < b.p.id end)
	for _, s in ipairs(struck) do s.p.pose = s.pose end

	-- The thrown kubb lies where it stopped, a field kubb of the target half
	-- (in or out), until the round is judged.
	k.kind, k.half, k.established = "field", def, false
	k.pose = poseFrom(o.rest, k.pose)
	k.where = "pitch"
	if ownHit then
		-- II.C.4b at the final position: a kubb that touched a field kubb in
		-- the thrower's own half is out whatever later kubbs do to it
		k.fouled = true
		k.pose.onTop = nil
		self.sheet:note("a kubb hit a field kubb in the thrower's own half (II.C.4b)")
	end

	if #self.firstQueue == 0 and #self.rethrowQueue == 0 then self:_judge(pid) end
	self:_next()
end

-- ---------- raising (II.D) ----------

-- choice: an index into need().decision.choices, or nil for the automatic
-- chooser (game.raisePolicy, or `policy`).
function Game:raise(choice, policy)
	if self.phase ~= "raise" then fail("not raising now (" .. self.phase .. ")") end
	local k = self.kubbs[self.current]
	local ctx = self:context(self.defender, k.id)
	local dec = raising.options(k.pose, ctx)
	if #dec.choices == 0 then fail("kubb " .. k.id .. " cannot be raised in bounds") end
	if choice == nil then choice = raising.choose(dec, ctx, policy or self.raisePolicy) end
	local c = dec.choices[choice]
	if not c then fail("no raising choice " .. tostring(choice)) end
	k.pose = copyPose(c.pose)
	k.pose.standing, k.pose.onTop = true, nil
	self:_next()
	return c
end

-- Raise every pending kubb automatically.
function Game:raiseAll(policy)
	while self.phase == "raise" do self:raise(nil, policy) end
end

-- ---------- punishment kubbs (II.D.11) ----------

function Game:placePunishment(pose)
	if self.phase ~= "punish" then fail("no punishment kubb to place (" .. self.phase .. ")") end
	local k = self.kubbs[self.current]
	local p = { x = pose.x, y = pose.y, standing = true, angle = pose.angle or 0 }
	local ok, why = raising.punishmentCheck(p, self:context(self.defender, k.id))
	if not ok then return false, why end
	removeFrom(self.punishQueue, k.id)
	k.pose, k.where, k.kind, k.half = p, "pitch", "field", self.defender
	self:_next()
	return true
end

function Game:autoPunishment(policy)
	local k = self.kubbs[self.current]
	local pose = raising.autoPunishment(self:context(self.defender, k.id), policy)
	if not pose then fail("no valid punishment spot") end
	return self:placePunishment(pose)
end

-- ---------- batons (II.B) ----------

local function set(list)
	local s = {}
	for _, v in ipairs(list or {}) do s[v] = true end
	return s
end

-- outcome: see docs/notes/rules-engine.md "Baton outcome".
function Game:throwBaton(o, player)
	if self.phase ~= "batons" then fail("not throwing batons now (" .. tostring(self.phase) .. ")") end
	o = o or {}
	local att, def = self.attacker, self.defender
	local pid = self:player(att, player)
	local n = self.batonIndex + 1
	self.batonIndex, self.batonsLeft = n, self.batonsLeft - 1
	local kingShot = self:allDown(def)
	local toppled = set(o.toppled)
	local kingDown = o.kingToppled or toppled.king
	toppled.king = nil
	for id in pairs(toppled) do
		local k = self.kubbs[id]
		if not k then fail("unknown piece " .. tostring(id)) end
		if k.where ~= "pitch" then fail("piece " .. id .. " is not on the pitch") end
	end

	local function earlyKing(token, why, at)
		self.sheet:baton(pid, token, at)
		self.sheet:note("b" .. n .. " " .. why)
		self:_finish(def, "king toppled early")
	end

	-- II.B.1: an illegal throw (helicopter). Everything is put back and the
	-- baton is forfeited. Interpretation: a king it topples before every
	-- kubb is down still loses the game; on a king shot it is stood up.
	if o.illegal then
		if kingDown and not kingShot then
			return earlyKing("E", "illegal throw toppled the king early")
		end
		self.sheet:baton(pid, "Z")
		return self:_afterBaton()
	end

	-- II.B.11: field kubbs in the attacker's own half hit by its baton.
	local own = false
	for _, id in ipairs(o.ownHalfHit or {}) do
		local k = self.kubbs[id]
		if k and k.where == "pitch" and k.kind == "field" and k.half == att then own = true end
	end
	for id in pairs(toppled) do
		local k = self.kubbs[id]
		if k.kind == "field" and k.half == att then own = true end
	end
	for id in pairs(o.moved or {}) do
		local k = self.kubbs[id]
		if k and k.where == "pitch" and k.kind == "field" and k.half == att then own = true end
	end
	if own then
		if kingDown and not kingShot then
			return earlyKing("E", "baton hit its own half and toppled the king early")
		end
		self.sheet:baton(pid, "Z")
		self.sheet:note("b" .. n .. " hit a field kubb in the thrower's own half; all put back (II.B.11)")
		return self:_afterBaton()
	end

	-- A legal throw.
	local standingAfter = 0
	for _, k in ipairs(self:fieldKubbs(def)) do
		if not toppled[k.id] then standingAfter = standingAfter + 1 end
	end
	local f, b, early = 0, 0, 0
	local fAt, bAt = {}, {}   -- where the kubbs the token counts stood before the throw
	local ids = {}
	for id in pairs(toppled) do ids[#ids + 1] = id end
	sort(ids)
	for _, id in ipairs(ids) do
		local k = self.kubbs[id]
		if k.half == def and k.kind == "field" then
			f = f + 1
			fAt[#fAt + 1] = { x = k.pose.x, y = k.pose.y }
			k.where = "hand"
			self.hand[def][#self.hand[def] + 1] = id
		elseif k.half == def and k.kind == "base" then
			if standingAfter > 0 then
				early = early + 1   -- II.B.4a: raised where it was, still a base kubb
			else
				b = b + 1
				bAt[#bAt + 1] = { x = k.pose.x, y = k.pose.y }
				k.where = "hand"
				self.hand[def][#self.hand[def] + 1] = id
			end
		end
		-- An attacker's own base kubb toppled: stood back up (nothing applied).
	end
	-- Pieces moved without toppling stay where they came to rest, unless
	-- pushed out of bounds (II.B.7: returned to where they were).
	local pushedOut = 0
	for id, pose in pairs(o.moved or {}) do
		if not toppled[id] then
			local piece = id == "king" and self.king or self.kubbs[id]
			if piece and (id == "king" or piece.where == "pitch") and not (id == "king" and kingDown) then
				if pitch.onPitch(pose.x, pose.y) then
					piece.pose = { x = pose.x, y = pose.y, standing = true, angle = pose.angle or piece.pose.angle or 0 }
				else
					pushedOut = pushedOut + 1
				end
			end
		end
	end
	if early > 0 then
		self.sheet:note("b" .. n .. " toppled " .. (early == 1 and "a base kubb" or (early .. " base kubbs"))
			.. " early; raised (II.B.4a)")
	end
	if pushedOut > 0 then
		self.sheet:note("b" .. n .. " pushed " .. (pushedOut == 1 and "a kubb" or (pushedOut .. " kubbs"))
			.. " out without toppling; put back (II.B.7)")
	end

	for _, p in ipairs(bAt) do fAt[#fAt + 1] = p end
	if kingShot then
		if kingDown then
			self.sheet:baton(pid, "K")
			self:_finish(att, "king")
			return
		end
		self.sheet:baton(pid, "=")
		return self:_afterBaton()
	end
	if kingDown then
		return earlyKing(notation.hitToken(f, b, true), "toppled the king early", fAt)
	end
	self.sheet:baton(pid, notation.hitToken(f, b, false), fAt)
	return self:_afterBaton()
end

function Game:_afterBaton()
	if self.phase == "over" then return end
	if self.batonsLeft <= 0 then self:_startTurn() end
end

-- ---------- resign ----------

-- Resign from the menu, on the resigning team's own turn: `G`, then X for
-- the batons left. An unfinished inkast is written in full (see
-- _completeInkast) with a note.
function Game:resign(side, player)
	if self.phase == "over" then fail("the game is over") end
	side = side or self.attacker
	if side ~= self.attacker then fail("a team resigns on its own turn") end
	local pid = self:player(side, player)
	if self.phase == "toss" or self.phase == "rethrow" then
		local tosser = self.lastTosser or pid
		local added = self:_completeInkast(tosser)
		if added > 0 or #self.rethrowQueue > 0 then self.sheet:note("resigned during the inkast") end
	end
	self.sheet:baton(pid, "G")
	self:_finish(other(side), "resigned")
end

tw.rules = rules
core/save:
-- A match in progress as plain data, and back (resume). Pure: no playdate.*.
--
-- core/match's table `m` is plain tables but for two metatables, the engine
-- game's (rules.Game) and its score sheet's (notation.Sheet), and the
-- current throw's setup, which match.setup builds again from the engine.
-- save.pack copies what a resume needs into tables of numbers, strings and
-- booleans only (as playdate.datastore writes JSON); save.unpack gives a
-- match table again with the metatables put back. A table met twice, a
-- function or a table with both list and named keys is an error: JSON could
-- not keep it.
import "core/tw"
import "core/rules"
import "core/notation"

local rules, notation = tw.rules, tw.notation

local save = {}

-- 2: teams of several players, with the throwing order and the lineup
-- (docs/PLAYERS.md); a version 1 save is not resumed (Jamie, 2026-11-15)
save.version = 2

local function plain(v, seen, path)
	local t = type(v)
	if t == "number" or t == "string" or t == "boolean" or t == "nil" then return v end
	if t ~= "table" then error("save: a " .. t .. " at " .. path) end
	if seen[v] then error("save: a table met twice at " .. path) end
	seen[v] = true
	local n, keys = #v, 0
	for _ in pairs(v) do keys = keys + 1 end
	local out = {}
	if n > 0 then
		if keys ~= n then error("save: a list with named keys at " .. path) end
		for i = 1, n do out[i] = plain(v[i], seen, path .. "[" .. i .. "]") end
	else
		for k, x in pairs(v) do
			if type(k) ~= "string" then error("save: a " .. type(k) .. " key at " .. path) end
			out[k] = plain(x, seen, path .. "." .. k)
		end
	end
	return out
end
save.plain = function(v) return plain(v, {}, "") end

-- Hands writer(d) what a resume needs of match `m`, plus `opts` (the match
-- scene's options: names, teams, vs, autoSettle, set, wind; the surface and opening are the
-- engine's own): the live tables, not a copy (copying the game
-- cost 43 ms on the device at turn 4), so writer must write it at once
-- (playdate.datastore.write). The score sheet's current turn is also its
-- last entry in turns, the one table the engine reaches two ways: it is
-- detached for the write and kept as an index.
function save.write(m, opts, writer)
	local sheet = m.game.sheet
	local cur, ci = sheet and sheet.current, nil
	if cur then
		for i, t in ipairs(sheet.turns) do if t == cur then ci = i end end
		sheet.current = nil
	end
	local ok, err = pcall(writer, {
		v = save.version, currentIndex = ci,
		game = m.game, start = m.start, mode = m.mode, turn = m.turn, tossed = m.tossed,
		text = m.text, debris = m.debris, order = m.order, lineup = m.lineup,
		opts = { vs = opts and opts.vs, names = opts and opts.names, teams = opts and opts.teams,
			autoSettle = opts and opts.autoSettle or nil,   -- the match options' raising
			set = opts and opts.set or nil,                 -- kubb set
			wind = opts and opts.wind or nil },             -- and wind
	})
	if sheet then sheet.current = cur end
	if not ok then error(err, 0) end
end

-- A plain copy of what save.write would write (tests; save.plain refuses
-- anything JSON could not keep).
function save.pack(m, opts)
	local d
	save.write(m, opts, function(t) d = save.plain(t) end)
	return d
end

-- The match table again (and the options), or nil and why.
function save.unpack(d)
	if type(d) ~= "table" or d.v ~= save.version or type(d.game) ~= "table" then
		return nil, "not a saved match of this version"
	end
	local g = setmetatable(d.game, rules.Game)
	local sheet = g.sheet
	if sheet then
		setmetatable(sheet, notation.Sheet)
		local ci = d.currentIndex or sheet.currentIndex
		if ci then sheet.current = sheet.turns[ci] end
		sheet.currentIndex = nil
	end
	local m = { game = g, start = d.start, mode = d.mode, turn = d.turn, tossed = d.tossed, text = d.text,
		settled = nil, setup = nil, debris = d.debris, order = d.order, lineup = d.lineup }
	return m, d.opts or {}
end

tw.save = save
core/swing:
-- The crank swing: the crank as a clock (DESIGN.md section 4, "The throw: the
-- crank as a clock"). Pure Lua: no playdate.*.
--
-- The crank is the throwing arm. Read as a clock, 6 is the arm hanging
-- straight down; the backswing goes up the left side (7 .. 12) and the forward
-- swing up the right (5 .. 1). This module only measures the crank: how far
-- back it went, where it stopped going forward, how fast and how steadily the
-- flick was. What a throw makes of that (power, launch angle, error) is the
-- plan's (core/throwplan), not this file's.
--
-- Angles are "forward degrees from the bottom": the raw crank change times
-- tune.forwardSign, so forward is positive. On the backswing 7 o'clock is
-- -30, 9 is -90, 10 is -120, 12 is -180; forward 5 is +30, 3 is +90, 1 is
-- +150, 12 is +180.
--
-- Fed one sample per frame: swing.update(s, delta, dt), delta the crank change
-- in degrees as playdate.getCrankChange gives it (the sign is applied here),
-- dt the frame time in seconds. The throw scene feeds the crank while idle
-- only once it has crossed the bottom of the turn going back (armAngle,
-- crossedBack), and then only the part past the bottom, so the arm starts at 0.
--
--   idle      back motion moves the arm behind the bottom (s.pending; forward
--             motion takes it off again). Past startBackDeg (7 o'clock: 6 to 7
--             is a dead zone) -> winding.
--   winding   s.arm is the real crank, never capped; s.back the farthest back
--             it has been (capped at backswingMaxDeg). Forward slower than
--             swingStartDps lets the arm down: back past the bottom it is a
--             "letdown" (no throw) -> idle. Forward at swingStartDps or faster
--             -> swinging (that frame is the flick's first).
--   swinging  every frame's forward speed goes into s.speeds. The crank has
--             stopped when the forward speed (averaged over speedWindow
--             frames) falls below releaseStopDps: the throw leaves where the
--             arm got farthest forward (releaseAngle). Stopped at or short of
--             the bottom it is a "letdown"; past it, a "release" with
--             how = "stopped". An arm that passes skyDeg (12 o'clock forward)
--             before stopping is released at once, how = "sky".
--   cooldown  after a release, cooldownS of frame time in which every crank
--             change is ignored (the crank swinging back after a throw must
--             not start the next one) -> idle.
--
-- update returns nil, "letdown" or "release"; after a release s.result holds
-- what was measured (fields at release() below). s.back stays as it was until
-- the next wind-up so the dial can keep its dot.
--
-- Crank sign. getCrankChange is negative anti-clockwise. Tried on hardware
-- (2026-11-13): with forwardSign = 1 the wind-up and the throw felt swapped,
-- so the forward swing is the anti-clockwise direction: forwardSign = -1.
-- It is the one constant to flip; nothing else changes.
import "core/tw"

local abs = math.abs

local swing = {}

swing.tune = {
	forwardSign = -1,      -- -1: anti-clockwise (negative getCrankChange) is the forward swing
	startBackDeg = 30,     -- back from the bottom before the wind-up starts: 6 to 7 o'clock is a
	                       -- dead zone, crossing 7 starts the throw
	backswingMaxDeg = 200, -- s.back and result.back stop growing here (a little past 12 o'clock,
	                       -- 180); the arm itself keeps counting
	swingStartDps = 200,   -- forward speed (deg/s) that starts the flick; slower forward is the
	                       -- arm being let down
	speedWindow = 2,       -- frames averaged for "forward speed" (the stop test and the flick
	                       -- speed), so one slow sample in a jittery flick does not stop it
	releaseStopDps = 150,  -- the crank has stopped when the forward speed falls below this
	                       -- (3 degrees a 20 ms frame)
	skyDeg = 180,          -- forward degrees: an arm past 12 o'clock before stopping is a sky
	                       -- ball, released there
	cooldownS = 0.3,       -- seconds of frame time after a release in which the crank is ignored
	fullFlickDps = 1000,   -- flick speed (deg/s, the peak speedWindow average) that gives
	                       -- flickFrac 1: all the power of the backswing
	minFlickFrac = 0.2,    -- flickFrac of the slowest flick (swingStartDps and under)
	pullFrames = 2,        -- pull = +1 when the flick's fastest frame is one of its last
	                       -- pullFrames frames (still speeding up into the stop), else -1
	roughFull = 3.0,       -- roughness (mean second difference of speed / mean speed) that gives
	                       -- smoothness 0. Hardware traces (2026-11-13): a flick is only 4 to 7
	                       -- frames at about 41 ms each and honest flicks measure up to 0.67
	                       -- from sampling jitter alone, so only a clearly stuttered swing
	                       -- (roughness over 1.0) is shaky enough to be a helicopter
	maxSamples = 512,      -- flick speed samples kept (about 10 s at 50 fps); later ones dropped
}

function swing.new()
	return {
		phase = "idle",
		pending = 0,   -- idle: degrees the arm is behind the bottom, before the wind-up starts
		arm = 0,       -- forward degrees from the bottom: where the crank really is (winding, swinging)
		back = 0,      -- farthest back this wind-up (positive degrees, capped at backswingMaxDeg)
		far = 0,       -- farthest forward this flick (forward degrees)
		n = 0,         -- flick speed samples
		speeds = {},   -- deg/s per frame of the flick (reused)
		cool = 0,      -- cooldown seconds left
		result = {},   -- filled at a release (reused)
	}
end

-- Back to idle at once (no cooldown). s.back is kept for the dial; the caller
-- clears it if it wants.
function swing.reset(s)
	s.phase, s.pending, s.arm, s.far, s.n, s.cool = "idle", 0, 0, 0, 0, 0
end

-- Where the crank is, as the throwing arm: forward degrees from the bottom of
-- the turn, in (-180, 180]. `pos` is getCrankPosition (0 = straight up,
-- growing clockwise). Negative = on the wind-up side.
function swing.armAngle(pos)
	local a = ((pos - 180) * swing.tune.forwardSign) % 360
	if a > 180 then a = a - 360 end
	return a
end

-- The throw starts at the bottom of the turn: true when the arm went from
-- `prev` (at or ahead of the bottom) to `a` (behind it) in one frame. The
-- 90 degree limit keeps the jump across the top of the turn from counting.
function swing.crossedBack(prev, a)
	return prev ~= nil and prev >= 0 and a < 0 and (prev - a) < 90
end

-- Smoothness 0..1 of speeds[1..n]: one minus the mean absolute second
-- difference relative to the mean speed. A flick that speeds up evenly has
-- small second differences; alternating fast and slow frames have large ones.
-- With fewer than three samples there is no evidence of jerk: 1.
function swing.smoothness(speeds, n)
	if n < 3 then return 1 end
	local sum = 0
	for i = 1, n do sum = sum + speeds[i] end
	local mean = sum / n
	if mean <= 0 then return 0 end
	local r = 0
	for i = 2, n - 1 do
		r = r + abs(speeds[i] - 0.5 * (speeds[i - 1] + speeds[i + 1]))
	end
	r = r / (n - 2) / mean
	r = 1 - r / swing.tune.roughFull
	if r < 0 then return 0 end
	if r > 1 then return 1 end
	return r
end

-- The forward speed: the mean of speeds over the speedWindow frames ending at `upto`.
local function windowSpeed(speeds, upto)
	local lo = upto - swing.tune.speedWindow + 1
	if lo < 1 then lo = 1 end
	local sum = 0
	for i = lo, upto do sum = sum + speeds[i] end
	return sum / (upto - lo + 1)
end

-- Fill s.result and go to the cooldown. `how` is "stopped" or "sky".
--   back          degrees: the farthest back the wind-up reached (capped at backswingMaxDeg)
--   releaseAngle  forward degrees from the bottom: the farthest forward the arm got (where
--                 the throw leaves; skyDeg or a little over for a sky ball)
--   flickDps      deg/s: the flick's peak speedWindow average
--   flickFrac     minFlickFrac .. 1: the share of the backswing's power the flick gives
--   smoothness    0..1 over the flick's frames (swing.smoothness)
--   shake         1 - smoothness
--   pull          +1: the flick's fastest frame was one of its last pullFrames (still
--                 speeding up into the stop); -1: it peaked earlier and was falling off
--                 before the stop. Which way a shaky throw pulls.
--   how           "stopped" or "sky"
--   frames        frames in the flick (the trailing frames below releaseStopDps not counted)
local function release(s, how)
	local t = swing.tune
	local r = s.result
	local speeds, n = s.speeds, s.n
	-- the flick is its frames up to the last one still turning at speed
	local used = n
	while used > 1 and speeds[used] < t.releaseStopDps do used = used - 1 end
	local flick, fast, fastAt = 0, -math.huge, 1
	for i = 1, used do
		local w = windowSpeed(speeds, i)
		if w > flick then flick = w end
		if speeds[i] >= fast then fast, fastAt = speeds[i], i end
	end
	local f = (flick - t.swingStartDps) / (t.fullFlickDps - t.swingStartDps)
	if f < 0 then f = 0 elseif f > 1 then f = 1 end
	local sm = swing.smoothness(speeds, used)
	r.back = s.back
	r.releaseAngle = s.far
	r.flickDps = flick
	r.flickFrac = t.minFlickFrac + (1 - t.minFlickFrac) * f
	r.smoothness = sm
	r.shake = 1 - sm
	r.pull = (fastAt > used - t.pullFrames) and 1 or -1
	r.how = how
	r.frames = used
	s.phase, s.pending, s.arm, s.n, s.cool = "cooldown", 0, 0, 0, t.cooldownS
	return "release"
end

-- At a measured stop (or a finger lift) release at the farthest forward
-- angle. Only a forward swing past the bottom can leave the hand.
function swing.stop(s)
	if s.phase == "swinging" and s.far > 0 then return release(s, "stopped") end
	swing.reset(s)
	return "letdown"
end

-- Feed one frame. Returns nil, "letdown" or "release" (then s.result holds
-- the measurements).
-- A touch contact explicitly releases on lift; while held it can slow down
-- during the upswing. Crossing the sky angle still releases immediately.
function swing.update(s, delta, dt, held)
	local t = swing.tune
	if dt <= 0 then return nil end
	local phase = s.phase

	if phase == "cooldown" then
		s.cool = s.cool - dt
		if s.cool <= 0 then s.phase, s.cool = "idle", 0 end
		return nil
	end

	local fwd = delta * t.forwardSign

	if phase == "idle" then
		local p = s.pending - fwd
		if p < 0 then p = 0 end
		s.pending = p
		if p >= t.startBackDeg then
			s.phase = "winding"
			if s.onArm then s.onArm(0, -p) end
			s.arm = -p
			s.back = (p < t.backswingMaxDeg) and p or t.backswingMaxDeg
			s.far, s.n = -p, 0
		end
		return nil
	end

	if phase == "winding" then
		if fwd > 0 and fwd / dt >= t.swingStartDps then
			s.phase = "swinging"
			s.far, s.n = s.arm, 0
			-- and this frame is the flick's first: on to swinging below
		else
			local a = s.arm + fwd
			if s.onArm then s.onArm(s.arm, a) end
			s.arm = a
			if -a > s.back then
				s.back = (-a < t.backswingMaxDeg) and -a or t.backswingMaxDeg
			end
			if a >= 0 then
				swing.reset(s)
				return "letdown"
			end
			return nil
		end
	end

	-- swinging
	local n = s.n
	if n < t.maxSamples then
		n = n + 1
		s.speeds[n] = fwd / dt
		s.n = n
	end
	local a = s.arm + fwd
	if s.onArm then s.onArm(s.arm, a) end
	s.arm = a
	if a > s.far then s.far = a end
	if s.far >= t.skyDeg then return release(s, "sky") end
	if not held and windowSpeed(s.speeds, n) < t.releaseStopDps then
		return swing.stop(s)
	end
	return nil
end

-- Run a recorded swing through a fresh state. `samples` is a flat array
-- {dt1, delta1, dt2, delta2, ...}. Returns the first event ("release" or
-- "letdown") and, for a release, the result table; or nil if the samples end
-- mid-swing.
function swing.replay(samples)
	local s = swing.new()
	for i = 1, #samples - 1, 2 do
		local ev = swing.update(s, samples[i + 1], samples[i])
		if ev then return ev, (ev == "release") and s.result or nil end
	end
	return nil
end

tw.swing = swing
core/throwplan:
-- The throw plan (DESIGN.md section 4, "The throw: the crank as a clock").
-- Pure Lua: no playdate.*.
--
-- The player picks a target (a point in the far half), a stance (where they
-- stand on or behind the throwing line) and a plan (the arc as a release
-- angle on the clock, a tilt for a baton, spin for a kubb). tw.plan turns
-- those into the gauge's two targets, the power target (the backswing this
-- throw needs) and the release target (where to stop the crank), and turns a
-- measured swing (core/swing's result) into a launch for core/world.
--
-- The clock, in degrees from 6 o'clock: the backswing goes up the left side
-- (30 = 7 o'clock, 90 = 9, 120 = 10, 180 = 12), the forward swing up the
-- right (30 = 5 o'clock, 90 = 3, 150 = 1, 180 = 12).
--
-- Two scales:
--   power  the backswing sets a launch speed (plan.speedFor). Its scale is
--          the reach (plan.reach): how far a clean baton at the reference
--          arc (3 o'clock, refLoftDeg) carries on flat ground from the hand.
--          0 m at 7 o'clock, 4 m at 9, 8 m at 10, and on up a quadratic:
--          corner to corner (9.4 m) at about 10:17, 13.3 m at 11, 20 m at 12.
--   loft   the release angle sets the launch angle (plan.loftFor), a line
--          through 5 o'clock = 12 degrees and 3 o'clock = 32 (half past 1 =
--          47, 12 o'clock = 62).
--
-- One frame throughout: the thrower's view frame (core/frame), throwing
-- from lineY toward +y, x to the right. Swivel is radians from straight
-- downfield, + = toward +x (right), as core/flight and core/world use it.
--
-- The functions the throw scene calls every aim frame (stance, snap, solve,
-- the scales) make no tables or closures: they fill an `out` table.
import "core/tw"
import "core/flight"
import "core/drill"
import "core/body"

local sqrt, sin, cos, tan, atan, rad, deg = math.sqrt, math.sin, math.cos, math.tan, math.atan, math.rad, math.deg
local floor, log, pi = math.floor, math.log, math.pi

local plan = {}
local flight, drill, body = tw.flight, tw.drill, tw.body

plan.tune = {
	-- the power scale (plan.reach): reach = a u + c u^2 with u = back - reachZeroDeg,
	-- a and c fitted through the two anchors below. A quadratic through
	-- (30, 0), (90, 4), (120, 8) has a = 1/45 and c = 1/1350, both positive, so
	-- it rises from zero, is smooth and monotonic, and gets steeper past 10
	-- o'clock: 9.4 m (corner to corner) at 128.6 degrees (about 10:17), 13.3 m
	-- at 11 o'clock, 20 m at 12 (overpowered: more than any throw needs).
	reachZeroDeg = 30,     -- backswing degrees where the reach is 0 (7 o'clock; the dead zone ends)
	reachAnchor1Deg = 90,  -- 9 o'clock ...
	reachAnchor1 = 4.0,    -- ... carries about 4 m
	reachAnchor2Deg = 120, -- 10 o'clock ...
	reachAnchor2 = 8.0,    -- ... carries 8 m: a baseline baton
	refLoftDeg = 32,       -- the reference arc the reach is measured at: 3 o'clock (loftFor(90))
	-- the loft scale (plan.loftFor): a line through two points
	loftRel1 = 30,  loftAt1 = 12,  -- 5 o'clock: low and flat
	loftRel2 = 90,  loftAt2 = 32,  -- 3 o'clock: the normal throw
	loftMinDeg = 2,        -- the launch angle never goes under this ...
	loftMaxDeg = 75,       -- ... or over this (a sky ball reaches it)
	-- the plan (B + d-pad)
	arc = { base = 90, king = 75, field = 60, drill = 135 }, -- default release by target: 3
