	                       -- o'clock at base kubbs, half past 3 at the king, 4 at field
	                       -- kubbs, half past 1 for a drilled kubb
	arcStepDeg = 15,       -- B + up/down moves the release target half an hour
	releaseMinDeg = 15,    -- the planned release stays between half past 5 ...
	releaseMaxDeg = 165,   -- ... and half past 12
	tiltStepDeg = 5,       -- B + left/right on a baton: one tap tilts the spin plane this much. Measured
	                       -- (tools/tiltgroups.lua, 2026-11-15): tilt deflects the baton after its first
	                       -- hit by only about 0.15 degrees per degree, so finer steps make no visible
	                       -- difference
	tiltMaxDeg = 20,       -- ... up to this either way (Jamie, 2026-11-15: tap up to 20 in steps of 5).
	                       -- With the shake it adds up toward legalTiltDeg, the helicopter
	spinSteps = 3,         -- B + left/right on a kubb: up to this many taps either way
	spinPerStep = 22,      -- rad/s about the long axis per tap (+ clockwise from behind), on top of the
	                       -- wrist's spiral (drill.tune.spiral). A spun drill holds its release attitude to
	                       -- the touch, a gyroscope; once down, spin moves it a little either way: which
	                       -- corner strikes first decides more than the spin (2026-11-16, the plain body
	                       -- with the turf's bite; tools/spinwall.lua)
	defaultLevel = "club", -- the level when none is given
	-- the swing against the plan (plan.launch)
	skyExtraDeg = 45,      -- a sky ball (the crank on past 12): its release counts as this
	                       -- many degrees past where it stopped (at least 12 o'clock), so it
	                       -- leaves near loftMaxDeg, high and short: the large error
	legalTiltDeg = 30,     -- a tilt over this is a helicopter (II.B.1); the old swing's
	                       -- 90 * (1 - smoothness) was legal at 30 or under
	shakeTiltDeg = 90,     -- tilt of a throw with shake 1 at full cost (the old mapping)
	lateralDeg = 3,        -- swivel pull of a throw with shake 1 at full cost (first guess:
	                       -- a baton at 8 m only hits within about 0.4 degrees)
	overPerDeg = 30,       -- the overpower multiplier grows by overGain per this many
	                       -- degrees of backswing past the power target
	steadyBelow = 0.25,    -- shake under this is STEADY
	-- Where a baton is aimed (Tyler's report, 2026-11-16: "all of them went clean
	-- over the field kubb"). A thrower aims at the kubb, not at the turf under it:
	-- the clean throw sends the baton's centre through the target piece at this
	-- share of the piece's height (a kubb 0.15 m tall: 7.5 cm up; the king 0.30
	-- m: 15 cm), so it meets the piece's face instead of coming down at its foot.
	-- A target not on a piece (an empty spot) is aimed at the ground, as before.
	-- Drilled kubbs are not aimed this way (drill.solveAt has its own landing).
	aimHeightShare = 0.5,
	-- The wrist checks the arm's rotation to aim for the level's tumbleTurns.
	-- On longer throws the arm speed limits how much of that rotation can be
	-- checked. A rough release adds seeded variation in turns (tumbleSd).
	armR = 0.9,            -- m, shoulder to the centre of the baton
	wristShare = 0.75,     -- maximum share the wrist can check or add
	tumbleMin = 0,         -- rad/s: the drawn rate never goes under this (no backspin)
	-- Nerves (2026-11-16): before this nothing but the shake put a throw
	-- left or right, so a long throw was as true as a short one. Every
	-- throw, the player's and the computer's, gets two seeded draws in plan.launch (opts.nerves): an angle off the planned
	-- line (degrees, so the miss in metres grows with the range) and a share
	-- of the throw's length. Their sd is the level's nervesDeg and nervesLen
	-- (plan.levels) times three things:
	--   effort     1 + effortGain x (reach / effortRefM - 1), never under
	--              effortMin: the power of the throw (the backswing as it
	--              counts) against a baseline baton
	--   roughness  1 + roughGain x the swing's shake (core/swing): the
	--              swing's own roughness
	--   overpower  the same multiplier as the shake's costs (overGain)
	-- and for a drilled kubb drillNerves of that.
	effortRefM = 8,        -- m: the reach of a baseline baton: effort 1
	effortGain = 2.5,      -- how much a longer reach adds (6 m: 0.375, 10 m: 1.625)
	effortMin = 0.15,      -- effort never goes under this (a 5.2 m reach and under)
	roughGain = 1,         -- shake 1 doubles the spread
	drillNerves = 1,       -- a drilled kubb's nerves against a baton's
	lenMin = -0.5,         -- the length share never takes more than half the throw
	fanSd = 1,             -- the aim fan (plan.spread) is this many sd either side
	-- the verdict's sideways cell (plan.launch's sideV): within straightM of
	-- the planned line at the target is STRAIGHT, else PULLED LEFT or RIGHT;
	-- the length (lenV) within longM of it is ON
	straightM = 0.06,      -- m: about a baton's hit either side of a kubb's centre
	longM = 0.3,           -- m
}

-- Throw levels (DESIGN 4 "Throw levels"): how wide the gauge's targets are and
-- how much a miss costs. First guesses, to be fitted from play.
--   powerHalf    degrees either side of the power target's center
--   releaseHalf  degrees either side of the release target's center
--   inGain       share of an error inside a target that still counts
--   shakeGain    share of the shake's tilt and pull that counts
--   overGain     how fast overpowering multiplies the shake's costs
--   nervesDeg    sd of the angle off the planned line (degrees) at effort 1,
--                a clean swing and no overpower (plan.tune "Nerves")
--   nervesLen    sd of the length error, a share of the throw, the same way
--   tumbleSd     sd of the tumble, in turns over the planned flight, times the
--                swing's roughness and the overpower (plan.tune "the baton's tumble")
plan.levels = {
	beginner = { powerHalf = 15, releaseHalf = 30, inGain = 0.1, shakeGain = 0.5,  overGain = 0.5,
		nervesDeg = 1.6, nervesLen = 0.06, tumbleTurns = 0.62, tumbleSd = 0.10 },
	club     = { powerHalf = 8,  releaseHalf = 18, inGain = 0.3, shakeGain = 0.75, overGain = 0.75,
		nervesDeg = 0.8, nervesLen = 0.03, tumbleTurns = 0.50, tumbleSd = 0.06 },
	pro      = { powerHalf = 4,  releaseHalf = 10, inGain = 0.6, shakeGain = 1,    overGain = 1,
		nervesDeg = 0.5, nervesLen = 0.02, tumbleTurns = 0.50, tumbleSd = 0.035 },
}
plan.LEVELS = { "beginner", "club", "pro" }

-- The level table for a name or a level table (nil: tune.defaultLevel).
function plan.level(l)
	if type(l) == "table" then return l end
	return plan.levels[l or plan.tune.defaultLevel] or plan.levels[plan.tune.defaultLevel]
end
local levelOf = plan.level

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The scales

-- The quadratic's coefficients from the anchors (worked out per call from the
-- tune, so a change to it takes at once; a few multiplications).
local function reachCoeffs()
	local t = plan.tune
	local u1, u2 = t.reachAnchor1Deg - t.reachZeroDeg, t.reachAnchor2Deg - t.reachZeroDeg
	local c = (t.reachAnchor2 / u2 - t.reachAnchor1 / u1) / (u2 - u1)
	return t.reachAnchor1 / u1 - c * u1, c
end

-- Meters a clean baton thrown with this backswing (degrees) carries at the
-- reference arc on flat ground from the hand height: the power scale.
function plan.reach(backDeg)
	local u = backDeg - plan.tune.reachZeroDeg
	if u <= 0 then return 0 end
	local a, c = reachCoeffs()
	return a * u + c * u * u
end

-- The backswing (degrees) whose reach is reachM: plan.reach's inverse.
function plan.backFor(reachM)
	local z = plan.tune.reachZeroDeg
	if reachM <= 0 then return z end
	local a, c = reachCoeffs()
	if c < 1e-12 then return z + reachM / a end
	return z + (-a + sqrt(a * a + 4 * c * reachM)) / (2 * c)
end

-- The speed that carries a baton R (m) from hand height h to the ground at
-- loft e (radians) through still air, with its drag: flight.predict's arc
-- (flight.speedForCarry), and that flight's time (s).
local function carrySpeed(R, e, h)
	return flight.speedForCarry(R, e, h, flight.tune.dragK.baton)
end
-- (h is the hand's height over the point the carry ends at: the ground, or
-- in plan.solve the aim height, plan.aimZFor)

-- The launch speed (m/s) a backswing gives with a full flick: the speed whose
-- clean flight at refLoftDeg carries plan.reach(backDeg).
function plan.speedFor(backDeg)
	local R = plan.reach(backDeg)
	if R <= 0 then return 0 end
	local ft = flight.tune
	local v = carrySpeed(R, rad(plan.tune.refLoftDeg), ft.handHeight)
	return v
end

-- How far a launch speed carries at the reference arc (m): the reach it is.
function plan.reachForSpeed(speed)
	local _, ly = flight.predict(0, 0, 0, plan.tune.refLoftDeg, speed)
	return ly
end

-- The backswing (degrees) that gives this launch speed with a full flick.
function plan.backForSpeed(speed)
	if speed <= 0 then return plan.tune.reachZeroDeg end
	return plan.backFor(plan.reachForSpeed(speed))
end

-- The launch angle (degrees) for a release angle (degrees past 6 o'clock on
-- the forward side), clamped to loftMinDeg..loftMaxDeg.
function plan.loftFor(releaseDeg)
	local t = plan.tune
	local l = t.loftAt1 + (releaseDeg - t.loftRel1) * (t.loftAt2 - t.loftAt1) / (t.loftRel2 - t.loftRel1)
	if l < t.loftMinDeg then return t.loftMinDeg end
	if l > t.loftMaxDeg then return t.loftMaxDeg end
	return l
end

-- The release angle (degrees) for a launch angle: plan.loftFor's inverse.
function plan.releaseFor(loftDeg)
	local t = plan.tune
	if loftDeg < t.loftMinDeg then loftDeg = t.loftMinDeg elseif loftDeg > t.loftMaxDeg then loftDeg = t.loftMaxDeg end
	return t.loftRel1 + (loftDeg - t.loftAt1) * (t.loftRel2 - t.loftRel1) / (t.loftAt2 - t.loftAt1)
end

-- The baton's planned tumble rate (rad/s) for a clean launch at speed (m/s)
-- and loftDeg (plan.tune, "the baton's tumble"): tumbleTurns over the flight,
-- inside the wrist's range about the arm's rate. The rate only; the clean
-- flight's time is plan.flightTime, or T when the caller has it already
-- (plan.solve: the speed's own solve gives it).
function plan.flightTime(speed, loftDeg, z)
	local _, _, T = flight.predict(0, 0, 0, loftDeg or plan.tune.refLoftDeg, speed, z)
	return T
end
function plan.tumbleFor(speed, loftDeg, T, level)
	local t = plan.tune
	T = T or plan.flightTime(speed, loftDeg)
	local arm = speed / t.armR
	local lo, hi = arm * (1 - t.wristShare), arm * (1 + t.wristShare)
	local r = T > 0 and 2 * pi * (plan.level(level).tumbleTurns or plan.levels.club.tumbleTurns) / T or 0
	if r < lo then r = lo elseif r > hi then r = hi end
	return r
end

-- Clamp a planned release to releaseMinDeg..releaseMaxDeg.
function plan.clampRelease(releaseDeg)
	local t = plan.tune
	if releaseDeg < t.releaseMinDeg then return t.releaseMinDeg end
	if releaseDeg > t.releaseMaxDeg then return t.releaseMaxDeg end
	return releaseDeg
end

-- The default release for a target kind: "base", "king", "field" or "drill".
function plan.arcFor(kind)
	return plan.tune.arc[kind] or plan.tune.arc.base
end

-- The height (m) a baton's centre is aimed through a piece of this kind:
-- "king" the king, anything else a kubb ("base", "field", "kubb"); nil (no
-- piece: an empty spot) the ground, 0. aimHeightShare of the piece's height.
function plan.aimZFor(kind)
	if not kind then return 0 end
	local k = kind == "king" and body.kinds.king or body.kinds.kubb
	-- At a half turn the lower end leads into the target. Give that end
	-- clearance over the grass as the centre crosses the near face.
	return plan.tune.aimHeightShare * 2 * k.hz + body.kinds.baton.hl
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Stance, snap and solve (every aim frame)

-- The default stance: straight behind the target (x clamped inside
-- +/- halfWidth, the line's ends), as far forward as allowed (forwardY, the
-- advantage line or the baseline; nil = lineY). Fills out.x, out.y.
function plan.stance(tx, ty, lineY, forwardY, halfWidth, out)
	local x = tx
	if x < -halfWidth then x = -halfWidth elseif x > halfWidth then x = halfWidth end
	out.x, out.y = x, forwardY or lineY
	return out
end

-- The nearest of targets[1..n] (each {x, y}: standing kubbs and the king)
-- within radius of (tx, ty), and its index; nil when none is that close.
function plan.snap(tx, ty, targets, n, radius)
	local best, bi, bd = nil, nil, radius * radius
	for i = 1, n do
		local p = targets[i]
		local dx, dy = p.x - tx, p.y - ty
		local d = dx * dx + dy * dy
		if d <= bd then best, bi, bd = p, i, d end
	end
	return best, bi
end

-- Solve the plan. q = { projectile = "baton" | "kubb", px, py (the stance),
-- tx, ty (the target), release (planned degrees, clamped to the plan's
-- range), level (name or table), surface and spin (a kubb's ground and
-- planned spin in taps: how far it runs on, drill.slideFor; nil: grass, none),
-- aimZ (a baton: the height its centre is aimed through at the target,
-- plan.aimZFor; nil: 0, the ground) }. Fills and returns `out`:
--   swivel     radians, + = right
--   dist       m from the stance to the target
--   loft       degrees, loftFor(release)
--   speed      m/s of the clean launch: a baton's center passes through the
--              target at aimZ (flight.carry to that height); a kubb's drill
--              rests on it (drill.solveAt at that loft)
--   aimZ       the height the baton's centre is aimed at (0 for a kubb)
--   back       the backswing that gives that speed with a full flick
--   powerLo, powerHi      the power target: back -/+ level.powerHalf
--   release, releaseLo, releaseHi   the release target: release -/+ level.releaseHalf
--   projectile, px, py, tx, ty, level (the level table)
--   tumble, flightT   a baton's planned tumble (rad/s) and clean flight time to the
--              target at aimZ (plan.tumbleFor)
-- For a kubb also drill.solveAt's x, band and T.
function plan.solve(q, out)
	local lv = levelOf(q.level)
	local rel = plan.clampRelease(q.release or plan.tune.arc.base)
	local loft = plan.loftFor(rel)
	local px, py, tx, ty = q.px, q.py, q.tx, q.ty
	if q.projectile == "kubb" then
		drill.solveAt(tx, ty, py, loft, out, px, q.surface, (q.spin or 0) * plan.tune.spinPerStep)
		out.tumble, out.flightT, out.aimZ = nil, nil, 0
	else
		local dx, dy = tx - px, ty - py
		local d = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
		local ft = flight.tune
		local z = q.aimZ or 0
		out.swivel, out.dist, out.loft, out.aimZ = atan(dx, dy), d, loft, z
		local speed, T = carrySpeed(d > 0.1 and d or 0.1, rad(loft), ft.handHeight - z)
		out.speed = speed
		out.tumble, out.flightT = plan.tumbleFor(speed, loft, T, lv), T
	end
	local back = plan.backForSpeed(out.speed)
	out.back, out.powerLo, out.powerHi = back, back - lv.powerHalf, back + lv.powerHalf
	out.release, out.releaseLo, out.releaseHi = rel, rel - lv.releaseHalf, rel + lv.releaseHalf
	out.projectile, out.px, out.py, out.tx, out.ty, out.level = q.projectile or "baton", px, py, tx, ty, lv
	return out
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Nerves (plan.tune "Nerves")

-- A seeded stream (Park-Miller with a scrambled seed): r.next() in [0, 1),
-- r.uniform(a, b), r.normal(sd). core/autothrow's rng is this one.
function plan.rng(seed)
	local h = floor(seed) & 0xffffffff
	h = ((h ~ (h >> 16)) * 0x45d9f3b) & 0xffffffff
	h = ((h ~ (h >> 16)) * 0x45d9f3b) & 0xffffffff
	h = h ~ (h >> 16)
	local s = h % 2147483647
	if s <= 0 then s = s + 2147483646 end
	local r = {}
	function r.next()
		s = (s * 48271) % 2147483647
		return (s - 1) / 2147483646
	end
	for _ = 1, 8 do r.next() end
	function r.uniform(a, b) return a + (b - a) * r.next() end
	function r.normal(sd)
		local u1 = r.next()
		if u1 < 1e-12 then u1 = 1e-12 end
		return sd * sqrt(-2 * log(u1)) * cos(2 * pi * r.next())
	end
	return r
end

-- The seed of a player's throw: from the swing as measured and the plan, the
-- way world.seedFrom seeds the ground from the launch, so the same swing at
-- the same plan draws the same nerves (replays, tests) and every other throw
-- its own.
local function mix(h, v)
	return (h ~ floor((v or 0) * 4096)) * 0x9E3779B1 & 0x7fffffff
end
local function swingSeed(sol, r)
	local h = mix(0x2545F491, r.back)
	h = mix(h, r.releaseAngle)
	h = mix(h, r.flickDps or r.flickFrac)
	h = mix(h, r.shake)
	h = mix(h, sol.tx)
	h = mix(h, sol.ty)
	h = mix(h, sol.px)
	return mix(h, sol.py)
end
plan.swingSeed = swingSeed

-- The effort of a throw with backswing back: its reach (plan.reach) against
-- effortRefM.
local function effortFor(back)
	local t = plan.tune
	local e = 1 + t.effortGain * (plan.reach(back) / t.effortRefM - 1)
	if e < t.effortMin then return t.effortMin end
	return e
end

-- The nerves' two sds for a throw at level lv (name or table) with backswing
-- back (degrees, as it counts), shake (0..1), overpower multiplier over (1:
-- none) and kubb (a drilled kubb): the angle off the line (degrees) and the
-- length share. No tables.
function plan.nervesSd(lv, back, shake, over, kubb)
	local t = plan.tune
	lv = levelOf(lv)
	local k = effortFor(back) * (1 + t.roughGain * (shake or 0)) * (over or 1)
	if kubb then k = k * t.drillNerves end
	return (lv.nervesDeg or 0) * k, (lv.nervesLen or 0) * k
end

-- The aim fan for solution sol (plan.solve) at its own power with a clean
-- swing: how far either side of the planned line (m) the throw spreads at
-- range m from the thrower (fanSd sds), and the sd of the angle (degrees).
-- (An aim fan drawn from it was tried in the throw scene on 2026-11-16 and
-- dropped: at club level 1 sd at 8 m is about 0.1 m, inside the target
-- circle, so the fan read as a narrow lane, not a spread.)
function plan.spread(sol, range, level)
	local sd = plan.nervesSd(level or sol.level, sol.back, 0, 1, sol.projectile == "kubb")
	return tan(rad(sd * plan.tune.fanSd)) * range, sd
end

-- The aim fan's two edges: from the thrower at px, py to the target tx, ty
-- (any frame with y down the pitch), the points plan.spread's half width
-- either side of the target, across the line. Fills and returns out (lx,
-- ly and rx, ry the two edges, half the half width in m).
function plan.fan(sol, px, py, tx, ty, level, out)
	out = out or {}
	local dx, dy = tx - px, ty - py
	local range = sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)
	local half = plan.spread(sol, range, level)
	local nx, ny = 0, 0
	if range > 0 then nx, ny = -dy / range, dx / range end
	out.half = half
	out.lx, out.ly = tx - nx * half, ty - ny * half
	out.rx, out.ry = tx + nx * half, ty + ny * half
	return out
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The launch (once per throw)

-- An error e against a target half width h: inside the target it counts
-- inGain of itself; outside, the part beyond the edge counts in full. The two
-- meet at the edge (continuous).
function plan.shrink(e, h, inGain)
	if e >= -h and e <= h then return e * inGain end
	if e > 0 then return h * inGain + (e - h) end
	return -h * inGain + (e + h)
end
local shrink = plan.shrink

local NO_OPTS = {}

-- Which side of the range [lo, hi] v is on: -1, 0, 1.
local function side(v, lo, hi)
	if v < lo then return -1 end
	if v > hi then return 1 end
	return 0
end

-- The launch for swing result `r` against the solution `sol`. r: back,
-- releaseAngle, flickFrac, smoothness, shake, pull (+1 / -1), how ("stopped"
-- or "sky"). opts = { projectile, tilt (planned degrees, a baton), spin
-- (planned taps, a kubb: + rolls right), level, nerves } (projectile and
-- level default to the solution's; nerves: nil or false none, true draws
-- them from a stream seeded by the swing and the plan (plan.swingSeed: a
-- player's throw), or a stream (plan.rng: the computer's own) to draw them
-- from; two normals either way). Fills and returns `out`:
--   speed, loft, swivel, tilt, tumble   the launch (world.launchBaton's arguments)
--   legal      false for a helicopter: |tilt| over legalTiltDeg (a baton; a kubb is always legal)
--   powerV     -1 short, 0 on, 1 long: the power the throw got (backswing times flick)
--              against the power target; -2 slow: the backswing was enough, the flick was not
--   releaseV   -1 low, 0 on, 1 high: where the crank stopped against the release target
--   steady     shake under steadyBelow
--   over       how much overpowering multiplied the shake's costs (0 = none)
--   back, release   the effective backswing and release after the target's forgiveness
--   sideDeg    degrees off the planned line, + = right: the shake's pull and the nerves
--   lenShare   the nerves' length error, a share of the throw (the speed is scaled by
--              sqrt(1 + lenShare), so the carry by about 1 + lenShare)
--   sideM, lenM   the same in metres at the plan's distance (sol.dist)
--   sdSide, sdLen  the nerves' sds this throw had (plan.nervesSd)
--   sideV      -1 pulled left, 0 straight, 1 pulled right (sideM against straightM)
--   lenV       -1 short, 0 on, 1 long by the nerves alone (lenM against longM)
--   tumble     a baton's turn rate (rad/s): the plan's, times the flick, plus a third
--              nerves draw of sdTurns turns over the planned flight (plan.tune "the baton's tumble")
-- For a kubb also noseDown, rollLand, spin (rad/s), wobble, jerk
-- (drill.body: world.launchDrill's arguments after the loft and speed);
-- tumble is 0 and tilt is only the shake's.
function plan.launch(sol, r, opts, out)
	local t = plan.tune
	opts = opts or NO_OPTS
	local lv = levelOf(opts.level or sol.level)
	local kubb = (opts.projectile or sol.projectile) == "kubb"
	local shake = r.shake or (1 - (r.smoothness or 1))
	local pull = (r.pull or 1) < 0 and -1 or 1
	local flick = r.flickFrac or 1
	local back = r.back or 0
	-- power: the backswing, forgiven inside the target, sets the speed; the
	-- flick delivers its share of it
	local effBack = sol.back + shrink(back - sol.back, lv.powerHalf, lv.inGain)
	out.speed = plan.speedFor(effBack) * flick
	-- release: where the crank stopped, forgiven inside the target, sets the
	-- loft; a sky ball counts skyExtraDeg past 12 o'clock or where it stopped
	local rel = r.releaseAngle or sol.release
	if r.how == "sky" then
		if rel < 180 then rel = 180 end
		rel = rel + t.skyExtraDeg
	end
	if rel < 0 then rel = 0 end
	local effRel = sol.release + shrink(rel - sol.release, lv.releaseHalf, lv.inGain)
	out.loft = plan.loftFor(effRel)
	-- overpower: every 30 degrees past the power target multiplies the shake's costs
	local past = back - sol.powerHi
	local m = 1 + lv.overGain * (past > 0 and past or 0) / t.overPerDeg
	local se = shake * lv.shakeGain * m -- the shake as it counts
	local shakeTilt = t.shakeTiltDeg * se
	-- sideways and along: the shake's pull (the swing's roughness, one way)
	-- and the nerves (two seeded draws, either way: opts.nerves)
	local zs, zl, zt = 0, 0, 0
	local nv = opts.nerves
	if nv then
		local rng = type(nv) == "table" and nv or plan.rng(swingSeed(sol, r))
		zs, zl = rng.normal(1), rng.normal(1)
		if not kubb then zt = rng.normal(1) end
	end
	local sdSide, sdLen = plan.nervesSd(lv, effBack, shake, m, kubb)
	local sideDeg = pull * t.lateralDeg * se + zs * sdSide
	if r.lineDeg then sideDeg = sideDeg + r.lineDeg end
	local len = zl * sdLen
	if len < t.lenMin then len = t.lenMin end
	out.speed = out.speed * sqrt(1 + len)
	out.swivel = sol.swivel + rad(sideDeg)
	local dist = sol.dist or 0
	local sideM, lenM = tan(rad(sideDeg)) * dist, len * dist
	out.sideDeg, out.lenShare, out.sideM, out.lenM = sideDeg, len, sideM, lenM
	out.sdSide, out.sdLen = sdSide, sdLen
	out.sideV = side(sideM, -t.straightM, t.straightM)
	out.lenV = side(lenM, -t.longM, t.longM)
	-- the power verdict goes by what the throw got: the backswing times the
	-- flick (Jamie's first play-test throw, 2026-11-15: back on the target, a
	-- 534 deg/s flick, 2.6 m of an 8 m throw, and the verdict said ON). Short
	-- of the target with the backswing on it or past it is a slow flick: -2.
	local got = plan.backForSpeed(plan.speedFor(back) * flick)
	local pv = side(got, sol.powerLo, sol.powerHi)
	if pv < 0 and back >= sol.powerLo then pv = -2 end
	out.powerV = pv
	out.releaseV = r.how == "sky" and 1 or side(r.releaseAngle or sol.release, sol.releaseLo, sol.releaseHi)
	out.steady = shake < t.steadyBelow
	out.over = m - 1
	out.back, out.release = effBack, effRel
	if kubb then
		out.tilt = pull * shakeTilt
		out.legal = true
		out.tumble = 0
		drill.body(1 - se, pull, (opts.spin or 0) * t.spinPerStep, out, out.loft - (sol.loft or out.loft))
	else
		local tilt = (opts.tilt or 0) + pull * shakeTilt
		out.tilt = tilt
		out.legal = (tilt < 0 and -tilt or tilt) <= t.legalTiltDeg
		-- the release's tumble: the plan's rate (a solve without one: worked
		-- out here), the flick's share of it, and the nerves' turns
		local rate, T = sol.tumble, sol.flightT
		if not rate then
			local v, l = sol.speed or out.speed, sol.loft or out.loft
			T = plan.flightTime(v, l, sol.aimZ)
			rate = plan.tumbleFor(v, l, T, lv)
		end
		local rangeFactor = math.min(1.5, math.max(0.5, (sol.dist or 8) / 8))
		local sdT = (lv.tumbleSd or 0) * rangeFactor * (1 + t.roughGain * shake) * m
		rate = rate * flick + (T and T > 0 and zt * sdT * 2 * pi / T or 0)
		if rate < t.tumbleMin then rate = t.tumbleMin end
		out.tumble, out.sdTurns = rate, sdT
	end
	return out
end

local POWER = { [-2] = "SLOW", [-1] = "SHORT", [0] = "ON", [1] = "LONG" }
local RELEASE = { [-1] = "LOW", [0] = "ON", [1] = "HIGH" }

local SIDE = { [-1] = "PULLED LEFT", [0] = "STRAIGHT", [1] = "PULLED RIGHT" }

-- The HUD's verdicts after a throw, a word each: power (SLOW, SHORT, ON, LONG),
-- release (LOW, ON, HIGH), steadiness (STEADY, SHAKY) and which way it went
-- (plan.sideText).
function plan.verdictText(out)
	return POWER[out.powerV or 0], RELEASE[out.releaseV or 0], out.steady and "STEADY" or "SHAKY",
		SIDE[out.sideV or 0]
end

-- Which way a throw went (sideV: -1, 0, 1): PULLED LEFT, STRAIGHT, PULLED RIGHT.
function plan.sideText(sideV)
	return SIDE[sideV or 0] or SIDE[0]
end

tw.plan = plan
core/trace:
-- Crank traces: one recorded swing per line of traces.jsonl. Pure Lua: no
-- playdate.*, so the game writes lines with trace.encode and desktop tools
-- read them back with trace.decode and replay them with core/swing.
--
-- A line is one JSON object:
--   {"v":1,"time":"2026-11-20 19:42:07","sign":-1,"release":"clock",
--    "event":"release","samples":[[0.02,4.5],[0.02,6.1],...],
--    "result":{"back":118,"releaseAngle":88.5,"flickDps":940,"flickFrac":0.94,
--              "smoothness":0.88,"shake":0.12,"pull":1,"how":"stopped",
--              "frames":6,"loft":32,"distance":8.41}}
-- samples are [dt seconds, raw getCrankChange degrees] per frame, from the
-- first frame of the wind-up to the frame of the release or let-down. "sign"
-- is swing.tune.forwardSign at the time. "result" is absent for a let-down.
-- Its first fields are what core/swing measured (the crank as a clock,
-- 2026-11-15; meanings at swing.lua's release()): back, releaseAngle,
-- flickDps, flickFrac, smoothness, shake, pull, how ("stopped" or "sky"),
-- frames. The game adds the throw's plan and what it made of the swing
-- (docs/notes/throw.md "The throw", 2026-11-15), y measured from the thrower's line:
--   "level"       the throw level (beginner, club, pro)
--   "projectile"  "baton" or "kubb" (a drilled kubb)
--   "drillId"     the practice drill's id in a drill run (8m, doubles, wall, ...)
--   "tx","ty"     the target circle; "px","py" the stance
--   "plan"        the planned release (clock degrees); "loft" its launch angle
--   "powerLo","powerHi","releaseLo","releaseHi"   the clock's targets
--   "planTilt"    a baton's planned tilt (degrees); "spin" a kubb's (taps)
--   "launchSpeed","launchLoft","swivelOff"   the launch (m/s, degrees, degrees
--                 off the plan's swivel: the shake's pull and the nerves);
--                 "tumbleRate", "tilt"
--   "legal"       false for a helicopter
--   "powerV","releaseV"   -1, 0, 1: short / on / long, low / on / high;
--                 "steady" true or false
--   "sideDeg","lenShare"   the nerves (2026-11-16, tw.plan.launch): degrees
--                 off the line (+ right) and the share long (+) or short;
--                 "sideV","lenV" -1, 0, 1: pulled left / straight / pulled
--                 right, short / on / long
--   "distance"    m from the release to the first touch
--
-- "release" says which swing wrote the line: "clock" for the crank as a
-- clock; "stop" (2026-11-14) for the release where the crank stopped against
-- the loft's notch; absent before that (released as the arm passed the
-- bottom). Older results carry that swing's fields (power, powerCap,
-- backswing, releaseSpeed, peakSpeed, tilt, legal, launchSpeed, tumbleRate,
-- launchLoft, how "passed", "slowed", "stopped" or "over"). Every line
-- decodes, and trace.replay runs any line's samples through today's swing.
--
-- A drilled kubb adds, after those, "mode":"drill" (a baton line has no
-- "mode") and, in meters with y measured from the thrower's baseline and x
-- across in the thrower's view:
--   "markerX","markerY"   the target circle (as tx, ty)
--   "landX","landY"       where the kubb first touched anything
--   "restX","restY"       where it came to rest
--   "throwerX"            where the thrower stood on the baseline
-- Lines from 2026-11-14 also carry "band", "verdict" and "cut" (the drill's
-- power band and A or B held for a cut), which today's throw has not.
import "core/tw"
import "core/swing"

local concat, fmt = table.concat, string.format

local trace = {}

local RESULT_KEYS = {
	-- what core/swing measured
	"back", "releaseAngle", "flickDps", "flickFrac", "smoothness", "shake", "pull", "how", "frames",
	-- the plan (added by the game)
	"level", "projectile", "drillId", "tx", "ty", "px", "py", "plan", "loft",
	"powerLo", "powerHi", "releaseLo", "releaseHi", "planTilt", "spin",
	-- what the throw made of it
	"launchSpeed", "launchLoft", "swivelOff", "tumbleRate", "tilt", "legal", "powerV", "releaseV", "steady",
	-- the nerves (core/throwplan "Nerves", 2026-11-16)
	"sideDeg", "lenShare", "sideV", "lenV",
	"distance",
	-- older lines' (the swing before 2026-11-15)
	"power",
	-- drills only (absent on a baton line)
	"mode", "band", "verdict", "cut", "markerX", "markerY", "landX", "landY", "restX", "restY", "throwerX",
}

local function num(v)
	if v ~= v or v == math.huge or v == -math.huge then return "0" end
	if math.type and math.type(v) == "integer" then return tostring(v) end
	return fmt("%.6g", v)
end

local function value(v)
	local ty = type(v)
	if ty == "number" then return num(v)
	elseif ty == "boolean" then return v and "true" or "false"
	elseif ty == "string" then return '"' .. v:gsub('[%c"\\]', "") .. '"'
	end
	return "null"
end

-- samples: flat {dt1, d1, dt2, d2, ...} with n pairs. result may be nil.
function trace.encode(samples, n, event, result, sign, time)
	local parts = {}
	for i = 1, n do
		parts[i] = "[" .. num(samples[2 * i - 1]) .. "," .. num(samples[2 * i]) .. "]"
	end
	-- every line written now comes from the crank as a clock, let-downs too
	local out = '{"v":1,"time":' .. value(time or "") .. ',"sign":' .. num(sign or 1)
		.. ',"release":"clock","input":"crank","event":' .. value(event or "") .. ',"samples":[' .. concat(parts, ",") .. "]"
	if result then
		local r = {}
		for _, k in ipairs(RESULT_KEYS) do
			if result[k] ~= nil then r[#r + 1] = '"' .. k .. '":' .. value(result[k]) end
		end
		out = out .. ',"result":{' .. concat(r, ",") .. "}"
	end
	return out .. "}"
end

-- A small JSON reader: objects, arrays, numbers, strings without escapes
-- beyond \" and \\, true, false, null. Enough for trace lines.
local function decoder(s)
	local i = 1
	local function ws() i = s:find("[^ \t\r\n]", i) or (#s + 1) end
	local parseValue
	local function parseString()
		local j = i + 1
		local buf = {}
		while true do
			local c = s:sub(j, j)
			if c == "" then error("unterminated string") end
			if c == '"' then break end
			if c == "\\" then j = j + 1; c = s:sub(j, j) end
			buf[#buf + 1] = c
			j = j + 1
		end
		i = j + 1
		return concat(buf)
	end
	function parseValue()
		ws()
		local c = s:sub(i, i)
		if c == "{" then
			i = i + 1
			local o = {}
			ws()
			if s:sub(i, i) == "}" then i = i + 1; return o end
			while true do
				ws()
				local k = parseString()
				ws()
				assert(s:sub(i, i) == ":", "expected :")
				i = i + 1
				o[k] = parseValue()
				ws()
				c = s:sub(i, i)
				i = i + 1
				if c == "}" then return o end
				assert(c == ",", "expected , or }")
			end
		elseif c == "[" then
			i = i + 1
			local a = {}
			ws()
			if s:sub(i, i) == "]" then i = i + 1; return a end
			while true do
				a[#a + 1] = parseValue()
				ws()
				c = s:sub(i, i)
				i = i + 1
				if c == "]" then return a end
				assert(c == ",", "expected , or ]")
			end
		elseif c == '"' then
			return parseString()
		elseif s:sub(i, i + 3) == "true" then i = i + 4; return true
		elseif s:sub(i, i + 4) == "false" then i = i + 5; return false
		elseif s:sub(i, i + 3) == "null" then i = i + 4; return nil
		else
			local a, b = s:find("^-?[%d.]+[eE]?[-+]?%d*", i)
			assert(a, "bad JSON at " .. i)
			i = b + 1
			return tonumber(s:sub(a, b))
		end
	end
	return parseValue
end

function trace.decode(line)
	return decoder(line)()
end

-- Replay a decoded trace through the current swing model. Returns the event
-- and result as swing.replay does. By default the trace's own sign is kept,
-- so a trace recorded before forwardSign was flipped replays as it was
-- thrown; with useCurrentSign the raw deltas meet today's forwardSign. Every
-- line, whichever swing wrote it ("release"), is replayed through today's.
function trace.replay(t, useCurrentSign)
	local swing = tw.swing
	local flat = {}
	local flip = useCurrentSign and 1 or (t.sign or 1) * swing.tune.forwardSign
	for _, p in ipairs(t.samples or {}) do
		flat[#flat + 1] = p[1]
		flat[#flat + 1] = p[2] * flip
	end
	return swing.replay(flat)
end

tw.trace = trace
core/wind:
-- The wind (Jamie and Tyler, 2026-11-14: "optional in a game to turn on wind
-- ... some indicator ... wind would affect the baton throws and kubb
-- throws"). Pure: no playdate.*.
--
-- A match's wind level comes from its options (WIND: off, light, strong).
-- Each turn the wind has a direction and a speed (wind.turn); each throw is a
-- gust of it (wind.gust): the speed and direction vary a little, so no two
-- throws meet quite the same air. Directions are in the world frame (radians,
-- the way the wind blows toward, 0 = +x), turned into a thrower's view frame
-- by wind.vector. core/world pushes the thrown piece with it in the air
-- (world.windX/Y, airDrag).
--
--   wind.levels        { off = 0, light = 2.5, strong = 6 } m/s, the turn's mean
--   wind.turn(rng, level)      dir, speed for a turn (speed 0 when off)
--   wind.gust(rng, dir, speed) dir, speed for one throw
--   wind.vector(dir, speed, side)  wx, wy in that side's view frame
--   wind.text(speed)           "WIND 4 M/S" (whole m/s, at least 1), nil when calm
import "core/tw"

local wind = {}

wind.levels = { off = 0, light = 2.5, strong = 6 }

wind.tune = {
	turnLow = 0.6,    -- a turn's speed: the level's mean times between these
	turnHigh = 1.3,
	gust = 0.25,      -- a throw's speed: the turn's times 1 +- this (uniform)
	gustDeg = 12,     -- a throw's direction: the turn's +- this (sd, degrees)
}

local pi, cos, sin, rad = math.pi, math.cos, math.sin, math.rad

function wind.turn(rng, level)
	local mean = wind.levels[level or "off"] or 0
	if mean <= 0 then return 0, 0 end
	local t = wind.tune
	return rng.uniform(-pi, pi), mean * rng.uniform(t.turnLow, t.turnHigh)
end

function wind.gust(rng, dir, speed)
	if speed <= 0 then return dir, 0 end
	local t = wind.tune
	return dir + rad(rng.normal(t.gustDeg)), speed * (1 + rng.uniform(-t.gust, t.gust))
end

-- Team B throws in the pitch turned 180 degrees (core/frame): a vector turns too.
function wind.vector(dir, speed, side)
	local wx, wy = speed * cos(dir), speed * sin(dir)
	if side == "B" then return -wx, -wy end
	return wx, wy
end

function wind.text(speed)
	if not speed or speed <= 0 then return nil end
	local n = math.floor(speed + 0.5)
	if n < 1 then n = 1 end
	return "WIND " .. n .. " M/S"
end

tw.wind = wind
core/world:
-- The physics world (DESIGN 5): 3D rigid bodies on a ground plane, fixed
-- step, impulse-based contacts with Coulomb friction and restitution.
-- Pure Lua: no playdate.*.
--
-- One step (world.step), after Box2D v3's soft-step order with one substep:
--   1. gravity and the gyroscopic term for awake bodies
--   2. contacts: body pairs first (an awake body moving into a sleeping one
--      wakes it), then the ground for every awake body
--   3. prepare the contacts and warm start the ground contacts from the
--      impulses of the step before
--   4. `iterations` sequential-impulse passes with a position bias (pushes
--      overlapping pieces apart, lets speculative contacts close their gap)
--   5. move and turn the bodies
--   6. `relaxIterations` passes without the push bias, so pushing apart
--      does not leave pieces with extra speed (no energy gain)
--   7. restitution, from each contact's approach speed before the solve,
--      with its friction
--   8. rolling resistance and dig, sleep, topple and touch bookkeeping
-- Tipping about an edge, rocking back and falling are all just contacts.
--
-- Surfaces are parameter sets (world.surfaces). "Dig": when a corner, edge
-- or baton end arrives steeply and fast, that contact loses its bounce, gets
-- extra friction for as long as it lasts (it is ploughed in), and the body
-- gets a rolling-resistance lever that fades over digTime (it is plugged).
-- "Bite": an edge or corner that strikes the turf is held sideways by it, an
-- extra friction coefficient that fades as it works loose. Every body meets
-- the ground the same way: a drilled kubb (world.launchDrill) is a plain
-- kubb once it is down; in flight it has the air's turn (world.aeroTurn).
--
-- Usage:
--   local w = world.new{ surface = "grass", pieces = { {id=, kind=, x=, y=, yaw=}, ... } }
--   world.launchBaton(w, x, lineY, swivel, loftDeg, speed, tumbleRate, tiltDeg)
--   while not world.isAtRest(w) do world.step(w) end
--   local r = world.result(w)
import "core/tw"
import "core/quat"
import "core/body"
import "core/collide"
import "core/flight"
import "core/pitch"
import "core/drill"

local quat, body, collide = tw.quat, tw.body, tw.collide
local sqrt, abs, min, max, sin, cos, rad, exp = math.sqrt, math.abs, math.min, math.max, math.sin, math.cos, math.rad, math.exp
local floor = math.floor

local world = {}

world.tune = {
	dt = 1 / 240,          -- s, the fixed step (DESIGN 5)
	g = 9.81,              -- m/s^2
	iterations = 4,        -- velocity passes per step with the position bias (guess: enough for
	                       -- a kubb on its edge and three-kubb dominoes at 240 Hz)
	relaxIterations = 1,   -- passes without the bias
	slop = 0.0005,         -- m of overlap left alone (stops resting contacts flickering)
	pushRate = 0.2,        -- fraction of the overlap beyond slop removed per step
	maxPush = 0.5,         -- m/s cap on the push-apart speed
	margin = 0.002,        -- m; contacts are made this far before touching, plus the distance
	                       -- the pieces can close in one step (speculative contacts)
	restitutionSpeed = 0.4,-- m/s; slower impacts do not bounce
	batonTurnHold = 1,     -- share of the ground's rolling resistance (surf.roll) that also holds a
	                       -- baton's end-over-end turn on the ground (all of it holds its roll
	                       -- about the long axis; the plug, dig, holds both)
	restitutionIterations = 4, -- bounce passes (one pass over a flat landing's corners overshoots)
	restitutionMaxIterations = 32, -- and when the bounce reaches a row, up to this many: they stop once
	restitutionTol = 1e-4, -- no impulse changes by this (N s); the push crosses a row of four in 10 to 30
	pairMu = 0.4,          -- wood on wood friction, every pair of pieces (kubb on kubb, the king, a baton,
	                       -- a stake): clean dry wood on wood 0.25 to 0.5, oak on oak sliding 0.48 along
	                       -- the grain and 0.32 across it (Engineering ToolBox, friction coefficients).
	                       -- Kubb on kubb was 0.2 (wet wood) from 2026-11-15 to 2026-11-16 so a tight row
	                       -- fell; at 0.4 it stands more (docs/notes/physics.md, "Edge on edge")
	pairE = 0.35,          -- wood on wood bounce: no measured wood on wood figure found; a wooden
	                       -- ball on concrete is 0.60 (The Physics Factbook, 2005) and a block gives
	                       -- up more. 0.2 from 2026-11-15 to 2026-11-16, to hide a bounce solved
	                       -- without the kubb's footing (docs/notes/physics.md, "The pair bounce with its footing")
	warm = 0.9,            -- fraction of last step's ground impulses applied up front
	gyro = true,           -- gyroscopic term (torque-free precession; implicit, stable)
	flightTurns = 4,       -- a drilled kubb's turn in flight (the air's turn, the gyroscopic term
	                       -- and its attitude) is stepped this many times a step: a drill spinning
	                       -- at 25 rad/s or more precesses too far in one 1/240 s step (docs/notes/physics.md,
	                       -- "Physics", "The turn in flight")
	sleepLin = 0.03,       -- m/s: below this ...
	sleepAng = 0.3,        -- rad/s: ... and this ...
	sleepTime = 0.25,      -- s: ... for this long while touching something: the body sleeps
	wakeLin = 0.05,        -- m/s: a touching awake body moving faster than this (or turning
	wakeAng = 0.5,         -- faster than this, rad/s) wakes a sleeping one
	toppleDeg = 5,         -- toppled: the long axis came within this of parallel to the ground
	pitchHalfWidth = 2.5,  -- m (DESIGN 2)
	pitchLength = 8,
	outMargin = 0.04,      -- m beyond a pitch line before a center counts as out (base kubbs
	                       -- stand centered on the baselines)
	maxTime = 12,          -- s; a throw is called at rest after this long regardless
	stakeHeight = 0.15,    -- m above the ground (6 inches, Jamie 2026-11-14); stakes are fixed posts of radius pitch.stakeRadius
	-- the air's drag on a thrown piece per kind (world.airDrag) is
	-- tw.flight.tune.dragK, the figure the aim solves with
	aeroK = 0.00022,       -- the air's turn on a drilled kubb in flight (world.aeroTurn): rho (k2 - k1)
	                       -- volume: half the slender-body (Munk) moment of a 7 x 7 x 15 cm block (k2 - k1
	                       -- about 0.5), which overstates a bluff block; an estimate. It turns the long axis
	                       -- broadside to the air, so a kubb with too little spin tumbles
}

-- Ground surfaces: one parameter set each (DESIGN 5). All guesses, to be
-- tuned on hardware in stages 2 and 4.
--   mu          Coulomb friction, wood on the ground
--   e           restitution (bounce)
--   dig         how strongly a steep, fast arrival digs in (0 = never). The
--               dig amount of a new contact is dig * steepness * ramp, where
--               steepness = approach speed / contact speed (1 = straight in)
--               and ramp goes 0 -> 1 between digSpeed and digSpeed + digRamp
--   digSpeed, digRamp  m/s
--   digLever    m; rolling resistance lever (per unit dig) a dug-in body gets
--   digTime     s; how fast that lever fades
--   roll        m; rolling resistance lever for the round baton at all times
--   texture     (optional) what a flat plane leaves out (Jamie, 2026-11-14:
--               "in a real game there is always random stuff because of the
--               surface"). The ground is cut into `cell`-sized patches, each
--               with its own values from a hash of the patch and the throw's
--               seed (world.groundSeed), read only when a contact is new:
--     muVar, eVar, digVar  a patch's friction, bounce and dig vary by up to
--               this share either way (clumps, bare spots, soft ground)
--     bump      the patch's tilt: a steep landing (approach faster than
--               bumpSpeed m/s) meets ground sloped up to bump (times its
--               steepness squared) each way, and that step's push and friction
--               lean with it, so it is turned and nothing is added
--     drag      1/s: a lying piece or a baton touching the ground with its
--               full weight loses this share of its ground speed a second (the
--               blades hold it; pressed more lightly, less)
--     grip, gripSpeed  1/s and m/s: and this much more a second below
--               gripSpeed, so it stops instead of creeping
--     footMu, footSpeed  (optional; snow) a piece standing on an end
--               (within 30 degrees of upright: a kubb, the king or a baton)
--               whose foot slides faster than footSpeed m/s ploughs: a
--               resistance at the foot of at most footMu times the ground's
--               push, so it tips the way it is going where the surface's own
--               friction is too low to tip it
--     bite      an edge or corner that strikes the turf cuts into it and is
--               held sideways by it: an extra friction coefficient on that
--               contact, ramped like dig by the edge's own arrival speed and
--               scaled by pointed() (0 on a face)
--     biteTime  s: how fast the hold weakens while the edge stays down
--     plough    1/s per m (optional): the drag grows with the distance a piece
--               has slid since it last left the ground (snow piles up in front
--               of it), so a slide starts slick and ends heavy
world.surfaces = {
	grass = {
		name = "grass", mu = 0.7, e = 0.15,
		dig = 1.0, digSpeed = 0.3, digRamp = 1.5, digLever = 0.006, digTime = 0.15,
		bite = 0.7, biteTime = 0.05,
		roll = 0.01,
		texture = { cell = 0.25, muVar = 0.3, eVar = 0.5, digVar = 0.5, bump = 0.12, bumpSpeed = 0.8,
			drag = 2.5, grip = 12, gripSpeed = 0.5 },
	},
	-- sand (DESIGN 5): very high dig, almost no bounce or slide; pieces plug where
	-- they land, so placement is all in the air. Its texture: soft and packed
	-- spots (dig varies a lot), ridges and footprints that turn a landing more
	-- than grass does, and sand that drags hard and grabs.
	sand = {
		name = "sand", mu = 0.9, e = 0.03,
		dig = 3.0, digSpeed = 0.2, digRamp = 1.0, digLever = 0.03, digTime = 0.5,
		bite = 2, biteTime = 0.1,
		roll = 0.03,
		texture = { cell = 0.2, muVar = 0.25, eVar = 0.4, digVar = 0.7, bump = 0.18, bumpSpeed = 0.6,
			drag = 6, grip = 20, gripSpeed = 0.6 },
	},
	-- snow (Jamie, 2026-11-14): packed snow is slick to a fast piece, but soft:
	-- a steep landing plugs, almost nothing bounces, and a sliding piece ploughs
	-- snow ahead of it, so it starts fast and stops heavy. Icy and soft patches
	-- (friction and dig vary most of all here).
	snow = {
		name = "snow", mu = 0.25, e = 0.02,
		dig = 2.5, digSpeed = 0.3, digRamp = 1.2, digLever = 0.025, digTime = 0.4,
		bite = 0, biteTime = 0.05,
		roll = 0.004,
		texture = { cell = 0.3, muVar = 0.5, eVar = 0.3, digVar = 0.8, bump = 0.1, bumpSpeed = 0.8,
			drag = 0.6, grip = 4, gripSpeed = 0.3, plough = 1.5,
			footMu = 0.3, footSpeed = 0.3 },
	},
	-- ICE (stage 7, not built): very low friction for the Minnesota slide,
	-- something like mu = 0.05, e = 0.1, dig = 0, roll = 0.0005. Add it
	-- here as another parameter set; nothing else should need to change.
}
-- The surfaces a game can be played on, in the order they are offered.
world.SURFACES = { "grass", "sand", "snow" }

-- Optional profiling (the device autobench): set world.prof to a table
-- from world.newProf(clock) and world.step adds the seconds of each phase
-- into it. nil (the default) costs one test per phase.
world.prof = nil
world.PHASES = { "forces", "pairs", "ground", "prepare", "solve", "integrate", "relax",
	"restitution", "store", "tail", "lone" }
function world.newProf(clock)
	local p = { clock = clock, narrow = 0 }
	for _, k in ipairs(world.PHASES) do p[k] = 0 end
	return p
end

-- The awake set's epoch: bumped whenever any body in any world wakes, falls
-- asleep or is added. A world caches what the lone-flight test needs (the one
-- awake body, the highest point of everything else) and rebuilds it when
-- the epoch has moved. A sleeping body is never moved by hand; if one ever
-- is, call world.touch() so the cache is rebuilt.
local epoch = 0
function world.touch() epoch = epoch + 1 end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Building a world

function world.new(opts)
	opts = opts or {}
	local surf = opts.surface or "grass"
	if type(surf) == "string" then surf = assert(world.surfaces[surf], "unknown surface " .. surf) end
	-- opts.texture = false: the surface as a flat plane (tests of one piece of
	-- mechanics; tools/groundstats --flat)
	if opts.texture == false and surf.texture then
		local flat = {}
		for k, v in pairs(surf) do flat[k] = v end
		flat.texture = nil
		surf = flat
	end
	local w = {
		bodies = {}, n = 0, byId = {},
		surface = surf,
		time = 0, steps = 0,
		projectile = nil,
		firstContact = nil,   -- the projectile's first contact: {t, x, y, z, with}
		firstHit = nil,       -- its first contact with another body: same fields
		contacts = 0,         -- contacts in the last step (for the bench)
		awakeCount = 0,       -- awake bodies in the last step
		bouncePasses = 0,     -- bounce passes run so far (stage 7; for the bench)
		groundSeed = opts.groundSeed or 0,   -- the ground texture's seed (world.launch sets it
		groundSeedFixed = opts.groundSeed ~= nil,   -- from the throw unless one is given here)
		-- the wind (m/s, horizontal): it pushes the thrown piece until its
		-- first contact (airDrag); none, and it meets still air
		windX = opts.windX or 0, windY = opts.windY or 0,
		windOn = (opts.windX or 0) ~= 0 or (opts.windY or 0) ~= 0,
	}
	if opts.stakes ~= false then world.addStakes(w) end
	for _, p in ipairs(opts.pieces or {}) do world.addPiece(w, p) end
	return w
end

-- The six pitch stakes (core/pitch) as static posts, ids stake1 .. stake6.
-- They never move or wake; anything touching one marks it touched.
function world.addStakes(w)
	local h, r = world.tune.stakeHeight, tw.pitch.stakeRadius
	for i, s in ipairs(tw.pitch.stakes) do
		local b = world.addBody(w, "stake", "stake" .. i)
		b.r = r
		b.hl = h / 2 - r
		b.radius = h / 2
		body.setPose(b, s.x, s.y, h / 2, 1, 0, 0, 0)
		b.awake = false
	end
end

function world.addBody(w, kind, id)
	epoch = epoch + 1
	local b = body.new(kind, id)
	w.n = w.n + 1
	b.index = w.n
	w.bodies[w.n] = b
	w.byId[b.id] = b
	return b
end

-- Add a piece at rest on the ground. p = { id, kind, x, y, yaw } stands a
-- kubb or king up (a baton lies along yaw); or give a full pose
-- p.qw, p.qx, p.qy, p.qz (z is then chosen so it rests on the ground unless
-- p.z is given). Pieces start asleep.
function world.addPiece(w, p)
	local b = world.addBody(w, p.kind, p.id)
	local qw, qx, qy, qz = p.qw, p.qx, p.qy, p.qz
	if not qw then
		qw, qx, qy, qz = quat.fromAxisAngle(0, 0, 1, p.yaw or 0)
		if p.kind == "baton" then
			-- lie down: local z (the segment) along the yaw direction
			local tw_, tx, ty, tz = quat.fromAxisAngle(1, 0, 0, -math.pi / 2)
			qw, qx, qy, qz = quat.mul(qw, qx, qy, qz, tw_, tx, ty, tz)
		end
	end
	body.setPose(b, p.x or 0, p.y or 0, 0, qw, qx, qy, qz)
	if p.z then
		b.z = p.z
	else
		b.z = -body.lowestZ(b)
	end
	b.awake = false
	-- a piece that is already down (from an earlier throw) stays toppled
	b.toppled = p.toppled or (b.shape == 1 and (body.lying(b, sin(rad(world.tune.toppleDeg))) or body.wouldFall(b)))
	b.wasToppled = b.toppled
	return b
end

local function wake(b)
	if not b.awake and not b.static then
		epoch = epoch + 1
		b.awake = true
		b.everAwake = true
		b.sleepTime = 0
	end
end
world.wake = wake

-- Launch a projectile body (baton or kubb) with a full pose and velocity.
-- Angular velocity is in the world frame.
-- The ground texture's seed for a throw: from the launch itself, so the same
-- throw meets the same ground (replays, tests) and every other throw its own.
local function seedFrom(...)
	local h = 0x2545F491
	for _, v in ipairs { ... } do
		h = (h ~ math.floor(v * 4096)) * 0x9E3779B1 & 0x7fffffff
	end
	return h
end
world.seedFrom = seedFrom

function world.launch(w, kind, id, x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz, vx, vy, vz, wx, wy, wz)
	local b = world.addBody(w, kind, id)
	body.setPose(b, x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz)
	body.setVelocity(b, vx, vy, vz, wx, wy, wz)
	if not w.groundSeedFixed then w.groundSeed = seedFrom(x, y, vx, vy, vz, wx, wy, wz) end
	wake(b)
	b.touched = true
	w.projectile = b
	b.dragK = tw.flight.tune.dragK[kind] or 0
	return b
end

-- Unit horizontal direction of the swivel and the launch direction at the
-- loft (the same conventions as core/flight).
local function launchDir(swivel, loftDeg)
	local e = rad(loftDeg)
	local ce = cos(e)
	return sin(swivel) * ce, cos(swivel) * ce, sin(e)
end

-- The baton launch from stage 1's swing outputs: it leaves the hand at
-- (x, lineY, flight.tune.handHeight) heading along the swivel at the loft,
-- held upright, turning end over end at tumbleRate (rad/s) with the top end
-- tipping forward. tiltDeg tilts the plane it turns in about the line of
-- flight (0 = clean end over end, 90 = a flat helicopter): the angular
-- velocity is about the tilted axis, so a helicopter really spins flat.
-- Returns the pose and velocities as 13 numbers.
function world.batonLaunchState(x, lineY, swivel, loftDeg, speed, tumbleRate, tiltDeg)
	local dx, dy = sin(swivel), cos(swivel)
	local lx, ly, lz = launchDir(swivel, loftDeg)
	local tau = rad(tiltDeg or 0)
	-- u: "up" of the turning plane, z turned about d toward the right by tau
	local rx, ry = dy, -dx
	local st, ct = sin(tau), cos(tau)
	local ux, uy, uz = rx * st, ry * st, ct
	-- k = d x u, the axis the baton turns about
	local kx, ky, kz = dy * uz, -dx * uz, dx * uy - dy * ux
	local kn = sqrt(kx * kx + ky * ky + kz * kz)
	kx, ky, kz = kx / kn, ky / kn, kz / kn
	-- local axes: x = k, y = d, z = u (the baton starts along u)
	local qw, qx, qy, qz = quat.fromAxes(kx, ky, kz, dx, dy, 0, ux, uy, uz)
	local h = tw.flight.tune.handHeight
	return x, lineY, h, qw, qx, qy, qz,
		speed * lx, speed * ly, speed * lz,
		-tumbleRate * kx, -tumbleRate * ky, -tumbleRate * kz
end

function world.launchBaton(w, x, lineY, swivel, loftDeg, speed, tumbleRate, tiltDeg, id)
	return world.launch(w, "baton", id or "baton",
		world.batonLaunchState(x, lineY, swivel, loftDeg, speed, tumbleRate, tiltDeg))
end

-- A lobbed kubb (stage 3's simple inkast; drilling and the cut are stage 4):
-- the same launch as a clean baton, upright in the hand and turning end
-- over end at tumbleRate, as body `id` (the kubb's own id).
function world.launchKubb(w, id, x, lineY, swivel, loftDeg, speed, tumbleRate)
	return world.launch(w, "kubb", id,
		world.batonLaunchState(x, lineY, swivel, loftDeg, speed, tumbleRate, 0))
end

-- A drilled kubb (core/drill), launched the way a baton is: a plain rigid
-- body released from the swing, and the world does the rest (2026-11-16,
-- Jamie: "we didn't treat Kubb throws with the same physics as baton
-- throws"). It leaves the hand at (x, lineY, handHeight) along the swivel at
-- the loft, held by its back end with its long axis pointing down the line,
-- the nose noseDownDeg below the horizontal (a kubb hanging from the hand at
-- the end of an underhand swing), rolled rollDeg about that axis (0: a face
-- flat to the side). The wrist's snap spins it about the long axis at
-- spinRate (rad/s; + = clockwise seen from behind). Nothing is solved back
-- from the landing: a fast spiral is a gyroscope, so the kubb lands about
-- as it left the hand, nose first; the air's turn (world.aeroTurn) tumbles
-- one with too little spin. wobbleRate (rad/s) is a jerky swing's nose-up
-- turn about the right-hand axis; dPitch, dYaw (about the kubb's own up) and
-- dSpin (rad/s) are the swing's own scatter of the release turn, and
-- dNoseDeg of its attitude. Returns the pose and velocities as 13 numbers.
function world.drillLaunchState(x, lineY, swivel, loftDeg, speed, noseDownDeg, rollDeg, spinRate, wobbleRate,
		dPitch, dYaw, dSpin, dNoseDeg)
	dPitch, dYaw, dSpin = dPitch or 0, dYaw or 0, dSpin or 0
	local dx, dy = sin(swivel), cos(swivel)
	local lx, ly, lz = launchDir(swivel, loftDeg)
	local a = rad(noseDownDeg + (dNoseDeg or 0))
	local ca, sa = cos(a), sin(a)
	-- local z: the long axis, nose forward and down; r: the right-hand side
	local zx, zy, zz = dx * ca, dy * ca, -sa
	local rx, ry, rz = dy, -dx, 0
	-- local y = z x r (so r x y = z), then both turned by the roll about z
	local yx, yy, yz = zy * rz - zz * ry, zz * rx - zx * rz, zx * ry - zy * rx
	local c, s = cos(rad(rollDeg or 0)), sin(rad(rollDeg or 0))
	local Xx, Xy, Xz = c * rx + s * yx, c * ry + s * yy, c * rz + s * yz
	local Yx, Yy, Yz = -s * rx + c * yx, -s * ry + c * yy, -s * rz + c * yz
	local qw, qx, qy, qz = quat.fromAxes(Xx, Xy, Xz, Yx, Yy, Yz, zx, zy, zz)
	-- the turn: the spiral about z, a nose-up pitch about r (the wobble and
	-- the scatter's), a yaw about the kubb's own up (y, unrolled)
	local sp, pr = spinRate + dSpin, wobbleRate + dPitch
	return x, lineY, tw.flight.tune.handHeight, qw, qx, qy, qz,
		speed * lx, speed * ly, speed * lz,
		sp * zx + pr * rx + dYaw * yx, sp * zy + pr * ry + dYaw * yy, sp * zz + pr * rz + dYaw * yz
end

-- The swing's scatter of a drill's release: four normals (sd 1) from the
-- launch and the ground's seed when a test or tool fixed it, so a throw is
-- the same every time it is replayed and every other throw its own.
local function drillScatter(w, x, lineY, swivel, loftDeg, speed, spinRate, wobbleRate)
	local h = seedFrom(x, lineY, swivel, loftDeg, speed, spinRate, wobbleRate,
		w.groundSeedFixed and w.groundSeed or 0)
	local s = h % 2147483647
	if s <= 0 then s = s + 2147483646 end
	local function u()
		s = (s * 48271) % 2147483647
		return (s - 1) / 2147483646
	end
	for _ = 1, 4 do u() end
	local function normal()
		local u1 = u()
		if u1 < 1e-12 then u1 = 1e-12 end
		return sqrt(-2 * math.log(u1)) * cos(2 * math.pi * u())
	end
	return normal(), normal(), normal(), normal()
end

-- launchDrill throws kubb `id` with drillLaunchState and the swing's scatter
-- (drill.tune: pitchSdDps, yawSdDps, spinSd, noseSdDeg, each times
-- 1 + scatterJerk x the jerk read from wobbleRate against drill.tune.wobbleRate).
-- On the ground it is a plain kubb, like any other piece.
function world.launchDrill(w, id, x, lineY, swivel, loftDeg, speed, noseDownDeg, rollDeg, spinRate,
		wobbleRate)
	local dt = tw.drill.tune
	wobbleRate = wobbleRate or 0
	local jerk = wobbleRate / dt.wobbleRate
	if jerk < 0 then jerk = -jerk end
	if jerk > 1 then jerk = 1 end
	local k = 1 + dt.scatterJerk * jerk
	local n1, n2, n3, n4 = drillScatter(w, x, lineY, swivel, loftDeg, speed, spinRate, wobbleRate)
	local b = world.launch(w, "kubb", id, world.drillLaunchState(x, lineY, swivel, loftDeg, speed,
		noseDownDeg, rollDeg, spinRate, wobbleRate,
		n1 * rad(dt.pitchSdDps) * k, n2 * rad(dt.yawSdDps) * k, n3 * dt.spinSd * k, n4 * dt.noseSdDeg * k))
	b.aeroK = world.tune.aeroK
	return b
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The solver's contacts
--
-- Speed on the device (docs/notes/physics.md "Physics", device costs): a Lua function
-- call costs about 9 us there, a C call (math.sqrt, math.abs, math.min) about
-- 4 us and every switch to another table a cache miss, so the hot paths below
-- are written out in full: no helper calls per pair, per contact or per pass,
-- comparisons instead of math.abs/min/max, and each solver contact is one
-- record (the array part of one table, read with constant indices) rather than
-- sixty parallel arrays. The arithmetic is the same as the plain version, term
-- for term and in the same order, so results are unchanged. Ground contacts
-- (normal +z, tangents +x and +y, nothing on the other side) and contacts
-- with a sleeping or static body (nothing moves on the other side) skip the
-- terms that are zero.

local C = collide.C
local cA, cB, cSlot = C.A, C.B, C.slot
local cPx, cPy, cPz, cNx, cNy, cNz, cSep = C.px, C.py, C.pz, C.nx, C.ny, C.nz, C.sep

-- Record fields. Kind: 1 ground, 2 two awake bodies, 3 B asleep or static.
local K_A <const>, K_B <const>, K_KIND <const>, K_IDX <const> = 1, 2, 3, 4
local K_NX <const>, K_NY <const>, K_NZ <const> = 5, 6, 7
local K_T1X <const>, K_T1Y <const>, K_T1Z <const>, K_T2X <const>, K_T2Y <const>, K_T2Z <const> = 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13
-- A's angular terms: (ra x d) and I^-1 (ra x d) for d = n, t1, t2; then B's
local K_ANX <const>, K_ANY <const>, K_ANZ <const>, K_WANX <const>, K_WANY <const>, K_WANZ <const> = 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19
local K_A1X <const>, K_A1Y <const>, K_A1Z <const>, K_WA1X <const>, K_WA1Y <const>, K_WA1Z <const> = 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25
local K_A2X <const>, K_A2Y <const>, K_A2Z <const>, K_WA2X <const>, K_WA2Y <const>, K_WA2Z <const> = 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31
local K_BNX <const>, K_BNY <const>, K_BNZ <const>, K_WBNX <const>, K_WBNY <const>, K_WBNZ <const> = 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37
local K_B1X <const>, K_B1Y <const>, K_B1Z <const>, K_WB1X <const>, K_WB1Y <const>, K_WB1Z <const> = 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 43
local K_B2X <const>, K_B2Y <const>, K_B2Z <const>, K_WB2X <const>, K_WB2Y <const>, K_WB2Z <const> = 44, 45, 46, 47, 48, 49
local K_MN <const>, K_MT1 <const>, K_MT2 <const> = 50, 51, 52   -- effective masses
local K_BIAS <const>, K_RELAX <const> = 53, 54                  -- velocity targets with and without the push
local K_V0 <const>, K_MU <const>, K_E <const> = 55, 56, 57
local K_LN <const>, K_LT1 <const>, K_LT2 <const> = 58, 59, 60   -- accumulated impulses
local K_LNMAX <const> = 61                                      -- largest normal impulse seen
local K_REST <const> = 62                                       -- a bounce pass's velocity target

local REC = {}   -- the records of this step's active contacts, 1 .. nRec (reused)
local nRec = 0
local BOUNCE = {}   -- the records a bounce pass solves, 1 .. nBounce (reused)

-- Per body, filled each step: position, bounding radius, awake, speed bound.
local BX, BY, BZ, BR, AW, SPD, NXT = {}, {}, {}, {}, {}, {}, {}
-- Per awake body, its velocity before this step's forces (world.step stage 1),
-- for the trapezoid move of a body with no contact (stage 5)
local OVX, OVY, OVZ = {}, {}, {}
-- Bodies woken in this step's pair loop (indices), and for each the index below
-- which its pairs with sleepers were passed untested (world.step).
local WK, WLO = {}, {}
local WT, WPOS = {}, {}

-- Implicit gyroscopic step (Bullet's computeGyroscopicImpulseImplicit_Body):
-- one Newton step of I w' = I w - dt w' x I w' in the body frame. Keeps a
-- spinning baton or kubb precessing correctly without blowing up.
-- The air's drag on the thrown piece in flight (audit 8, 2026-11-16; the
-- wind, Jamie and Tyler, 2026-11-14): k |r| r with r = wind - v, the air's
-- velocity past it, and k = 0.5 rho Cd A / m per kind (b.dragK,
-- tw.flight.tune.dragK, where the figures and their sources are). Still air
-- or wind, the same quadratic drag; the aim solves with it in still air
-- (flight.carry). Applied by world.step and the lone step alike (written out
-- there, term for term: no call per step), right after gravity, only to
-- w.projectile until its first contact: after that the
-- pieces move slowly and briefly through the air (a kubb knocked flying at
-- 3 m/s for 0.3 s would lose about 5 cm/s) and the ground's forces dwarf it.
local function airDrag(w, b, dt)
	local k = b.dragK
	local rx, ry, rz = w.windX - b.vx, w.windY - b.vy, -b.vz
	local kd = k * dt * sqrt(rx * rx + ry * ry + rz * rz)
	b.vx, b.vy, b.vz = b.vx + kd * rx, b.vy + kd * ry, b.vz + kd * rz
end
world.airDrag = airDrag

-- The air's turn on the thrown piece in flight (2026-11-16, "Drilling"): a
-- block moving at an angle to its long axis is turned broadside by the air
-- (the slender-body, Munk, moment), tau = K (v . z)(v x z) with z the long
-- axis and K = rho (k2 - k1) volume (world.tune.aeroK per kind). A spiral
-- turns that into a precession, so the nose follows the flight path; with
-- too little spin the kubb tumbles. Applied like airDrag: only to
-- w.projectile until its first contact. The step applies it in substeps,
-- in the kubb's frame (flightTurn); this is the same term in world axes.
local function aeroTurn(w, b, dt)
	local k = b.aeroK
	if not k or k == 0 then return end
	local vx, vy, vz = b.vx, b.vy, b.vz
	if w.windOn then vx, vy = vx - w.windX, vy - w.windY end
	local zx, zy, zz = b.r13, b.r23, b.r33
	local s = k * dt * (vx * zx + vy * zy + vz * zz)
	-- angular impulse s (v x z), through the world inverse inertia
	local tx, ty, tz = s * (vy * zz - vz * zy), s * (vz * zx - vx * zz), s * (vx * zy - vy * zx)
	b.wx = b.wx + b.i11 * tx + b.i12 * ty + b.i13 * tz
	b.wy = b.wy + b.i12 * tx + b.i22 * ty + b.i23 * tz
	b.wz = b.wz + b.i13 * tx + b.i23 * ty + b.i33 * tz
end
world.aeroTurn = aeroTurn

local function gyro(b, dt)
	local r11, r12, r13, r21, r22, r23, r31, r32, r33 =
		b.r11, b.r12, b.r13, b.r21, b.r22, b.r23, b.r31, b.r32, b.r33
	local wx, wy, wz = b.wx, b.wy, b.wz
	-- body frame
	local ox = r11 * wx + r21 * wy + r31 * wz
	local oy = r12 * wx + r22 * wy + r32 * wz
	local oz = r13 * wx + r23 * wy + r33 * wz
	local Ix, Iy, Iz = b.Ix, b.Iy, b.Iz
	local ix, iy, iz = Ix * ox, Iy * oy, Iz * oz
	-- f = dt * (o x I o)
	local fx = dt * (oy * iz - oz * iy)
	local fy = dt * (oz * ix - ox * iz)
	local fz = dt * (ox * iy - oy * ix)
	if fx * fx + fy * fy + fz * fz < 1e-20 then return end
	-- J = I + dt (skew(o) I - skew(I o))
	local a11 = Ix
	local a12 = dt * (-oz * Iy + iz)
	local a13 = dt * (oy * Iz - iy)
	local a21 = dt * (oz * Ix - iz)
	local a22 = Iy
	local a23 = dt * (-ox * Iz + ix)
	local a31 = dt * (-oy * Ix + iy)
	local a32 = dt * (ox * Iy - ix)
	local a33 = Iz
	-- solve J d = f (Cramer)
	local c11 = a22 * a33 - a23 * a32
	local c12 = a23 * a31 - a21 * a33
	local c13 = a21 * a32 - a22 * a31
	local det = a11 * c11 + a12 * c12 + a13 * c13
	if det < 1e-30 and det > -1e-30 then return end
	local inv = 1 / det
	local dx = (c11 * fx + (a13 * a32 - a12 * a33) * fy + (a12 * a23 - a13 * a22) * fz) * inv
	local dy = (c12 * fx + (a11 * a33 - a13 * a31) * fy + (a13 * a21 - a11 * a23) * fz) * inv
	local dz = (c13 * fx + (a12 * a31 - a11 * a32) * fy + (a11 * a22 - a12 * a21) * fz) * inv
	ox, oy, oz = ox - dx, oy - dy, oz - dz
	b.wx = r11 * ox + r12 * oy + r13 * oz
	b.wy = r21 * ox + r22 * oy + r23 * oz
	b.wz = r31 * ox + r32 * oy + r33 * oz
end

-- A drilled kubb's turn in flight (the projectile with an air's turn,
-- b.aeroK, until its first contact), in n substeps of dt / n: a kubb
-- spinning at 25 rad/s or more precesses too far in one 1/240 s step
-- (docs/notes/physics.md, "Physics", "The turn in flight"). It works in the kubb's own
-- frame, where both terms are cheap: the air's velocity past it (the wind
-- less its own velocity, constant over the step) is turned against the
-- kubb's spin each substep, the air's turn (aeroTurn's tau = K (v.z)(v x z))
-- is a kick to the two cross axes, and the gyroscopic term of a body with a
-- square section (Ix = Iy, every kubb) is an exact turn of the cross spin at
-- (Ix - Iz) wz / Ix (Euler's equations; Cayley's rotation, which keeps its
-- size). The attitude takes each substep's spin (q <- q + hs/2 q (0, w));
-- it is normalized and the rotation matrix, world inverse inertia and world
-- spin are made once at the end. Called by the lone step and by world.step's
-- stage 5, so the two stay identical; stage 1 applies neither term to it.
-- Written out: one call a step, no tables, one square root.
local function flightTurn(w, b, dt, n, useGyro)
	local hs = dt / n
	local h = 0.5 * hs
	local r11, r12, r13, r21, r22, r23, r31, r32, r33 =
		b.r11, b.r12, b.r13, b.r21, b.r22, b.r23, b.r31, b.r32, b.r33
	-- spin and the air's velocity past it, in the kubb's frame
	local wx, wy, wz = b.wx, b.wy, b.wz
	local ox = r11 * wx + r21 * wy + r31 * wz
	local oy = r12 * wx + r22 * wy + r32 * wz
	local oz = r13 * wx + r23 * wy + r33 * wz
	local vx, vy, vz = b.vx, b.vy, b.vz
	if w.windOn then vx, vy = vx - w.windX, vy - w.windY end
	local ux = r11 * vx + r21 * vy + r31 * vz
	local uy = r12 * vx + r22 * vy + r32 * vz
	local uz = r13 * vx + r23 * vy + r33 * vz
	local ka = (b.aeroK or 0) * hs
	local iIx, iIy = b.iIx, b.iIy
	-- the cross spin turns at gz x wz a second (0 without the gyroscopic term)
	local gz = useGyro and (b.Ix - b.Iz) * iIx * hs or 0
	local qw, qx, qy, qz = b.qw, b.qx, b.qy, b.qz
	for _ = 1, n do
		-- the air's turn: tau = K (v . z)(v x z), z the long axis = (0, 0, 1)
		local s = ka * uz
		ox, oy = ox + s * uy * iIx, oy - s * ux * iIy
		-- the gyroscopic term: (ox, oy) turned by -gz oz (Cayley)
		local t = 0.5 * gz * oz
		local d = 1 / (1 + t * t)
		local c, sn = (1 - t * t) * d, 2 * t * d
		ox, oy = c * ox + sn * oy, c * oy - sn * ox
		-- the attitude: q <- q + hs/2 q (0, o)
		qw, qx, qy, qz = qw - h * (qx * ox + qy * oy + qz * oz),
			qx + h * (qw * ox + qy * oz - qz * oy),
			qy + h * (qw * oy + qz * ox - qx * oz),
			qz + h * (qw * oz + qx * oy - qy * ox)
		-- the air's velocity in the turned frame: u <- u - hs o x u, to second order
		local cx, cy, cz = oy * uz - oz * uy, oz * ux - ox * uz, ox * uy - oy * ux
		local ex, ey, ez = oy * cz - oz * cy, oz * cx - ox * cz, ox * cy - oy * cx
		ux, uy, uz = ux - hs * cx + h * hs * ex, uy - hs * cy + h * hs * ey, uz - hs * cz + h * hs * ez
	end
	local qn = sqrt(qw * qw + qx * qx + qy * qy + qz * qz)
	if qn < 1e-12 then
		qw, qx, qy, qz = 1, 0, 0, 0
	else
		qn = 1 / qn
		qw, qx, qy, qz = qw * qn, qx * qn, qy * qn, qz * qn
	end
	b.qw, b.qx, b.qy, b.qz = qw, qx, qy, qz
	local xx, yy, zz = qx * qx, qy * qy, qz * qz
	local xy, xz, yz = qx * qy, qx * qz, qy * qz
	local xw, yw, zw = qw * qx, qw * qy, qw * qz
	r11, r12, r13 = 1 - 2 * (yy + zz), 2 * (xy - zw), 2 * (xz + yw)
	r21, r22, r23 = 2 * (xy + zw), 1 - 2 * (xx + zz), 2 * (yz - xw)
	r31, r32, r33 = 2 * (xz - yw), 2 * (yz + xw), 1 - 2 * (xx + yy)
	b.r11, b.r12, b.r13, b.r21, b.r22, b.r23, b.r31, b.r32, b.r33 = r11, r12, r13, r21, r22, r23, r31, r32, r33
	local ia, ic, ie = iIx, iIy, b.iIz
	b.i11 = r11 * r11 * ia + r12 * r12 * ic + r13 * r13 * ie
	b.i12 = r11 * r21 * ia + r12 * r22 * ic + r13 * r23 * ie
	b.i13 = r11 * r31 * ia + r12 * r32 * ic + r13 * r33 * ie
	b.i22 = r21 * r21 * ia + r22 * r22 * ic + r23 * r23 * ie
	b.i23 = r21 * r31 * ia + r22 * r32 * ic + r23 * r33 * ie
	b.i33 = r31 * r31 * ia + r32 * r32 * ic + r33 * r33 * ie
	-- the spin back in the world frame, by the new attitude
	b.wx = r11 * ox + r12 * oy + r13 * oz
	b.wy = r21 * ox + r22 * oy + r23 * oz
	b.wz = r31 * ox + r32 * oy + r33 * oz
end

-- How pointed the body meets the ground, 0..1. A box flat on a face is 0
-- (the load spreads, nothing digs); on an edge at 45 degrees or on a corner,
-- 1. A baton lying flat is 0; at 45 degrees or steeper, end first, 1.
local SQRT_HALF = math.sqrt(0.5)
local function pointed(b)
	if b.shape == 1 then
		local m = max(abs(b.r31), abs(b.r32), abs(b.r33))
		return min(1, (1 - m) / (1 - SQRT_HALF))
	end
	return min(1, abs(b.r33) / SQRT_HALF)
end
world.pointed = pointed

local function noteContact(w, b, other, px, py, pz)
	local rec = { t = w.time, x = px, y = py, z = pz, with = other and other.id or "ground" }
	if not w.firstContact then w.firstContact = rec end
	if other and not w.firstHit then w.firstHit = rec end
end

-- One sequential-impulse pass over records 1 .. n of list (REC, or the
-- bounce pass's BOUNCE), each held to its target r[tk] (K_BIAS, K_RELAX or
-- K_REST): the normal impulse, then the friction, capped at mu times the
-- normal impulse accumulated so far. Returns the largest change it made to
-- any impulse (N s), for the bounce passes' convergence test.
local function solve(tk, list, n)
	local dm = 0
	for i = 1, n do
		local r = list[i]
		local a, kind = r[K_A], r[K_KIND]
		local ima = a.im
		local avx, avy, avz, awx, awy, awz = a.vx, a.vy, a.vz, a.wx, a.wy, a.wz
		if kind == 1 then
			-- the ground: n = +z, t1 = +x, t2 = +y
			local anx, any = r[K_ANX], r[K_ANY]
			local vn = avz + awx * anx + awy * any
			local old = r[K_LN]
			local lam = old - r[K_MN] * (vn - r[tk])
			if lam < 0 then lam = 0 end
			r[K_LN] = lam
			if lam > r[K_LNMAX] then r[K_LNMAX] = lam end
			local d = lam - old
			if d ~= 0 then
				if d > dm then dm = d elseif -d > dm then dm = -d end
				avz = avz + ima * d
				awx, awy, awz = awx + d * r[K_WANX], awy + d * r[K_WANY], awz + d * r[K_WANZ]
			end
			local a1y, a1z, a2x, a2z = r[K_A1Y], r[K_A1Z], r[K_A2X], r[K_A2Z]
			local v1 = avx + awy * a1y + awz * a1z
			local v2 = avy + awx * a2x + awz * a2z
			local o1, o2 = r[K_LT1], r[K_LT2]
			local l1, l2 = o1 - r[K_MT1] * v1, o2 - r[K_MT2] * v2
			local cap = r[K_MU] * lam
			local m2 = l1 * l1 + l2 * l2
			if m2 > cap * cap then
				local s = (m2 > 0) and (cap / sqrt(m2)) or 0
				l1, l2 = l1 * s, l2 * s
			end
			r[K_LT1], r[K_LT2] = l1, l2
			local d1, d2 = l1 - o1, l2 - o2
			if d1 ~= 0 or d2 ~= 0 then
				if d1 > dm then dm = d1 elseif -d1 > dm then dm = -d1 end
				if d2 > dm then dm = d2 elseif -d2 > dm then dm = -d2 end
				avx, avy = avx + ima * d1, avy + ima * d2
				awx = awx + d1 * r[K_WA1X] + d2 * r[K_WA2X]
				awy = awy + d1 * r[K_WA1Y] + d2 * r[K_WA2Y]
				awz = awz + d1 * r[K_WA1Z] + d2 * r[K_WA2Z]
			end
			a.vx, a.vy, a.vz, a.wx, a.wy, a.wz = avx, avy, avz, awx, awy, awz
		elseif kind >= 3 then
			-- B asleep or static, or a landing on a tilted patch (4): nothing
			-- moves on the other side
			local nx, ny, nz = r[K_NX], r[K_NY], r[K_NZ]
			local vn = avx * nx + avy * ny + avz * nz
				+ awx * r[K_ANX] + awy * r[K_ANY] + awz * r[K_ANZ]
			local old = r[K_LN]
			local lam = old - r[K_MN] * (vn - r[tk])
			if lam < 0 then lam = 0 end
			r[K_LN] = lam
			if lam > r[K_LNMAX] then r[K_LNMAX] = lam end
			local d = lam - old
			if d ~= 0 then
				if d > dm then dm = d elseif -d > dm then dm = -d end
				avx, avy, avz = avx + ima * d * nx, avy + ima * d * ny, avz + ima * d * nz
				awx, awy, awz = awx + d * r[K_WANX], awy + d * r[K_WANY], awz + d * r[K_WANZ]
			end
			local t1x, t1y, t1z, t2x, t2y, t2z = r[K_T1X], r[K_T1Y], r[K_T1Z], r[K_T2X], r[K_T2Y], r[K_T2Z]
			local v1 = avx * t1x + avy * t1y + avz * t1z
				+ awx * r[K_A1X] + awy * r[K_A1Y] + awz * r[K_A1Z]
			local v2 = avx * t2x + avy * t2y + avz * t2z
				+ awx * r[K_A2X] + awy * r[K_A2Y] + awz * r[K_A2Z]
			local o1, o2 = r[K_LT1], r[K_LT2]
			local l1, l2 = o1 - r[K_MT1] * v1, o2 - r[K_MT2] * v2
			local cap = r[K_MU] * lam
			local m2 = l1 * l1 + l2 * l2
			if m2 > cap * cap then
				local s = (m2 > 0) and (cap / sqrt(m2)) or 0
				l1, l2 = l1 * s, l2 * s
			end
			r[K_LT1], r[K_LT2] = l1, l2
			local d1, d2 = l1 - o1, l2 - o2
			if d1 ~= 0 or d2 ~= 0 then
				if d1 > dm then dm = d1 elseif -d1 > dm then dm = -d1 end
				if d2 > dm then dm = d2 elseif -d2 > dm then dm = -d2 end
				local px, py, pz = d1 * t1x + d2 * t2x, d1 * t1y + d2 * t2y, d1 * t1z + d2 * t2z
				avx, avy, avz = avx + ima * px, avy + ima * py, avz + ima * pz
				awx = awx + d1 * r[K_WA1X] + d2 * r[K_WA2X]
				awy = awy + d1 * r[K_WA1Y] + d2 * r[K_WA2Y]
				awz = awz + d1 * r[K_WA1Z] + d2 * r[K_WA2Z]
			end
			a.vx, a.vy, a.vz, a.wx, a.wy, a.wz = avx, avy, avz, awx, awy, awz
		else
			-- two awake bodies
			local b = r[K_B]
			local imb = b.im
			local bvx, bvy, bvz, bwx, bwy, bwz = b.vx, b.vy, b.vz, b.wx, b.wy, b.wz
			local nx, ny, nz = r[K_NX], r[K_NY], r[K_NZ]
			local dvx, dvy, dvz = avx - bvx, avy - bvy, avz - bvz
			local vn = dvx * nx + dvy * ny + dvz * nz
				+ awx * r[K_ANX] + awy * r[K_ANY] + awz * r[K_ANZ]
				- bwx * r[K_BNX] - bwy * r[K_BNY] - bwz * r[K_BNZ]
			local old = r[K_LN]
			local lam = old - r[K_MN] * (vn - r[tk])
			if lam < 0 then lam = 0 end
			r[K_LN] = lam
			if lam > r[K_LNMAX] then r[K_LNMAX] = lam end
			local d = lam - old
			if d ~= 0 then
				if d > dm then dm = d elseif -d > dm then dm = -d end
				avx, avy, avz = avx + ima * d * nx, avy + ima * d * ny, avz + ima * d * nz
				awx, awy, awz = awx + d * r[K_WANX], awy + d * r[K_WANY], awz + d * r[K_WANZ]
				bvx, bvy, bvz = bvx - imb * d * nx, bvy - imb * d * ny, bvz - imb * d * nz
				bwx, bwy, bwz = bwx - d * r[K_WBNX], bwy - d * r[K_WBNY], bwz - d * r[K_WBNZ]
			end
			local t1x, t1y, t1z, t2x, t2y, t2z = r[K_T1X], r[K_T1Y], r[K_T1Z], r[K_T2X], r[K_T2Y], r[K_T2Z]
			dvx, dvy, dvz = avx - bvx, avy - bvy, avz - bvz
			local v1 = dvx * t1x + dvy * t1y + dvz * t1z
				+ awx * r[K_A1X] + awy * r[K_A1Y] + awz * r[K_A1Z]
				- bwx * r[K_B1X] - bwy * r[K_B1Y] - bwz * r[K_B1Z]
			local v2 = dvx * t2x + dvy * t2y + dvz * t2z
				+ awx * r[K_A2X] + awy * r[K_A2Y] + awz * r[K_A2Z]
				- bwx * r[K_B2X] - bwy * r[K_B2Y] - bwz * r[K_B2Z]
			local o1, o2 = r[K_LT1], r[K_LT2]
			local l1, l2 = o1 - r[K_MT1] * v1, o2 - r[K_MT2] * v2
			local cap = r[K_MU] * lam
			local m2 = l1 * l1 + l2 * l2
			if m2 > cap * cap then
				local s = (m2 > 0) and (cap / sqrt(m2)) or 0
				l1, l2 = l1 * s, l2 * s
			end
			r[K_LT1], r[K_LT2] = l1, l2
			local d1, d2 = l1 - o1, l2 - o2
			if d1 ~= 0 or d2 ~= 0 then
				if d1 > dm then dm = d1 elseif -d1 > dm then dm = -d1 end
				if d2 > dm then dm = d2 elseif -d2 > dm then dm = -d2 end
				local px, py, pz = d1 * t1x + d2 * t2x, d1 * t1y + d2 * t2y, d1 * t1z + d2 * t2z
				avx, avy, avz = avx + ima * px, avy + ima * py, avz + ima * pz
				awx = awx + d1 * r[K_WA1X] + d2 * r[K_WA2X]
				awy = awy + d1 * r[K_WA1Y] + d2 * r[K_WA2Y]
				awz = awz + d1 * r[K_WA1Z] + d2 * r[K_WA2Z]
				bvx, bvy, bvz = bvx - imb * px, bvy - imb * py, bvz - imb * pz
				bwx = bwx - d1 * r[K_WB1X] - d2 * r[K_WB2X]
				bwy = bwy - d1 * r[K_WB1Y] - d2 * r[K_WB2Y]
				bwz = bwz - d1 * r[K_WB1Z] - d2 * r[K_WB2Z]
			end
			a.vx, a.vy, a.vz, a.wx, a.wy, a.wz = avx, avy, avz, awx, awy, awz
			b.vx, b.vy, b.vz, b.wx, b.wy, b.wz = bvx, bvy, bvz, bwx, bwy, bwz
		end
	end
	return dm
end

-- Rolling resistance: an angular impulse of lever * normal impulse against
-- the body's spin, never more than stops it.
local function rollResist(b, lever, impulse)
	local L = lever * impulse
	if L <= 0 then return end
	local wx, wy, wz = b.wx, b.wy, b.wz
	local w2 = wx * wx + wy * wy + wz * wz
	if w2 < 1e-12 then return end
	local wn = sqrt(w2)
	local ux, uy, uz = wx / wn, wy / wn, wz / wn
	local ix = b.i11 * ux + b.i12 * uy + b.i13 * uz
	local iy = b.i12 * ux + b.i22 * uy + b.i23 * uz
	local iz = b.i13 * ux + b.i23 * uy + b.i33 * uz
	-- angular impulse that stops the spin along u: wn / (u . I^-1 u)
	local stop = wn / (ux * ix + uy * iy + uz * iz)
	if L >= stop then
		b.wx, b.wy, b.wz = 0, 0, 0
	else
		b.wx, b.wy, b.wz = wx - L * ix, wy - L * iy, wz - L * iz
	end
end

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The step

local boxBox, capsuleBox, capsuleCapsule = collide.boxBox, collide.capsuleBox, collide.capsuleCapsule
local groundBox, groundCapsule = collide.groundBox, collide.groundCapsule

-- The lone flight. A step with exactly one body awake that is clear of the
-- ground and above everything else (its lowest point higher than the
-- highest point of every sleeping or static body, by more than the contact
-- margin the step could use) finds no contact: the full step would then only
-- apply gravity and the gyroscopic term, move and turn that body and do its
-- bookkeeping. loneStep does exactly that and nothing else, in the same
-- order with the same arithmetic, so results are bit-identical; it saves
